payload.answer:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Does ZB-2p achieve a near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs?"
(Design-only document. No experiment has been run; /workspace contains no code, and all source-specific claims below are marked as either brief-confirmed or literature/context-based.)

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. OBJECTIVE AND HYPOTHESIS
════════════════════════════════════════════
Objective: Empirically determine whether the ZB-2p schedule (automatic planner output of the zero-bubble pipeline-parallelism Megatron-LM fork), activated via --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2 × (number of pipeline stages), achieves a near-zero pipeline bubble rate on real multi-GPU hardware, and — if it deviates — localize the cause.

Hypothesis H1 (from the Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism paper): ZB-2p reduces theoretical bubble to ~0, while 1F1B retains (p−1)/(m+p−1) and ZB-1p retains roughly (p−1)/(m+p−1) minus ~75% of it. Operational predictions:
  P1: measured ZB-2p steady-state bubble rate ≤ 1–2% absolute (per scheme's own idle share of iteration time);
  P2: measured ZB-2p bubble rate < ZB-1p < 1F1B (ordering test);
  P3: deviations of ZB-2p from its planner's predicted timeline are attributable to identifiable causes (comm wait, stage imbalance, synchronization skew), not to the scheduler itself failing.

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. CONFIGURATION MATRIX
════════════════════════════════════════════
Factor matrix (all arms run at identical model size, microbatch count m, global batch, and total GPU count per configuration):

  Scheme (3): 1F1B | ZB-1p | ZB-2p
  Pipeline size PP (2): 4 | 8
  Placement (2): single-node (≤8 GPUs, NVLink) | multi-node (e.g., 2 nodes × 4–8 GPUs, Ethernet/IB inter-node)
  Stress scenarios (2, run for ZB-2p only unless resources allow all arms):
    S1 stage-load imbalance: one stage's compute inflated ~20% (e.g., wider MLP) to see if ZB-2p's slack absorbs or leaks bubbles;
    S2 high inter-node latency: place PP=8 across 2 nodes so T_comm/T_iter is elevated.

Core matrix: 3 schemes × 2 PP sizes × 2 placements = 12 cells.
Stress extensions: 2 scenarios × ZB-2p × {PP=4, PP=8} × 2 placements = up to 8 cells.
Repeats: ≥3 per cell → 12 × 3 = 36 core runs + 8–24 stress runs ≈ 44–60 runs total. Each run: 5 warmup iterations (excluded) + 50 measured steady-state iterations (single-node) or 30 (multi-node, slower).

Node split rationale: PP=4 and single-node PP=8 are single-node cells; PP=8 multi-node and all S2 cells are the multi-node subset (~1/3 of core cells) — this isolates the inter-node stress axis without doubling the whole matrix.

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. ACTIVATION OF ZB-2p (brief-confirmed flag semantics)
════════════════════════════════════════════
--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward set to 2 × PP (e.g., PP=4 → 8; PP=8 → 16). Per the paper/fork context, this pushes the schedule into the ZB-2p regime (two backward chunks in flight per stage); the fork's automatic planner then emits the schedule. Verification at runtime: assert from the fork's log/planner output that the emitted schedule is labeled ZB-2p (the fork prints the schedule type); do not infer mode from the flag value alone. Memory note (context-based): ZB-2p holds more activations; if OOM occurs, enable optimizer sharding / reduce microbatch and record this as a deviation in the run log rather than silently changing the model size between arms.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. CONTROLS AND BASELINES
════════════════════════════════════════════
  C1 (primary baseline): 1F1B — textbook bubble rate predicted analytically as (p−1)/(m+p−1) for each (m, p) pair.
  C2 (attribution control): ZB-1p — separates "zero-bubble machinery exists" from "2p scheduling specifically drives bubble to zero."
  C3 (measurement-validity control / sanity check): the 1F1B baseline's measured steady-state bubble rate must match (p−1)/(m+p−1) within a pre-set tolerance (e.g., ±20% relative or ±2 percentage points absolute). If it does not, the profiling methodology itself is suspect and all results are quarantined until the cause (timer overhead, window placement, sync skew) is fixed. This check is run first, before any ZB arm.
  C4 (planner cross-check): for every ZB-2p run, extract the planner's predicted timeline and compare with the measured timeline.

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY
════════════════════════════════════════════
Metric definition (primary): bubble_rate = Σ_r idle_r / (p × T_iter), where idle_r is time rank r is neither computing a forward/backward chunk nor doing overlapping communication within its schedule slot, and T_iter is the steady-state iteration time. Reported per scheme and per configuration as BOTH absolute (idle share of iteration time, %) and relative to the 1F1B baseline of the same cell.

Measurement window: strictly steady-state. First 5 iterations discarded as fill/warmup; last 2 iterations before ramp-down (drain) excluded; fill/drain phases are reported separately (as their own overhead figure) but never folded into the steady-state bubble rate, since fill/drain inflates all schemes equally in kind but unequally in magnitude and would confound the near-zero claim. If the fork's timeline tool marks fill/drain boundaries, use them; otherwise detect steady state as iterations with stable T_iter (drift < 1% over a 10-iteration window) and cut the window conservatively inside it.

Instruments (dual, as agreed):
  (a) Megatron per-rank timers (forward/backward/comm/optimization elapsed times per rank per iteration) — primary, low overhead;
  (b) torch.profiler (or equivalent trace export) on all pipeline ranks for a 5–10 iteration window in a subset of runs — independent cross-check of idle windows; used in at least one run per core cell.
  (c) The fork's clock-profile/timeline visualization (context-based: the zero-bubble repo ships a timeline dump) for direct schedule-vs-measured comparison.

Timeline-vs-measured mismatch analysis (turns the number into a diagnosis):
  A "mismatch" = an idle window present in the measured per-rank timeline but absent in the planner's predicted schedule (i.e., the rank should have had work). Mismatch rate reported as fraction of predicted-busy time lost. Localization protocol:
    - window coincides with cross-rank communication wait → classify comm wait (verify via NCCL/torch.distributed timeline markers);
    - window follows an upstream stage's slow chunk → classify load imbalance (correlate with per-stage chunk durations);
    - window varies across repeats with no systematic schedule position → classify synchronization skew / jitter (report variance across repeats);
  Each ZB-2p run receives a mismatch taxonomy so the final claim reads "near-zero, and residual bubbles come from X," not just a percentage.

Run hygiene: lock clocks if permitted, pin ranks, record NCCL version, GPU model, driver, and the emitted schedule; identical seeds/data across arms within a cell; inter-run cooldown to rule out thermal drift; per-iteration timers logged to disk for offline recomputation.

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
════════════════════════════════════════════
  A1: per cell, mean ± std of absolute bubble rate across ≥3 repeats; report 95% CI (t-based, small n acknowledged).
  A2: ordering test P2 via pairwise comparisons (Wilcoxon signed-rank across matched cells, or bootstrap CI on scheme differences; n is small — nonparametric preferred over ANOVA).
  A3: near-zero test P1: absolute bubble rate ≤ 2% (pre-registered threshold) per ZB-2p cell; report every cell, including failures.
  A4: planner fidelity: per ZB-2p cell, predicted vs measured timeline divergence (mismatch rate + taxonomy from §5).
  A5: stress analysis: ZB-2p bubble rate delta between balanced vs S1/S2 cells; determines whether near-zero survives real-world stressors.
  A6: C3 sanity gate reported first; all downstream numbers conditional on it passing.

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. SUCCESS / FAILURE CRITERIA
════════════════════════════════════════════
  CONFIRMED: ZB-2p shows absolute steady-state bubble rate ≤ 2% in all balanced core cells (single- and multi-node), with 95% CI upper bound < 5%, ordering P2 holds, and residual idle is taxonomized as comm/imbalance/skew with mismatch rate ≤ ~5% of predicted-busy time.
  PARTIALLY CONFIRMED: near-zero holds in single-node balanced cells but degrades measurably under imbalance or multi-node comm — then the answer is conditional and the taxonomy identifies which stressor breaks it.
  NOT CONFIRMED: ZB-2p bubble rate materially exceeds threshold in balanced cells, or planner-predicted schedule and measured timeline diverge beyond mismatch tolerance, or C3 sanity gate fails (methodology invalid; redesign measurement before concluding anything about ZB-2p).

════════════════════════════════════════════
8. FEASIBILITY ASSESSMENT
════════════════════════════════════════════
  Hardware: minimum 8 GPUs of one type for single-node cells; 2 nodes × 4–8 GPUs for multi-node cells. GPU-disabled here — execution assumed to happen on an external stand (stated assumption).
  Memory: ZB-2p's higher activation footprint is an explicit resource constraint: budget a model configuration sized for the ZB-2p worst case; if OOM forces optimizer sharding, apply it identically across all three arms in that configuration and log it.
  Runtime: ~44–60 runs × (55–85 iterations) ≈ a few hours of GPU wall time per configuration class; well within a one-day allocation per node-pair. Feasible.
  Software: Megatron-LM fork with zero-bubble support; NCCL; torch.profiler. Network disabled in this sandbox — repo acquisition must occur on the execution stand.

════════════════════════════════════════════
9. ASSUMPTIONS (vs. fixed requirements)
════════════════════════════════════════════
Fixed by task: design-only; ZB-2p activated via zero-bubble config flag (brief); no execution claimed.
Assumed (not confirmed by local code): external multi-GPU stand availability; specific Megatron fork version matching the zero-bubble paper's code; availability of timeline dump utility; GPU clock control permissions; that compute dominates comm for the chosen model in single-node cells (needed for clean baseline sanity check).

════════════════════════════════════════════
10. UNCERTAINTIES (open, resolved only by execution)
════════════════════════════════════════════
  U1: Flag semantics --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2×PP are brief-confirmed, not code-confirmed; runtime schedule-type verification (§3) is the safeguard.
  U2: ZB-2p memory pressure may constrain model size or require optimizer sharding; its effect on the comparison must be neutralized across arms.
  U3: Whether a built-in bubble-rate metric exists in the fork is unknown; the dual-instrument methodology does not depend on it.
  U4: Magnitude of residual bubbles under imbalance/inter-node comm — the central empirical question; taxonomy in §5 is designed to answer "why" even if the answer is "no."
  U5: Small repeat count (n=3) limits statistical power; conclusions rest on effect size plus planner-fidelity analysis, not solely on significance tests.

PROPUESTA PRELIMINAR DE ENFOQUE (fase 2)

Pregunta: ¿ZB-2p, activado con --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2 × n_stages, alcanza una tasa de burbuja cercana a cero al perfilarlo en múltiples GPUs?

1) Diseño del experimento
- Sistema: entrenamiento de pipeline paralelo (PP = p etapas, TP=1, DP=1) sobre un modelo estándar (p.ej. GPT pequeño pre-layernorm), con el schedule automático de zero bubble.
- Condiciones (brazos del experimento):
  A. Baseline 1F1B clásico (sin zero bubble) — control negativo, burbuja teórica ≈ (p−1) por ciclo.
  B. ZB-H1 o ZB-H2 (opcional, control intermedio) — para situar el resultado.
  C. ZB-2p: activar el schedule con zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2p (y la(s) bandera(s) adicionales que el código requiera para el modo automático, p.ej. enable-zero-bubble / h2 / vpp-off según el repositorio).
- Factores a variar (recomendado un pequeño grid): p ∈ {4, 8}, número de microbatches m ∈ {8p, 16p} (m suficientemente grande para que el estado estacionario domine sobre warmup/tail), tamaño de modelo/tiempo por microbatch aproximadamente equilibrado entre F y B (ZB-2p asume F ≈ B; si B ≠ F la burbuja mínima no es cero — ver supuestos).
- Réplicas: ≥3 corridas por condición, mismas semillas/tokens, con warm-up de iteraciones descartadas antes de medir.

2) Variables a medir
- Primaria: tasa de burbuja empírica por GPU, definida como burbuja = 1 − (tiempo total en cómputo útil F/B/Z) / (tiempo de pared del step), medida con un perfilador por dispositivo (torch.profiler / PyTorch Kineto, nsys, o los timers de Megatron por stage). Para ZB-2p el backward dividido (B y Z/partial-B) cuenta como cómputo útil; F/B/Z no solapados con comunicación bloqueante cuentan como burbuja.
- Secundarias: tiempo de step end-to-end, tiempo de warmup y de tail (para descomponer burbuja total vs. burbuja de estado estacionario), uso máximo de memoria de activaciones (ZB-2p con 2p pendientes consume más memoria que ZB-H1 — comprobar que no induce OOM ni recomputación), throughput (tokens/s), y, si el código lo expone, comparación del schedule generado (salida del planificador automático: número de warmup microbatches, pendientes máximas efectivas) contra el schedule teórico.
- Teórica de referencia: burbuja teórica del paper para ZB-2p en la misma configuración (p, m), para cuantificar la brecha empírico-teórica.

3) Plan de análisis
- Por corrida y por rank: extraer del timeline los intervalos de kernels F/B/Z, construir la línea de tiempo por microbatch y computar la fracción de burbuja en (a) todo el step y (b) estado estacionario (excluyendo warmup/tail identificados por el patrón del schedule).
- Estadística: media ± IC95% (o desviación) por condición; contraste ZB-2p vs 1F1B y vs teórico. Criterio de éxito pre-registrado: burbuja de estado estacionario de ZB-2p ≤ ~1–2 % (y significativamente menor que 1F1B), y burbuja total que converja a la fórmula teórica conforme m/p crece.
- Sanity checks: verificar en el log que el flag se parseó y que el planificador realmente emitió el schedule ZB-2p (no un fallback silencioso a 1F1B/ZB-H1 — riesgo típico si el flag equivocado o incompatible se ignora); verificar que las pendientes máximas observadas en el timeline no exceden 2p.

4) Controles y amenazas a la validez
- Control positivo/negativo: 1F1B (burbuja conocida >0) y, si se puede, el bubble teórico del paper.
- Igualdad de carga: mismo modelo, datos, batch global, semillas; sincronizar comunicaciones (no solapar con cómputo salvo el que el schedule prescribe) para que la burbuja medida sea atribuible al schedule.
- Aislar el efecto del flag: variar solo zero-bubble-max-pending-backward (y el modo) entre brazos.
- Medición no intrusiva: confirmar que el overhead del profiler es <1 % (comparar step time con y sin profiler).
- Verificar el mapeo exacto flag→schedule en el código fuente; el nombre "--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward" de la tarea podría corresponder a "--zb-max-pending-backward" o similar en el repositorio real.

SUPUESTOS (distintos de requisitos fijos)
1. El código de referencia será el fork de Megatron-LM del paper de zero bubble (o un Megatron-LM reciente con schedule zero-bubble equivalente); como el workspace está vacío, este es un supuesto fuerte que requiere confirmación del investigador.
2. Entorno objetivo: ≥8 GPUs reales (p.ej. 1 nodo × 8) para p=8; si solo hay menos, limitar p a {2,4}. Presupuesto de cómputo estimado: O(10–20) minutos de GPU por corrida con un modelo pequeño (~100–300M params) y ~10–20 iteraciones medibles ⇒ <10 h de GPU en total para el grid propuesto con réplicas. Esto es estimación, no requisito confirmado.
3. F ≈ B en tiempo por microbatch (el paper lo asume); si no, se medirá la ratio F/B y se ajustará la interpretación.
4. El flag max-pending = 2p es compatible con la memoria disponible; si no, registrar el fallo como resultado (limitación práctica de ZB-2p).

payload.answer:
DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL FINAL — ¿Logra ZB-2p una tasa de burbuja cercana a cero al ser perfilado en múltiples GPUs?

=====================================================================
1. PREGUNTA DE INVESTIGACIÓN
=====================================================================
¿El algoritmo de planificación automática (ZB-2p) alcanza, en la práctica, una tasa de burbuja cercana a cero cuando se perfila en múltiples GPUs, activando el schedule mediante la configuración de zero bubble indicada: --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2 × n_stages (el nombre/semántica exacta del flag se trata como supuesto a verificar contra el código real, véase §8)?

=====================================================================
2. HIPÓTESIS (pre-registrada)
=====================================================================
H1 (principal): Con ZB-2p activado (max-pending-backward = 2p) y m = 8p microbatches, la tasa de burbuja de estado estacionario por GPU es ≤ 2 % y la burbuja total del step queda dentro del límite teórico reportado para ZB-2p (±2 puntos porcentuales de brecha empírico-teórica).
H0: La burbuja de estado estacionario es > 2 % o estadísticamente indistinguible de la del baseline 1F1B.
Criterio de éxito pre-registrado ("cercano a cero" cuantificado):
  (a) Burbuja de estado estacionario: media por-rank ≤ 2 %, con IC95 % que no incluya la burbuja del baseline 1F1B.
  (b) Burbuja total del step: ≤ burbuja teórica de ZB-2p + 2 pp, y estrictamente menor que la burbuja teórica de 1F1B ≈ (p−1)·t_F/(m·t_F + ...) bajo las mismas condiciones.
  (c) Verificación estructural: el schedule emitido por el planificador automático es ZB-2p (no un fallback silencioso; ver sanity checks, §7).

=====================================================================
3. DISEÑO Y BRAZOS EXPERIMENTALES
=====================================================================
Sistema: entrenamiento con paralelismo de pipeline (TP=1, DP=1, VPP/interleaving desactivado) sobre un modelo GPT-like pequeño-mediano (100–300M params, pre-Layernorm), activaciones/recomputación idénticas entre brazos. Framework: el fork de Megatron-LM con planificador zero-bubble (implementación de referencia del paper "Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism"); como el workspace no contiene código, la disponibilidad de este repositorio es un supuesto fuerte (§8).

Brazos (única diferencia entre brazos: configuración del schedule):
  A. Control negativo — 1F1B clásico: zero bubble desactivado, warmup estándar (n_warmup ≈ p−1).
  B. (Opcional, si el código lo soporta sin coste extra) Control intermedio — ZB-H1: max-pending-backward = p−1. Permite situar la curva 1F1B < ZB-H1 < ZB-2p.
  C. Tratamiento — ZB-2p: activación mediante --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2 × n_stages (supuesto a verificar; posibles equivalentes reales: --zb-max-pending-backward 2p, más flags de modo p.ej. --enable-zero-bubble / --zb-2p / h2, según el repositorio). Se registrará en el log qué flags se parsearon y el schedule emitido.

Grid simplificado (viabilidad con presupuesto incierto):
  - p (número de etapas) ∈ {4, 8}; m (microbatches) = 8p (mínimo viable: 32 y 64 microbatches). Extensión opcional si sobra presupuesto: m = 16p para confirmar la tendencia de convergencia al límite teórico.
  - Hardware mínimo viable: 8 GPUs en un solo nodo (p.ej. 8×A100 40/80 GB o equivalentes) con NVLink/PCIe homogéneo; con solo 4 GPUs, limitar a p=4. 1 proceso por GPU, mismo nodo para evitar ruido de red inter-nodo.
  - Réplicas: ≥ 3 corridas por celda (brazo × p), semillas fijas y compartidas; por cada corrida se mide el mismo número de iteraciones (p.ej. 20) tras descartar 10 iteraciones de warm-up.
  Total de corridas mínimo: 2 brazos × 2 valores de p × 3 réplicas = 12 corridas (+6 si se incluye ZB-H1).

Variables fijadas (controles): mismo modelo, datos sintéticos o dataset fijo, batch global, optimizador, secuencia de semillas, longitud de iteración medida (steps idénticos), y overhead de profiler verificado (§5). Se mide la ratio t_B/t_F del modelo elegido en un pre-check (ver §8, supuesto de F≈B).

=====================================================================
4. MÉTRICAS Y MÉTODO DE PERFILADO
=====================================================================
Definición operativa de "tasa de burbuja" (se reportan ambas):
  Definición 1 — Burbuja total del step:
      Bubble_total = 1 − Σ_gpus Σ_(kernels útiles en el step) dur(kernel) / Σ_gpus T_wall(step)
    donde "kernels útiles" = cómputo de forward (F), backward completo (B) y backward parcial (Z/partial-B) prescritos por el schedule; NO se computan como útiles los solapamientos con comunicación si el schedule no los prescribe, ni la re-multiplicación/recomputación extra que ZB-2p no requiera. T_wall(step) es el tiempo de pared del step por rank (desde el primer evento al último, por iteración).
  Definición 2 — Burbuja de estado estacionario:
      Se identifica la ventana de estado estacionario del timeline (iteraciones tras warm-up, excluyendo el tramo de warmup del schedule y el tail final), y se aplica la misma fórmula restringida a esa ventana. Motivación: la burbuja total incluye warmup/tail que ninguna schedule puede eliminar por completo; la de estado estacionario aísla el desempeño del planificador automático.
  Descomposición reportada: Bubble_total = Bubble_warmup + Bubble_steady + Bubble_tail (fracciones estimadas del timeline).

Instrumentación (perfilado por-rank, no intrusivo):
  - Primario: torch.profiler (Kineto) activado solo en las iteraciones de medición, exportando trace por rank; clasificación de kernels F/B/Z por nombre de op y por posición en el schedule (validada con el log del planificador). Alternativa de menor overhead: nsys con rangos NVTX instrumentados por el código (si el repositorio ya instrumenta stages/microbatches, se reutiliza).
  - Secundario (cross-check): timers del framework por stage/step (p.ej. timers de Megatron) para T_wall y throughput (tokens/s).
  - Verificación de overhead: comparar step time con y sin profiler; requisito: overhead < 1 %, si no, usar nsys/NVTX.

Métricas por corrida: Bubble_total, Bubble_steady (media y por-rank), Bubble_warmup, Bubble_tail, T_wall(step), throughput, memoria máxima de activaciones (para confirmar que max-pending = 2p no dispara OOM ni recomputación extra), y parámetros del schedule emitido (nº de warmup microbatches, pendientes máximas efectivas observadas en el timeline ≤ 2p).

=====================================================================
5. PLAN DE ANÁLISIS ESTADÍSTICO
=====================================================================
- Por celda (brazo × p): media ± IC95 % de Bubble_steady y Bubble_total entre réplicas (n≥3; si n≥5, test t de Welch contra H0: media = 2 %; con n=3, reporte descriptivo con rango).
- Contraste principal: ZB-2p vs 1F1B en la misma (p, m) — diferencia de medias con IC95 % (bootstrap sobre ranks/réplicas).
- Brecha empírico-teórica: comparar Bubble_total empírica con la fórmula teórica de ZB-2p del paper para (p, m) — reportar brecha en puntos porcentuales y su tendencia al aumentar m (si se corre m=16p).
- Verificación estructural del timeline: reconstruir la matriz microbatch×stage del schedule observado y compararla con el schedule teórico ZB-2p (orden de F/B/Z y pendientes máximas ≤ 2p); reportar desviaciones.
- Decisión: se responde "sí, burbuja cercana a cero" solo si se cumplen (a), (b) y (c) del §2 simultáneamente.

=====================================================================
6. CONTROLES Y AMENAZAS A LA VALIDEZ
=====================================================================
- Control 1F1B (requisito mantenido): ancla la escala de burbuja; su burbuja medida debe aproximarse a la teórica ((p−1)/m-escala); si no, la instrumentación está mal calibrada.
- Atribución causal al flag: entre brazos solo cambia la configuración del schedule; resto idéntico byte a byte (mismo seed, datos, modelo).
- Degradación silenciosa del planificador automático (requisito mantenido — sanity checks):

payload.answer:
# ZB-2p 调度实际气泡率是否接近零 —— 最终实验设计（design-only）

## 0. 研究问题与判定标准（事先约定，避免事后定标）

**问题**：在多卡 GPU 上，通过 `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward` 设为 2×流水线级数激活的 ZB-2p 自动调度，其实测稳态气泡率是否接近零？

**判定阈值（预先约定）**：
- 主判据：ZB-2p 在稳态迭代上的实测气泡率 **< 2%**（均值置信区间上限落入该范围）即判为"接近零"。理由：1F1B 基线在 p=4、M=16 时理论气泡率为 (p−1)/(M+p−1)=3/19≈15.8%，p=8、M=16 时为 7/23≈30.4%；将阈值定在 2% 意味着相对 1F1B 降幅 ≥ ~85%，足以区分"调度算法确实消除气泡"与"仅略有改善"。
- 辅判据：同时报告 ZB-2p 相对 1F1B 的**相对下降幅度**（1 − bubble_ZB2p / bubble_1F1B），并与理论公式（待核对，见 §1）对照。

## 1. 执行前准备：旗标核验（有效性的前置条件，未完成不得开跑）

在所用 Megatron-LM 源码中逐项核对，结果写入实验记录并作为前置条件：
1. **`--enable-zero-bubble`**：在 `megatron/training/arguments.py` 确认旗标名、默认值，及它是否为启用 zero-bubble 调度分支的总开关。
2. **`--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward`**：在 `arguments.py` 与 `megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/schedules.py` 确认其语义（是 backward-in-flight 上限还是调度变体选择器），以及取 2×p 时激活的是 **ZB-2p** 还是 ZB-V/ZB-H 变体——判据是调度循环中 warmup 微批计数/两遍（two-pass）backward 的分支条件。若发现取值映射不同（例如需要额外旗标如两遍执行开关、`--enable-zero-bubble` 之外的细分开关），**记入设计文档并在启动命令中补齐**。
3. **计时器**：确认 `--zero-bubble-pipeline-timer`（或等价旗标）的输出格式：各 rank 的 bubble rate 定义、统计哪些迭代、输出位置（stdout/log）。
4. **理论公式核对**：从论文与代码核对 ZB-2p 理论气泡率公式及 1F1B 公式 (p−1)/(M+p−1)，写入记录作为预期值来源。以上任一项无法核实则实验中止并回报。

## 2. 气泡率定义与测量口径（写死）

- **分母与分子**：气泡率 = 每卡在稳态迭代窗口内 **GPU 空闲时间占比**，即 bubble_rate = (窗口时长 − ∑该卡实际前向/后向计算占用时长) / 窗口时长。窗口为去掉 warmup 与 cooldown 后的连续迭代区间（具体跳过迭代数从代码 warmup 步骤数 p−1 推得并记入文档）。
- **warmup/cooldown**：明确**不计入**气泡率统计窗口（它们是算法固有部分，计入会抬高所有方法的表观气泡率）；但在报告中单独报告一次"含 warmup/cooldown 的端到端气泡率"作为参考。
- **口径层次**：以**框架自报 pipeline timer** 为主指标；外部 profiler（torch profiler/nsys 时间线）为交叉验证。两者偏差 >2 个百分点时，以外部时间线人工复核并报告分歧原因。跨卡结果取各 rank 的最大气泡率（瓶颈 rank）与均值两个口径分别报告。
- **计时代理**：若无空闲时间直接输出，则以稳态迭代平均耗时相对该卡纯计算耗时的膨胀量代理，代理换算式记入文档。

## 3. 实验矩阵

- 模型：GPT 类 decoder-only，约 124M–350M（hidden 1024–1536，24 层），每 stage 单卡可容纳；seq_len 与 batch_size 固定并记录。
- 流水线级数 p ∈ {4, 8}，每级 1 卡，TP=1、DP=1（即 4/8 卡，单机或单机多卡）。
- 微批次 M ∈ {8, 16, 32}（气泡率理论 ∝ (p−1)/M，扫描验证趋势）。
- 方法：{1F1B 基线, ZB-2p}；总配置 2×3×2 = 12 个。
- 重复：每配置 **≥5 次独立运行**（独立进程/顺序随机化），固定模型种子，记录 GPU 型号、驱动、NCCL/PyTorch/Megatron commit。
- 对照：1F1B 必须复现理论 (p−1)/(M+p−1) ±测量误差，否则测量管线先修正再继续。

## 4. 统计与分析计划

- 每配置报告稳态气泡率的**均值 ± 标准差与 95% 置信区间**（n≥5；若用 n=5，正态近似下以 t 分布计算 CI，并注明样本量小、以稳健中位数佐证）。
- 对比检验：同 (p, M) 下 ZB-2p vs 1F1B 做 Welch t 检验（或 n 小时 Mann-Whitney U），报告效应量与相对下降幅度；检验方向为单侧（预期 ZB-2p 更低）。
- **计时开销处理**：比较开启/关闭 profiler 时的端到端耗时，差值 <1% 才采信 profiler 数据；主指标取自无 profiler 的运行。
- **跨卡时钟/事件同步**：气泡率按各卡自身事件区间计算（rank 内相对时间），避免绝对时钟对齐问题；跨卡对比仅用同一次运行内的时间线。每次运行前做 NCCL 预热迭代并丢弃。
- 异常值处理：预登记规则——单次运行结果偏离同配置中位数 >3×MAD 时复核日志后决定剔除，剔除记录留痕。

## 5. 可行性说明

- **硬件假设**：单节点 8×GPU（A100/H100 40–80GB 或同级），p=4 用其中 4 卡。所有配置显存需求 <40GB/卡（小模型 + 每 stage 一卡），ZB-2p 额外内存开销（约 2(p−1) 个激活缓冲，按论文）仍在余量内。
- **单次运行时长量级**：小模型、数十次迭代即可进入稳态，单次运行预计 2–10 分钟；12 配置 × 5 次 ≈ 60 次运行，含启动开销约 1–2 个 GPU 日内可完成。
- **沙箱自足性**：当前沙箱无 GPU、无网络、仓库未提供（/workspace 仅含 task.json，track.md 注明"design-only，无需仓库与算力"），故本设计**不依赖本沙箱执行**：设计稿本身自足——旗标核验步骤（§1）、测量口径（§2）、判定标准（§0）均已写死，任何具备 8 卡环境与 Megatron-LM 代码的执行者可按稿复现；沙箱内不执行任何实验、不虚构结果。

## 6. 假设（区别于固定要求）

- 目标框架为 Megatron-LM 且 ZB-2p 实现于其 pipeline_parallel 调度模块（源码不可见，属待核实假设）。
- 模型按层切分流水线、GPT 类结构；理论气泡率公式以论文为准。
- 任务注记 `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward = 2×p` 足以激活 ZB-2p（若 §1 核验否证，则以代码为准修订命令并记录）。

## 7. 预登记结论模板

- 若 ZB-2p 稳态气泡率 CI 上限 <2% 且显著低于 1F1B：回答"是，实测接近零"，并报告与理论的偏差及瓶颈 rank 分析。
- 若介于 2%–1F1B 理论值之间：回答"显著降低但未达零"，分析残余气泡来源（warmup 残留、通信、负载不均）。
- 若与 1F1B 无显著差异或复现失败：回答"否/不可判定"，并指出旗标核验或测量管线的失效点。

payload.answer:
## Initial inspection findings

The workspace at /workspace contains **only a `task.json`** — no codebase is present. The task metadata itself states: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."* There is therefore no Megatron-LM / zero-bubble-pipeline source tree, no README, no benchmark scripts, and no configuration files to inspect here. I confirmed with filesystem-wide searches (top-level directories and name searches for megatron/zero-bubble artifacts) that nothing relevant exists outside /workspace.

Consequently, the design below is grounded in the documented behavior of the upstream codebases this question clearly refers to: the **Megatron-LM pipeline-parallelism implementation with zero-bubble support** (the Megatron-LM PR that added `--enable-zero-bubble`, `--zero-bubble-max-pending`, `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward`) and its research precursor, the **zero-bubble-pipeline repository** (Qi et al., "Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism," 2024), which contains the automatic schedule-search algorithm (`vpp_scheduler`-style automatic search), a `visualize.py` tool that emits per-rank SVG timelines, and bubble-rate formulas. I will state every source-dependent claim as an assumption to be verified against the actual repo when one is supplied.

## Proposed experimental approach (high level)

**Research question:** Does the automatic scheduler's ZB-2p output achieve near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs?

**1. Codebase / entry points (to be verified once a repo is available):**
- Schedule selection: `--enable-zero-bubble` plus `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 2p` (e.g., `--pipeline-model-parallel-size 4` → `8`), with the automatic schedule search enabled (in the research repo this is the default path that invokes the automatic solver; in Megatron-LM it corresponds to the ZB path that builds a schedule for `v = 2p`).
- Profiling entry points: (a) the repo's `visualize.py` / timeline dump for exact per-microbatch schedule inspection; (b) end-to-end throughput runs (train step time) compared against a computed zero-bubble theoretical runtime; (c) optional PyTorch profiler / NSYS traces of each pipeline rank to measure per-rank idle ("bubble") time directly.

**2. Measurement definition (decide this up front, two complementary metrics):**
- **Primary: timeline-based bubble rate.** From per-rank timelines (SVG schedule dump and/or profiler trace), compute bubble_rate = (total rank time − busy compute time) / total rank time for the steady-state window, and also the paper-style bubble formula ((p−1)·(t_f+t_b)/[(s)(t_f+t_b+t_w)]-type) for cross-checking. "Near zero" will be pre-registered as **bubble rate ≤ 2%** (ZB-2p has zero theoretical bubble; 2% absorbs measurement noise; baseline 1F1B is expected ≥ (p−1)/(m+p−1) ≈ tens of percent).
- **Secondary: throughput ratio.** Measured step time vs. analytically derived zero-bubble ideal time; consistency between the two metrics guards against a scheduler that looks good on paper but stalls in practice.

**3. Configurations to profile (factorial, kept small to fit a modest GPU budget):**
- Pipeline sizes p ∈ {4, 8}; microbatches m ∈ {8·p, 16·p} (sufficiently large to be in steady state); model: a standard GPT-style transformer sized so forward+backward ≈ tens of ms (e.g., ~1–6B parameters with sequence length 2048, hidden 2048–4096) — small enough per-GPU memory to allow v=2p in-flight backward activations without OOM.
- GPUs: single node 8×A100/H100 (p=4 needs 4 GPUs, p=8 uses all 8 with one rank per GPU; no model parallelism in the first pass so F/B times are uniform).
- Baselines, identical model/data/TP/PP settings, only the schedule flags changed: (i) eager 1F1B (default Megatron), (ii) ZB-1p (`--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward p`, or the ZB-V equivalent), (iii) ZB-2p.
- Replication: ≥5 timed iterations after warm-up, median and IQR; fixed data loader and seeds.

**4. Controls / confounder mitigation:**
- Disable or hold constant dataloading (synthetic/fixed cached data) and run a non-pipeline (single-stage or TP-only) reference to quantify pure GEMM/comm time.
- Check comm-vs-compute overlap: bubble accounting must distinguish "rank idle waiting for schedule input" from "rank idle due to network jitter" — verify ZB-2p's added p2p traffic (double-buffered backward sends) doesn't degrade throughput and get misread.
- Determinism check of the scheduler: run schedule search twice (different seeds if the solver is stochastic) and diff the schedules; verify the emitted schedule matches the known ZB-2p pattern (forward passes pushed ahead, backwards released by `v=2p` constraint) before benchmarking.
- Warm-up excluded; steady-state window (middle ~50% of microbatches) used for bubble computation so ramp-up/fill-drain phases don't inflate the estimate.
- Timer/profiler sync across ranks (barrier + synchronized clocks, or a single trace file) to avoid cross-rank clock skew faking bubbles.

**5. Interpretation rule:** ZB-2p "truly achieves near-zero in practice" iff (a) measured timeline bubble rate ≤ 2% across all (p, m) configurations, (b) throughput within ~3% of theoretical zero-bubble ideal, and (c) both are significantly better than 1F1B and ZB-1p (paired comparison over iterations).

## Consequential assumptions (mine, to be confirmed)

1. The actual codebase will be the Megatron-LM/zero-bubble-pipeline family where `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 2p` selects the ZB-2p schedule via automatic search; flag names, schedule-search API, and visualize tooling may differ in whatever repo is finally supplied.
2. Hardware: 8×A100/H100 (or comparable) single node with NVLink-class interconnect is available; no multi-node experiments.
3. Runtime budget: hours, not days — each configuration run is a ~1–3 min training window plus profiler overhead; total across ~8 configurations × 3 schedules × 5 reps is well under a day.
4. The automatic scheduler is deterministic (or repeatable with a fixed seed) for fixed (p, m, timing estimates); I will verify this rather than assume it, since the search may depend on estimated per-microbatch times.
5. F/B compute times are approximately uniform across stages (no model parallelism skew); otherwise a "bubble" per the paper's definition can look nonzero even for a perfect schedule.

## Key uncertainties

- Exact flag semantics in the supplied repo (e.g., whether ZB-2p requires `--enable-zero-bubble` plus the backward-pending flag, and whether the automatic solver is a separate entry point) — to be resolved by source inspection when the repo is provided.
- Whether the repo exposes exact per-microbatch timelines (making the timeline metric precise) or only aggregate timing (forcing the timing-ratio metric to be primary).
- How "near zero" should be thresholded (2% is a defensible pre-registration choice but is a design decision, not a fact).
- Sensitivity of ZB-2p to OOM with large v=2p pending backwards on smaller GPUs; memory headroom must be measured before the factorial run.
- Confounders that could mask or fake the result: network jitter and NCCL/p2p contention (can create fake bubbles), warm-up/caching effects (can hide bubbles), clock skew across ranks, and dataloading stalls outside the schedule.

Per the task scope, this is a design-only proposal; no experiment has been run and no results are claimed. I'm ready to turn this into a full protocol (exact commands, measurement scripts, analysis plan) upon approval.

payload.answer:
# Final Experiment Design (design-only; no experiment has been run)

**Question:** Does the automatic scheduling algorithm's ZB-2p output truly achieve a near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs?

**Activation target:** ZB-2p is enabled via `--enable-zero-bubble` plus `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 2p` (i.e., the flag set to twice the number of pipeline stages, p), with the automatic schedule search engaged.

---

## 1. Exact setup

### 1.1 Codebase and entry points

- **Codebase (assumption A1):** The Megatron-LM fork with zero-bubble support — either upstream Megatron-LM (which merged the zero-bubble pipeline PR adding `--enable-zero-bubble`, `--zero-bubble-max-pending`, `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward`) or the research repository `zero-bubble-pipeline` (Qi et al., 2024), which contains the automatic schedule search, `visualize.py` for per-rank SVG timelines, and benchmark scripts.
- **Verification step for A1:** On obtaining the repo, (a) `grep -r "zero-bubble-max-pending-backward"` to confirm flag names; (b) locate the automatic-search entry point (search for `automatic`, `search_schedule`, `vpp_scheduler`, or `solve`); (c) locate the timeline/visualization tool; (d) read the README's bubble-rate definition. If flag names or entry points differ, adapt the commands below; the design logic is unchanged.
- **Entry points:** the standard pretraining launcher (e.g., `pretrain_gpt.py`) for timing runs; the schedule-search / schedule-dump entry point for inspecting the solver's output; `visualize.py` (or equivalent) for timeline rendering.

### 1.2 ZB-2p activation (exact flag combination)

For pipeline size p:
```
--enable-zero-bubble
--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward <2p>
```
plus the automatic-schedule flag(s) identified in §1.1 verification (in the research repo the automatic search is the path used for ZB-2p; confirm whether an explicit `--automatic-pipeline-schedule`-style flag or a default is needed). Also verify whether `--zero-bubble-max-pending` must be set explicitly or is derived.

**Pre-run schedule sanity check (mandatory, §3):** dump the solver's schedule for each (p, m) configuration and verify it matches the canonical ZB-2p pattern (warmup forwards limited to roughly m + p rather than 2p−1; backwards released at double-buffer depth 2p; final p microbatches' backwards draining without idle).

### 1.3 Configurations (factorial design)

| Axis | Levels |
|---|---|
| Pipeline size p | 4, 8 |
| Microbatches m | 8·p, 16·p (i.e., 32/64 at p=4; 64/128 at p=8) |
| Model | GPT-style transformer, ~1–6B params (hidden 2048–4096, layers chosen so per-microbatch F+B ≈ 30–80 ms), seq len 2048, batch = m per pipeline step |
| Parallelism | PP = p; TP = 1; DP = 1 (first pass; no model parallelism so stage times are uniform) |
| Hardware | 1 node, 8× A100/H100 80GB (or comparable). p=4 uses 4 GPUs; p=8 uses all 8. |
| Precision | bf16, fixed seed, fixed dataset (synthetic or cached real data — no dataloader stalls) |

Rationale: m ≥ 4p ensures a substantial steady state; p=4 and p=8 span the regime where 1F1B's theoretical bubble ((p−1)/(m+p−1): ~11% vs ~3% at m=64) differs enough from zero for the comparison to be discriminating.

### 1.4 Baselines (matched settings; only schedule flags change)

1. **Eager 1F1B** — default Megatron pipeline schedule (no zero-bubble flags).
2. **ZB-1p** — `--enable-zero-bubble --zero-bubble-max-pending-backward p` (paper's ZB-H/V-equivalent with theoretical bubble ~ (p−1)/(m+p−1) × ½ factor; exact formula per paper).
3. **ZB-2p** — the treatment, as in §1.2.

All runs use identical model config, batch size, seeds, dataloader, warmup/iteration counts, and precision.

### 1.5 Replication

- ≥ 30 warmup iterations (excluded), ≥ 20 timed iterations per run; median and IQR reported.
- Each configuration × schedule cell replicated 3 times (fresh process) to capture run-to-run variance; scheduler determinism check (§3.1) run once per configuration.

---

## 2. Measurement plan

### 2.1 Metric 1 — Timeline-based per-rank bubble rate (primary)

- **Source (assumption A2, verify):** per-microbatch schedule dump (`visualize.py` SVG or a JSON trace) and/or PyTorch profiler / NSYS per-rank traces. Verification: confirm the tool emits per-microbatch start/end times per rank; if only aggregate timing exists, promote Metric 2 to primary.
- **Computation:** for each rank r and steady-state window W (see §2.3):
  `bubble_rate_r = (|W| − busy_compute_time_r(W)) / |W|`, where busy time = union of forward and backward kernel-interval coverage on that rank (from profiler kernels, or schedule intervals from the dump).
  Report `mean_r bubble_rate_r` and the max across ranks.
- **Complementarity:** cross-check the timeline-derived rate against the paper's closed-form bubble formula for ZB-2p (theoretically 0) and 1F1B ((p−1)/(m+p−1)) — a large discrepancy flags measurement error rather than physics.

### 2.2 Metric 2 — Timing-ratio vs theoretical ideal (secondary)

- Derive the zero-bubble ideal step time: `T_ideal = t_f + t_b + m·(t_f + t_b)/1`-style steady-state bound from measured single-stage F/B times (measure t_f, t_b once per configuration with the profiler on a single rank).
- Report `efficiency = T_ideal / T_measured_step` per run. For ZB-2p, near-zero bubble implies efficiency ≥ ~0.98.

### 2.3 Steady-state windowing rule (pre-registered)

- Exclude the first 4p and last 4p microbatch slots (warm-up fill / drain) of each timed iteration; analyze the middle contiguous window covering ≥ 50% of microbatches. Window boundaries are defined on the schedule timeline, not on wall-clock, so they are schedule-invariant.
- Across timed iterations, the analyzed windows are concatenated only after verifying iteration-to-iteration schedule stability.

### 2.4 Pre-registered "near zero" threshold

- **bubble_rate ≤ 2%** (max-across-ranks), for the timeline metric; **efficiency ≥ 0.98** for the timing metric.
- **Justification:** ZB-2p's theoretical bubble is 0, so any residual must be measurement/kernel/comm noise. Empirically, kernel-launch gaps and p2p jitter on healthy NVLink nodes contribute ≲1–2% idle; a 2% bound therefore distinguishes "truly near zero" from "merely better than baseline," while 1F1B's expected 3–11%+ bubble at our configurations cannot pass it. The threshold is fixed before data collection.

---

## 3. Controls and validity checks

1. **Scheduler determinism & emitted-schedule verification:** run the automatic search twice per configuration (and, if it accepts a seed, with two different seeds); diff the schedules. Then verify the schedule's structure matches the canonical ZB-2p pattern and that the effective pending-backward limit equals 2p (log inspection). If schedules differ across runs, record the seed/config dependency and report bubble rates per emitted schedule rather than pooling.
2. **Communication confounders:** (a) synthetic/frozen dataloader so input stalls can't masquerade as bubbles; (b) report p2p message counts and bytes per step for ZB-2p (which sends more backward activations) and compare throughput to rule out comm degradation being the true cause of any gap; (c) if available, run with a fixed NCCL algorithm/environment across cells.
3. **Clock sync:** before profiling, execute a barrier and verify cross-rank clock offset < 1 ms (e.g., via synchronized `time.time()` exchange or a single trace collector). Prefer single-trace collection (torch profiler per rank merged by the tool) over cross-rank wall-clock arithmetic.
4. **Warm-up:** JIT/allocator/cache warm-up iterations excluded per §2.3; CUDA graphs off (they alter launch-gap structure) or on for all cells identically.
5. **Memory feasibility of v=2p:** ZB-2p keeps up to 2p in-flight backwards; measure peak memory in a short pilot run per configuration before the factorial runs. If peak > 90% of HBM, activate activation-recompute offloading consistent across all schedules, or fall back (§5).
6. **Single-stage reference:** one non-pipelined run per model config to establish pure F/B compute time and detect any per-rank heterogeneity (should be uniform; if not, per-stage expected bubbles are computed from measured stage times rather than the uniform formula).

---

## 4. Analysis plan

- **Primary criterion (C1):** mean-across-ranks (and max-across-ranks) timeline bubble rate ≤ 2% in every (p, m) configuration for ZB-2p, in the pre-registered steady-state window.
- **Secondary criterion (C2):** throughput efficiency ≥ 0.98 (T_ideal/T_measured) in every configuration; C1 and C2 must agree (disagreement triggers a measurement audit, not a conclusion).
- **Superiority criterion (C3):** ZB-2p bubble rate significantly lower than 1F1B and ZB-1p — paired comparison over the 3 replicates per cell (median difference with IQR; with n=3 replicates × 20 iterations, report medians and dispersion and a rank-based sign test per configuration; avoid over-strong parametric claims given small replicate counts).
- **Reporting:** one table per configuration (p, m) × schedule: median step time, IQR, timeline bubble rate (mean/max rank), efficiency vs ideal, peak memory. One figure per configuration: per-rank timeline excerpt for ZB-2p vs 1F1B. Verdict rule: ZB-2p "truly achieves near-zero in practice" iff C1 ∧ C2 ∧ C3 all hold; partial outcomes reported explicitly (e.g., C1 passes but C2 fails ⇒ near-zero *schedule* but overhead-dominated *implementation*).
- **Deviations:** any deviation from this protocol (flag differences, fallbacks used, threshold changes) is documented before analysis; thresholds are not adjusted post hoc.

---

## 5. Feasibility and fallbacks

- **Runtime estimate:** each run is a ~60–150 s training window (30 warmup + 20 timed iterations at ~2–5 s/step) plus profiling overhead. Cells: 2 p-levels × 2 m-levels × 3 schedules × 3 replicates = 36 runs ≈ 2–3 h including pilots and the determinism checks; comfortably within a day on one 8-GPU node.
- **Hardware footprint:** ≤ 8 GPUs, ≤ 80 GB HBM per GPU at the 6B-param upper end (verify in the §3.5 pilot).
- **Fallbacks:**
  - *OOM at v=2p:* enable selective recompute identically across schedules; or reduce m at fixed p; or drop to p=8 with a smaller model. Never change memory strategy between schedules within a comparison.
  - *Fewer GPUs (e.g., 4 only):* run only p=4 configurations; the p-level comparison is dropped, not approximated.
  - *No timeline tooling:* promote Metric 2 (timing ratio) to primary and use profiler-derived busy-time histograms as a coarse substitute.
  - *Automatic solver stochastic or unavailable:* fix the seed / fall back to the hand-written ZB-2p schedule in the repo, and explicitly report that the *automatic* claim is untested in that case.
  - *Jitter-heavy cluster:* increase replicates to 5 and use medians; add a p2p latency probe before the campaign.

---

## Assumptions register (unverified, each with its resolving check)

| # | Assumption | Verification step |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | Repo is Megatron-LM/zero-bubble-pipeline with the named flags and automatic search | grep flags + README + schedule-search entry point |
| A2 | Per-microbatch timelines are obtainable (visualize.py or profiler) | Run the tool on a 2-stage toy model |
| A3 | 8×A100/H100 single node available; ≤ 8 GPUs suffice | Hardware audit before pilots |
| A4 | Scheduler output is deterministic for fixed (p, m, estimates) | Double-run + schedule diff (§3.1) |
| A5 | F/B times uniform across stages (TP=1, homogeneous GPUs) | Single-stage reference timings |
| A6 | "Near zero" = ≤ 2% bubble / ≥ 0.98 efficiency | Fixed pre-registration; justified in §2.4 |

No experiment has been executed and no results are claimed; this document is the complete design deliverable.

**Initial Inspection के निष्कर्ष**

1. `/workspace` में केवल `task.json` मौजूद है; कोई track.md फ़ाइल, कोड, dataset या config नहीं है। `task.json` के `documents.track.md` फ़ील्ड में ब्रीफ़ दिया गया है: *"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."*
2. वातावरण: network disabled, GPU नहीं, system Python में torch/transformers/datasets इंस्टॉल नहीं हैं — यानी कोई वास्तविक inference चलाना feasible नहीं है, और design-only स्कोप की पुष्टि करता है।

**प्रस्तावित Approach (Draft Plan)**

**1. RepoBench 'cross_file_first' को समझना:**
- RepoBench (Zhang et al., ICLR 2024, repo: thevgergjh/RepoBench) तीन retrieval-augmented settings देता है: `repo-level` (सारी files दिखाई जाती हैं), `cross-file` (सिर्फ़ एक referenced file दिखाई जाती है), और `repo-level-prompt` (retrieved files दिखाई जाती हैं)। हर setting में दो सब-variants हैं: `cross_file_first` — referenced file पहली बार project में import हुई है, और `cross_file_random` — referenced file पहले से import थी। हमारा target: `repobench_python_v1.1` का `cross_file_first` split।
- हर example में: `repo_name`, `file_path`, `context` (referenced file की relevant lines: `code`, `all_line`, `all_line_import`), `import_module`, `code_snippet` (current file की prompt lines), `next_line` (ground truth)।
- Prompt construction: context + code_snippet मिलाकर next-line completion generate करवाना है — यही बड़े code-specialized मॉडल (CodeLlama-7b) की स्ट्रेंथ है, इसलिए comparison अर्थपूर्ण है।

**2. Metrics:**
- **Edit similarity** (Levenshtein-based, RepoBench का मुख्य metric) — मुख्य metric के रूप में।
- **Exact match (EM)** — strict secondary metric।
- Optional: token-level accuracy नहीं जोड़ेंगे जब तक researcher न कहे, ताकि design सरल रहे।

**3. Controls (दोनों मॉडलों के लिए समान):**
- समान prompt template और instruction (CodeLlama instruction-tuned हो तो base variant चुनना बेहतर ताकि GPT-2 जैसे base model के साथ तुलना निष्पक्ष रहे — CodeLlama-7b base चुनने का सुझाव)।

**4. Feasibility / Tokenizer-Context अंतर:**
- GPT-2: context window 1024 tokens (base) — यह सबसे बड़ी बाधा है; इसलिए shared cap 1024 tokens तक रखना व्यावहारिक है, या GPT-2 के context तक। यह GPT-2 को असहाय नहीं बनाएगा, बल्कि context दोनों को समान मिलेगा (fair comparison)।

- Tokenizer अंतर से prompt tokens अलग होंगे, पर content समान रहेगा; हम characters/context window की सीमा को समान रखेंगे और दोनों के लिए truncation लॉग करेंगे।

**5. अगले चरण (approval के बाद):**
- पूरा design document: exact prompt template, metric formulas, sample-size न्यायोचित करण (power analysis), दोनों models के वर्शन, results presentation format (mean±std, paired comparison), और संभावित confounders (context truncation rate, tokenizer differences)।

**क्या यह approach सही लगता है? विशेष रूप से कृपया बताएँ:** (a) क्या CodeLlama-7b base variant ठीक है या instruct चाहिए, (b) sample size कोई प्राथमिकता (200/500/1000), (c) शेयर्ड context cap 1024 ठीक है या GPT-2-large (2048) बनाम CodeLlama के बीच कोई और साझा cap।

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design: GPT-2 बनाम CodeLlama-7b — RepoBench Python, `cross_file_first`

**Status:** Design-only document. कोई experiment नहीं चलाया गया; कोई results नहीं माने गए हैं। (वातावरण पुष्टि: /workspace में केवल task.json, torch/transformers अनुपस्थित, network disabled, GPU नहीं — इसलिए निष्पादन इस design के दायरे में नहीं है।)

---

## 1. शोध प्रश्न

GPT-2 (base) बनाम CodeLlama-7b (base) की performance अंतर क्या है RepoBench Python `cross_file_first` setting में (cross-file context, जिसमें referenced file पहली बार project में import हुई है)?

## 2. Dataset और Task सेटअप

- **Data:** `repobench_python_v1.1`, `cross_file_first` split (स्रोत: HF dataset `thevgergjh/RepoBench`; original GitHub repo-bench JSON विकल्प के रूप में — दोनों एक ही underlying benchmark हैं)।
- **हर example के fields:** `repo_name`, `file_path`, `context` (referenced file की relevant lines: variants `code`, `all_line`, `all_line_import`), `import_module`, `code_snippet` (current file की prompt lines), `next_line` (ground truth)।
- **Task:** next-line completion — context + code_snippet देकर `next_line` predict करवाना। CodeLlama जैसे code-specialized मॉडल की ताक़त यही है, इसलिए तुलना अर्थपूर्ण है।
- **Primary sampling:** fixed random seed (seed=42) से **n=500 examples**। 200 = pilot tier, 1000 = compute-dependent संभावना।

## 3. Prompt Template (exact, दोनों मॉडलों के लिए समान)

दोनों base (non-instruct) मॉडल हैं, इसलिए raw completion-style template:

```
# Here are some relevant code fragments from other files of the repo:

{CONTEXT_LINES}

# The below code from the repo contains the following imports:

{IMPORT_MODULE}

# The following code snippet is from the file being completed:

{CODE_SNIPPET}
```

यह RepoBench के original evaluation template (cross-file variants) के अनुरूप है। Base मॉडलों के लिए कोई chat/instruction wrapper नहीं।
- **Sensitivity (secondary, वैकल्पिक):** `CodeLlama-7b-Python` variant को sensitivity analysis के रूप में एक ही पाइपलाइन पर चलाया जा सकता है; प्राथमिक निष्कर्ष CodeLlama-7b (base) पर आधारित रहेंगे।
- **Robustness (वैकल्पिक):** GPT-2-large को optional robustness check (context cap बढ़ने पर नतीजों की स्थिरता) के तौर पर उल्लेख।

## 4. Controls (समानता गारंटी)

| Control | मान |
|---|---|
| Prompt template | ऊपर दिया गया, identical text दोनों के लिए |
| Decoding | Greedy (temperature=0, top_p=1, no sampling); `max_new_tokens` = 64 |
| Context cap | **1024 tokens** shared cap (GPT-2 base primary है तब तक) |
| Truncation policy | Context की **शुरुआत** truncate; recent lines prompt के अंत में (RepoBench default) |
| Dropped examples | जिन examples में context पूरी तरह truncate हो जाए, वे **दोनों** मॉडलों के लिए समान रूप से हटाए जाएँ; **truncation rate** रिपोर्ट होगा |
| Example समूह | वही 500 (seed=42) examples दोनों मॉडलों के लिए |
| Tokenizer अंतर | Content समान; हर model के अपने tokenizer से tokenize। Token-निरपेक्ष **character-cap fallback**: यदि tokenizer से cap enforce करने में असमानता आए, तो समान character-count cap (जैसे 4096 chars) दोनों पर लागू |

## 5. Metrics (formulas)

- **Edit Similarity (primary):** `1 − Levenshtein(generated, ground_truth) / max(len(generated), len(ground_truth))`, generated और ground truth को normalize (strip whitespace, leading indent) करके। RepoBench का primary metric — scale [0,1]।
- **Exact Match (secondary):** EM = 1 यदि normalized generated string == normalized ground truth; अन्यथा 0।
- प्रति example मान रिकॉर्ड; aggregate mean±std; bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples)।

## 6. Sample-size आधार (power analysis — arithmetic ही है, experiment नहीं)

Paired design (एक ही examples दोनों पर) के लिए paired t-test, α=0.05 two-sided, power=0.80, minimum detectable paired difference (SD units): d* = (1.96+0.84)/√n।

| n | d* | Δ (SD_diff=0.20) | Δ (0.25) | Δ (0.30) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 (pilot) | 0.198 | ~0.040 | ~0.050 | ~0.059 |
| **500 (primary)** | **0.125** | **~0.025** | **~0.031** | **~0.038** |
| 1000 (compute-dependent) | 0.089 | ~0.018 | ~0.022 | ~0.027 |

अर्थात n=500 पर लगभग 2.5–4 edit-similarity percentage points का अंतर detect होगा (SD_diff की धारणा पर; SD_diff का actual मान pilot से estimate होगा)। Paired design ही चुना गया क्योंकि यह variance काफ़ी घटाता है।

## 7. Results Presentation Format

- मुख्य तालिका: प्रति मॉडल mean Edit Similarity ± std, EM mean ± std, 95% bootstrap CI, n (post-drop)।
- **Paired comparison:** प्रति example difference `Δᵢ = ES_code − ES_gpt2`; paired t-test + Wilcoxon signed-rank (non-normality के लिए), और Δᵢ का mean±CI।
- Truncation rate, प्रति मॉडल token count वितरण, और फ़ाइल-रीपो स्तर की clustering का संकेत (उदाहरण के तौर पर cluster-robust check: रीपो-स्तर grouped mean के साथ sensitivity) रिपोर्ट होगा।
- Stratified breakdown (context variant: code/all_line/all_line_import) secondary रिपोर्ट।

## 8. Confounders और Mitigation

1. **Context truncation rate का अंतर** — समान cap/policy और दोनों के लिए समान dropped-set से नियंत्रित; rate रिपोर्ट।
2. **Tokenizer अंतर** — content समान, character-cap fallback।
3. **Instruction-vs-base mismatch** — दोनों base variants; अगर instruct उपयोग हो तो निष्पक्षता भंग होती, इसलिए टाला।
4. **Repository-level leakage/cluster effect** — paired design और seed-fixed subset; रीपो स्तर sensitivity check।
5. **Decoding स्टोकेस्टिसिटी** — greedy; शून्य randomness।
6. **GPT-2 का सीमित code pretraining** — यह confounder नहीं बल्कि शोध प्रश्न का ही हिस्सा है; दुभाष्य विषय है।

## 9. Feasibility (Compute Budget — मान्यताएँ, मापे गए आँकड़े नहीं)

- **GPT-2 (124M):** CPU पर भी 500 examples × 1024 tokens pragmatic; अनुमान: कुछ घंटे CPU पर, GPU पर मिनटों।
- **CodeLlama-7b:** बिना GPU practical नहीं (224 CPU affinity है पर inference बहुत धीमा)। आवश्यक: एक GPU (~24GB) या 4-bit quantization, या API fallback। **यह मान्यता है कि इस तरह का compute निष्पादन के समय उपलब्ध होगा** — वर्तमान वातावरण (GPU नहीं) में यह चरण असंभव है, इसलिए इस design का execution दूसरे वातावरण में होगा।
- समय अनुमान: CodeLlama-7b 4-bit GPU पर 500 examples ≈ 1–3 घंटे (अनुमान, न कि measurement)।
- डेटा पहुँच: HF dataset को एक बार डाउनलोड कर स्थानीय कैश करना (network required)।

## 10. स्पष्ट धारणाएँ (Assumptions — ये जानबूझकर माने गए हैं, स्रोत-समर्थित दावे नहीं)

1. `thevgergjh/RepoBench` व v1.1 स्कीमा सही स्रोत है; वास्तविक schema निष्पादन से पहले verify होगा।
2. RepoBench का original cross-file prompt template जानबूझकर अपनाया गया — यह पेपर के reported numbers से मोटी comparability देता है।
3. दोनों मॉडल HF hub वर्शन: `gpt2` (base, 124M) और `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf` (base)।
4. Edit Similarity की शुद्ध formula पेपर से verify होगी (Levenshtein आधारित — मुझे यह स्मरण है पर exact normalization पेपर से ही confirm होगी)।
5. SD_diff≈0.20–0.30 (edit-similarity scale) एक plausible prior है, मापा हुआ नहीं।

## 11. बची हुई अनिश्चितताएँ (Uncertainties)

- SD_diff का वास्तविक मान — pilot (n=200) से estimate होगा।
- CodeLlama वर्शन का HF snapshot revision / quantization का metrics पर प्रभाव।
- Dataset के exact schema/field नाम v1.1 में — निष्पादन से पहले inspect होंगे।
- Character-cap fallback का वास्तविक प्रभाव — pilot की truncation stats देखकर तय होगा।
- Compute उपलब्धता — इस design के निष्पादन के लिए बाहरी आवश्यकता।

---

**स्रोत आधार:** RepoBench (Zhang et al., ICLR 2024), HF `thevgergjh/RepoBench`, Meta CodeLlama card, HF `gpt2` model card। Power-analysis आँकड़े सीधे standard z-value arithmetic से ऊपर कैलकुलेट हुए।

Вопрос исследования: как small LM (типа GPT-2) сравнивается с большим code-specialized (CodeLlama-7b) на RepoBench Python, setting 'cross_file_first'.

Сейчас НЕ решаем задачу целиком. Сделай только следующее:

1. Input/repository inspection: осмотрись в /workspace — что реально там лежит (track.md и прочее), какие файлы/конфиги/данные есть, что из этого релевантно для дизайна. Прочитай track.md полностью и перескажи, что он фиксирует по deliverable и ограничениям.
2. На основе увиденного предложи proposed approach: как бы ты структурировал дизайн эксперимента — какие модели, какой снапшот/сплит RepoBench cross_file_first, какие метрики (например, exact match / identifier match / edit similarity), какой протокол prompt'ов и контекста cross-file.
3. Явно перечисли consequential assumptions и uncertainties: всё, что ты предполагаешь про setup, ресурсы, бюджет, доступность датасета/весов — и что из этого просто допущение, а не подтверждённый факт.

Ничего из того, что не видно в /workspace или не дано явно — это assumption, помечай так и есть. Жду: краткий отчёт по инспекции + proposed approach + список допущений. # ДИЗАЙН-ЭКСПЕРИМЕНТА (design-only, финальный)

**Исследовательский вопрос.** Как small LM (GPT-2) сравнивается с большим code-specialized LM (CodeLlama-7b base) на RepoBench Python в setting `cross_file_first` — как функция объёма cross-file контекста (R/1k, R/2k, R/4k).

**Роль документа.** Только дизайн. Прогон не выполнялся, результаты не симулируются; все цифры, кроме подтверждённых инспекцией окружения — assumptions (раздел 10).

---

## 1. Модели
- **Primary A (small, general):** `gpt2-large` (774M params), base LM.
- **Primary B (large, code-specialized):** `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf`, **base** (не instruct), без chat-шаблонов — решение зафиксировано, чтобы обе модели были чистыми next-token LM и сравнение не загрязнялось форматированием.
- **Вторично (опционально, режется первым при нехватке бюджета):** свип GPT-2 small (124M) → medium (355M) → large (774M) → XL (1.5B). Роль свипа — частично отделить эффект масштаба от эффекта «code-specialization» (см. раздел 7, confounder C3).

## 2. Датасет и сплиты
- Датасет: `tianyang/repobench_python_v1.1` (RepoBench, Liu et al., ICLR 2024), язык Python, setting `cross_file_first` (целевая строка впервые использует cross-file сущность).
- Retrieval-уровни: **все три** — R/1k, R/2k, R/4k (cross-file контекст ~1k/2k/4k токенов). Основной интерес — кривая качества как функция объёма контекста.
- **Primary: test-сплит** (канонично для бенчмарка). **Dev-сплит: пилот и санити** — отладка пайплайна, верификация кода метрик, проверка промпт-рендера; dev-результаты в основной отчёт не входят.
- Выборка: стратифицированная по retrieval-уровню, **N = 500 на уровень** (1500 total на модель в primary), фиксированный seed, стратификация по имеющимся стратам датасета (если есть — по repo; если нет — простая random без замены). Список id сэмплов фиксируется до прогона и переиспользуется для обеих моделей (одно и то же множество промпт-строк).

## 3. Prompt-протокол и усечение
- Структура промпта (канонический формат RepoBench, поле-состав из датасета): retrieved cross-file snippets → контекст текущего файла выше целевой строки → prefix целевой строки (то, что модель должна дополнить).
- Промпт-строка рендерится **один раз** из полей датасета и подаётся обеим моделям байт-в-байт идентично.
- **Фиксированное усечение** (одинаковое правило для всех моделей и уровней): при превышении токен-бюджета сначала подрезается retrieved-контекст (сверху, сохраняя фрагменты, ближайшие к использованию), затем — самое старое в контексте текущего файла; prefix целевой строки и её хвост не подрезаются никогда. Бюджет: 1536 токенов промпта (assumption из оригинальной бумаги — сверить с датасет-кардом перед стартом).
- Логирование: фактическая длина промпта в токенах **per-model** (GPT-2 BPE vs CodeLlama BPE дают разное число токенов на ту же строку) — обязательное поле в логах (см. confounder C2).

## 4. Декодинг
- Обе модели: greedy decoding, `max_new_tokens = 100`, без sampling-параметров, без few-shot примеров (zero-shot, как в протоколе RepoBench), без stop-хаков за исключением тримминга по newline-семантике датасета (правило тримминга фиксируется в коде метрик одинаково для обеих моделей).
- Идентичные generation-параметры; единственные легитимные отличия — tokenizer и max context window модели (GPT-2 1024 — см. риск R2).

## 5. Метрики (определения фиксируются до прогона)
Все — на **декодированном тексте** (модельно-независимо, т.к. токенизаторы разные), после детерминированного тримминга:
1. **Exact Match (EM):** сгенерированное дополнение строково совпадает с golden-продолжением целевой строки (после нормализации whitespace).
2. **Edit Similarity (ES):** нормализованный Levenshtein = 1 − dist/max(len); в [0,1].
3. **Identifier Match (IM):** identifier-based F1 — извлекаются идентификаторы из golden и предсказания, считается F1 по множествам (определение по бумаге RepoBench).

Первичная метрика для основного вывода: **EM** (самая строгая); ES/IM — вторичные, чувствительные к частичному угадыванию идентификаторов (критично именно для cross_file_first).

## 6. Контролы
- C-1: идентичные промпт-строки (байт-в-байт) для обеих моделей.
- C-2: одинаковый sample-сет, seed, decoding-параметры, код метрик.
- C-3: фиксированная стратегия усечения, независимая от модели.
- C-4: лог per-sample: prompt_id, уровень, per-model токен-длина промпта, raw output, тримнутое дополнение, все 3 метрики.
- C-5: pre-registration — определения метрик, стратификация, тесты записываются в дизайн-документ до прогона; промпт-рендер и код метрик валидируются на dev-сплите до запуска test.

## 7. Confounders (явный раздел документа)
- **C1. Токенизаторы:** одинаковый текст → разное число токенов → разная эффективная подача контекста. Митигация: лог per-model токен-длины (раздел 3), репорт разницы; при анализе — сверка, что промпты в пределах бюджета у обеих моделей.
- **C2. Эффективный контекст:** при усечении модели «видят» разный объём полезного контекста, если усечение применяется к уже токенизированному тексту. Митигация: усечение в символьном/токен-нейтральном пространстве по единому правилу; репорт распределения длин.
- **C3. Специализация confounded с масштабом:** CodeLlama-7b отличается от GPT-2 и код-корпусом, и размером (~7B vs 774M). Это нельзя полностью устранить двухточечным сравнением; свип GPT-2 small→XL — именно инструмент для грубой декомпозиции (если производительность CodeLlama лежит вне тренда GPT-2, это аргумент в пользу эффекта специализации/данных, но доказательством не является). Statement включён в выводы как ограничение.
- **C4. Cross_file_first смещён к редким/новым идентификаторам:** IM-метрика и error analysis частично раскрывают, за счёт чего выигрыш.

## 8. План анализа
- Основной вывод: парное сравнение per-sample (одни и те же сэмплы у обеих моделей):
  - EM: **McNemar's test** на дискордантных парах + точечная разница ΔEM с 95% CI (Wilson/по методу McNemar exact).
  - ES, IM: **paired bootstrap** (10 000 ресемплов, seed фиксирован) — 95% CI для разницы средних.
- Разрезы: (a) по retrieval-уровню R/1k/2k/4k — основной сюжет «функция от объёма контекста»; (b) тренд по размерам GPT-2 (вторичный); (c) длина промпта per-model как ковариата (описательно).
- Множественность: три метрики × три уровня — поправка Бенджамини–Хохберга на уровне метрик, уровни репортим дескриптивно с CI (не как confirmatory).
- Критерий «основного ответа» на вопрос: знак и CI разницы EM/ES/IM на каждом уровне, устойчивость знака по уровням.

## 9. Error analysis (план, без результатов)
- Стратификация ошибок EM по: длине golden-идентификатора; частоте идентификатора в retrieved-контексте (встречается/не встречается в поданном сниппете — ключевая диагностка cross_file_first); расстоянию первого использования от позиции в файле.
- Качественный разбор по 20–30 случайно выбранным дискордантным парам (выигрыш CodeLlama / выигрыш GPT-2) — категории: правильный идентификатор/неправильный, синтаксис, усечение контекста.

## 10. Feasibility, ресурсы, риски
- **Компьют:** инференс-only. CodeLlama-7b bf16 ≈ 14 GB весов + активации → 1×A100/80GB (или 2×24GB с offload) достаточна; GPT-2-семейство тривиально. Оценка нагрузки: primary 1500 сэмплов × 2 модели ≈ 3000 генераций ≤100 токенов — порядка единиц GPU-часов; полный свип добавляет ~3 модели × 1500 — остаётся реалистичным (соответствует решению «N=500 на уровень»).
- **R1. Сеть/веса:** в текущей среде сети нет — скачивание датасета/весов в исполнительной среде; проверить доступность снапшота и лицензию CodeLlama (research-use — разрешает).
- **R2. Context window GPT-2 = 1024 токена < бюджета 1536:** риск, что на R/2k–R/4k промпты физически не влезают в GPT-2. Митигация: правило усечения из раздела 3 применяется к фактическому токен-бюджету **каждой** модели (GPT-2 режется жёстче), а per-model фактическая длина логируется и репортится — иначе результат «GPT-2 хуже на R/4k» будет частично артефактом окна. Это главный методологический риск; альтернатива — исключить R/4k для GPT-2 с явной пометкой (решение за researcher при старте).
- **R3. Dev-сплит мал/недоступен в нужном объёме** — пилот может быть на подвыборке; не влияет на primary (test).
- **R4. Токенизационно-чувствительный тримминг** — фиксируется в коде метрик и валидируется на dev до прогона.

## 11. ASSUMPTIONS (непроверенный блок — по требованию, помечен как непроверенный)
1. Датасет `tianyang/repobench_python_v1.1` доступен на HF; схема полей и размеры test/dev сплитов cross_file_first **не проверены** (сеть disabled).
2. Промпт-формат и токен-бюджет ~1536 соответствуют оригинальной RepoBench — assumption, сверить с датасет-кардом/кодом авторов до старта.
3. `codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf` — корректный id base-модели; лицензия допускает использование — не проверено.
4. GPU-окружение для исполнения будет предоставлено отдельно (спецификация не дана в workspace).
5. Страты датасета (repo-level) пригодны для стратификации — не проверено.
6. track.md в /workspace отсутствует как файл; известна только запись в task.json: «Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required» — формат deliverable сверх «дизайн-документ» не зафиксирован.

Эксперимент не запускался и не симулировался; единственные выполненные действия — инспекция файлов и окружения (ls/find, проверка python/кэша).

Informe de inspección inicial (sin ejecución):

1) Contenido del repositorio: /workspace contiene únicamente task.json. No hay archivo físico track.md; su contenido está embebido en task.json: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." Confirmado: tarea solo de diseño, sin ejecución de experimentos.

2) Datos/documentación disponibles: No hay datasets locales (datasets: []), red deshabilitada, sin GPU, sin librerías (datasets/transformers/torch ausentes). No existe documentación local sobre RepoBench cross_file_first ni sobre GPT-2/CodeLlama-7b. Lo verificable sin inventar: RepoBench es un benchmark de auto-completado de código a nivel repositorio (ICLR 2024) con configuración cross_file_first (completar la primera llamada a una función/clase definida en otro archivo); dataset público en Hugging Face (tianyang/repobench_python_v1.1). Detalles finos (tamaño de splits, plantillas de prompt, métricas exactas) deben confirmarse contra fuentes en la fase de diseño, no desde memoria.

3) Esquema preliminar del diseño experimental:
- Variable independiente: modelo (GPT-2 vs CodeLlama-7b).
- Variables dependientes: Exact Match (EM) del código completado vs. ground truth (métrica estándar de RepoBench), más métricas auxiliares: edit similarity normalizada, tasa de sintaxis válida.
- Controles: mismas muestras (submuestra fija con semilla), mismo formato de prompt (mismo contexto cross-file + archivo actual, misma plantilla, ajustando solo tokenización), mismos parámetros de decodificación (greedy o sampling idéntico, mismo max_new_tokens), misma función de evaluación/normalización para ambos modelos.
- Suposiciones e incertidumbres abiertas: (a) recursos: CodeLlama-7b requiere ~14 GB VRAM en fp16 y este entorno no tiene GPU ni red — la ejecución real requeriría cómputo externo; (b) presupuesto: tamaño de la submuestra por decidir; (c) resultado empírico esperado: ventaja plausible de CodeLlama-7b por tamaño y especialización en código, pero no debe asumirse; (d) confound estructural: ventana de contexto muy distinta (GPT-2 ~1024 tokens vs CodeLlama ~16K), lo que obliga a decidir si se trunca el prompt a un máximo común o se da a cada modelo su máximo — decisión de diseño abierta.
