payload.answer:
FULL EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN (design-only; nothing was run, no results claimed).

=== TITLE ===
"Do threshold-triggered hostile events (pirate invasions) differentially affect the survival of hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical agents?"

=== 1. RATIONALE ===
The question is not "does the invasion reduce survival" (trivially yes, more difficulty), but whether the *interaction* between a discrete, score-triggered, built-in hostile event and the agent's temporal abstraction hierarchy changes survival. A hierarchical agent plans over longer horizons; a discrete, predictable, high-intensity event may reward anticipation (prepare before the threshold) differently than continuous pressure does. The design therefore centers on the hierarchy × mechanic interaction, with controls separating "the discrete event" from "more total difficulty."

=== 2. ENVIRONMENT (declared assumption) ===
Primary: Minecraft Java Edition (scripted via Malmo/MineDojo-style platform), survival mode.
- Rationale: hostile-event mechanics are genuinely *built-in* (pillager raids are part of vanilla hostile-event design), the trigger must be wired to a score threshold, and Minecraft natively provides a scoreboard system + command blocks/datapacks, so a datapack "scoreboard threshold → spawn invasion wave" is implementable without modifying engine code. This satisfies the researcher's single hard requirement: the mechanic is built-in AND toggleable.
- Toggle: the invasion datapack is enabled/disabled per condition (equivalently, a game-rule-style switch); toggle is verified in a pre-flight check (N=10 smoke episodes per setting confirming events fire only in the ON condition). Caveat stated honestly: exact gamerule/flag names are implementation details to be verified at setup time, not asserted facts here.
- Fallback (if Minecraft scripting proves brittle): an abstract survival simulator (grid/arena with resources, health, hostile entities) with an explicit event module implementing the same trigger rule. Better internal control, weaker external validity — declared as such.
Assumption E1: environment choice is mine, not source-fixed (per researcher clarification). Assumption E2: seedable/deterministic-enough runs.

=== 3. AGENTS (structural definition, per approved approach) ===
- Hierarchical (H): two temporal-abstraction levels. Manager selects options/subgoals every K steps (K=8–16); worker executes primitives. Reference family: options framework or HIRO. Two instantiations to avoid single-architecture artifacts: (H1) fixed-options pre-training + learned manager; (H2) end-to-end hierarchical policy learning.
- Non-hierarchical (F): flat single-level policy, parameter count matched to H within ±10% (counted, not assumed), same network family (CNN/MLP backbone), same observation and action space.
- Match: identical interaction budget, identical replay/rollout sizes, identical total gradient steps. If parameter matching forces architecture adjustments, both adjustments are documented.
- Training protocol (primary design): all four agent-condition-relevant variants trained from scratch, N_seed seeds per architecture, identical hyperparameter sweep budget (small, equal grid), best-on-validation-seeds checkpoint used for evaluation. Learning curves reported to show equal training opportunity.
- Fallback protocol (cheaper): rule-based/fixed policies — H uses a scripted planner over options (e.g., explicit "prepare-for-invasion" subgoal), F uses a reactive scripted policy matched in code complexity. Valid but external validity limited to "hand-designed policies"; declared as such. Pilot runs of this fallback can double as sanity checks for the trained design.

=== 4. CONDITIONS AND CALIBRATION (the requested specification) ===
Design: 2 (hierarchy: H, F) × 3 (event regime) factorial = 6 cells.
Event regimes:
- A. Invasion ON: built-in hostile event triggers when score crosses threshold θ (default: one-shot first crossing per episode; recurrence is a sensitivity axis). Invasion wave: M hostile entities spawned near agent, duration D, damage rate r.
- B. Baseline OFF: no invasion, otherwise identical.
- C. Constant-background-threat (the control, calibrated explicitly): no discrete event; instead a continuous, spatially uniform hostile presence (low-intensity persistent spawns / ambient damage source) calibrated to the invasion on two matched quantities, measured in PILOT runs (N=20 pilot episodes of condition A with a scripted reference agent):
  (i) expected cumulative damage per unit time: λ_C = λ_A (average damage rate over the full episode distribution of A, not a single point estimate; matched on the mean with a tolerance band ±10%);
  (ii) expected total damage per episode: since episodes under A are shorter, C is calibrated against the *counterfactual length distribution* (survival times under B extended to where threshold-crossing would occur), so C matches the total damage an A-episode would have delivered.
  What is deliberately NOT matched: temporal structure. A is bursty and threshold-locked; C is flat. That asymmetry is the point — it isolates "a discrete, anticipatable, threshold-triggered spike" from "the same amount of threat spread evenly." A secondary control C2 (bursty but score-independent, random-timing waves matched to A's intensity profile) separates "discreteness/burstiness" from "threshold contingency." So the full regime set is {A invasion, B off, C constant-matched, C2 bursty-random}, giving a 2×4 grid if compute allows; minimum viable is 2×3 (A, B, C).
- Threshold manipulation: θ ∈ {low, high} as a crossed sensitivity factor, to test whether effects depend on when the invasion arrives relative to the agent's skill trajectory.

=== 5. PROCEDURE ===
Phase 0: implementation + smoke tests (toggle verification, trigger verification, seed-reproducibility check: same seed → same event schedule).
Phase 1: pilots (N=20 scripted-agent episodes per regime) → calibration of C/C2, estimate survival-time variance for power reasoning.
Phase 2: training (if trained-agent track chosen) with equal budgets.
Phase 3: evaluation: per seed, M=50 evaluation episodes, deterministic evaluation protocol (ε=0, fixed spawn layout sampled from a seeded pool), episode truncation at T_max with censoring flag.
Interaction budget: explicit design parameter B_int (episodes×steps per agent). The number "60" seen in my orchestration metadata is NOT adopted as a fact; the design is parameterized, with a recommended minimum and a feasibility note below.

=== 6. METRICS ===
Primary: survival duration in environment steps to death (censored at T_max).
Secondary: time-to-threshold-crossing (mediator), score trajectory (rate of score accumulation — to detect "hierarchy just scores differently"), damage taken before/after crossing (within-episode contrast), for hierarchical agents: option-usage statistics (pre-invasion preparatory option frequency — mechanistic evidence of anticipation).

=== 7. ANALYSIS PLAN ===
- Kaplan–Meier survival curves per cell, log-rank tests pairwise.
- Pre-specified primary test: Cox proportional-hazards model with predictors hierarchy, regime, hierarchy×regime interaction; stratified by seed; survival times from different seeds treated as clustered (robust SEs).
- Mediation: does hierarchy affect survival *through* earlier/later threshold-crossing? Formal mediation decomposition (natural indirect effect via bootstrap).
- Multiple comparisons: Holm correction over the pre-specified interaction contrasts.
- Power reasoning (no runs): with heavily right-skewed/censored survival data, interaction tests need ~4× the sample of main effects; heuristic target: ≥20 seeds × 50 eval episodes per cell for the trained track (≈5,000 episodes/cell), which typically resolves hazard-ratio interactions ≥1.3–1.5 at α=0.05 under CV of survival times typical for survival games; final seed count adjusted after Phase-1 variance estimates. This is argued, not claimed as measured.
- Sensitivity analyses (pre-specified): θ low/high; one-shot vs recurring invasions; invasion intensity multiplier {0.5×, 1×, 2×}; exclusion of early deaths (< some floor) to check the effect isn't just "invasion instantly kills weak agents."

=== 8. FEASIBILITY (qualitative, no compute claimed) ===
- Minecraft track: engineering cost concentrated in the datapack trigger + observation/action plumbing; moderate risk. Fallback simulator: low risk, weaker external validity. Rule-based track: minimal compute; trained track: the dominant cost — bounded by choosing a small map, short T_max, and modest agent sizes; exact figures are design targets, not verified runtimes.
- Everything is executable in principle on CPU-only infrastructure at small scale; larger seed counts would need scaled compute (flagged as the main feasibility risk of the trained track).

=== 9. ASSUMPTIONS (declared) vs FIXED REQUIREMENTS ===
Fixed by researcher: mechanic must be built-in and toggleable; structural definition of hierarchy; KM/Cox + interaction acceptable; sensitivity analysis over trigger mechanics required; explicit calibration spec for the constant-threat control; no execution.
My assumptions (not facts): E1 environment choice (Minecraft primary, abstract fallback); E2 seedability; E3 parameter-count matching suffices for comparability; E4 damage-rate + total-damage matching is a fair operationalization of "equivalent difficulty"; E5 trained-agent track is preferred over rule-based for external validity (rule-based track retained as documented alternative).

=== 10. THREATS TO VALIDITY (honest limits) ===
- If the invasion's difficulty is dominated by total damage rather than temporal structure, conditions A and C converge — that itself is the interpretable finding, not a failure.
- Hierarchical agents may simply train slower; equal-budget matching mitigates but cannot eliminate this (report learning curves).
- Minecraft's own stochasticity (mob spawns, terrain) adds variance; seeded world generation and fixed layout pools mitigate.
- actor_step_budget=60 appears only in my orchestration metadata and is explicitly NOT confirmed by the researcher's brief; it is carried in this design only as an unverified environment note, with the actual interaction budget treated as a design parameter (see §5).

No experiment was run; all numbers above are design targets or reasoned heuristics, none is an outcome.

payload.answer:
DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL FINAL (design-only; ningún experimento fue ejecutado ni se afirma que lo haya sido)

TÍTULO
Efecto del disparo de mecánicas integradas (invasión pirata por umbral de puntuación) sobre la duración de supervivencia de agentes jerárquicos vs. no jerárquicos.

1. PREGUNTA Y RACIONAL
Pregunta: ¿el disparo de una mecánica integrada del juego —invasión pirata activada al alcanzar un umbral de puntuación— afecta las duraciones de supervivencia, y lo hace de forma diferencial según el tipo de agente (jerárquico vs. no jerárquico)?
Racional: las mecánicas integradas suelen introducir perturbaciones contingentes al rendimiento (al puntuar más, se desencadena la invasión). Si los agentes jerárquicos y no jerárquicos difieren en su tasa de puntuación, la mecánica puede afectarlos de manera desigual, y un efecto observado "de la mecánica" podría en realidad estar confundido con la habilidad. Un diseño factorial 2×2 con medición explícita de la frecuencia de disparo permite separar (a) el efecto del tipo de agente, (b) el efecto del disparo de la mecánica y (c) la interacción (¿la invasión penaliza más a un tipo de agente que al otro?).

2. DISEÑO: FACTORIAL 2×2 ALEORIZADO, EPISODIOS INDEPENDIENTES

Factores manipulados:
- Factor A — Estado de la mecánica integrada (invasión pirata):
  • A1 = INVACIÓN ACTIVADA (configuración por defecto del juego).
  • A0 = INVACIÓN DESACTIVADA.
- Factor B — Tipo de agente:
  • B-H = JERÁRQUICO; B-NH = NO JERÁRQUICO.

Celdas resultantes (4): {H, NH} × {mecánica ON, mecánica OFF}.

Unidades y réplicas: cada unidad experimental es un episodio de juego independiente. Se ejecutan N episodios por celda (ver §6 para elección de N), con las mismas semillas usadas en las cuatro celdas (bloques de semillas emparejadas: cada semilla aparece exactamente una vez en cada celda).

Variable de resultado primaria:
- Duración de supervivencia del episodio (DS): número de pasos del entorno hasta la terminación natural del episodio o hasta el límite de censura T_max, lo que ocurra primero. [Elección de diseño: pasos del entorno como unidad, por ser determinista y reproducible; el tiempo de reloj queda como resultado secundario.]

Resultados secundarios (pre-registrados, exploratorios):
- Puntuación máxima alcanzada en el episodio.
- Frecuencia de disparo del umbral: número de veces que se alcanza el umbral de puntuación que activa la invasión por episodio (y en qué paso ocurre por primera vez).
- Causa de terminación (categórica: muerte por invasión / otra muerte / censura por T_max).
- Retorno acumulado.

3. DEFINICIONES OPERATIVAS (ELECCIONES DE DISEÑO, NO HECHOS VERIFICADOS)
- Agente jerárquico [elección de diseño]: agente de política con al menos dos niveles de abstracción: un nivel de alto nivel que selecciona "opciones"/subpolíticas discretas cada k pasos (k ≥ 5), y un nivel de bajo nivel que ejecuta acciones primitivas condicionadas a la opción activa. Ejemplo canónico: arquitectura tipo options/feudal (manager selecciona objetivos; worker ejecuta acciones).
- Agente no jerárquico [elección de diseño]: agente de política plana (reactiva o feedforward) que emite una acción primitiva en cada paso del entorno, con capacidad de parámetros comparable a la del agente jerárquico.
- Duración de supervivencia [elección de diseño]: pasos del entorno hasta terminación, con censura a la derecha en T_max.
- Disparo de la mecánica: evento registrado cuando la puntuación del agente alcanza o supera el umbral U configurado en el juego; en la condición A0, el mismo umbral se registra pero no se dispara ninguna consecuencia (registro "fantasma" para covariables comparables).
- Interruptor de la mecánica [SUPUESTO, no verificado]: se asume que el entorno permite desactivar la invasión mediante un parámetro de configuración (p. ej., flag del tipo "pirate_invasion_enabled = False") sin alterar ninguna otra regla del juego. Este es un supuesto explícito; si el interruptor no existiera, el diseño requeriría una modificación mínima del código de la mecánica, documentada y aplicada por igual en ambas condiciones excepto en el flag.

4. CONTROLES
Controles de diseño (obligatorios):
- C1. Identidad del entorno: misma versión del binario/código del juego en las 4 celdas; única diferencia entre A1 y A0 = estado del flag de la invasión.
- C2. Semillas emparejadas: cada semilla s ∈ S = {s1…sN} se usa una vez por celda; dentro de cada semilla, el estado inicial del entorno es idéntico entre celdas.
- C3. Entrenamiento/evaluación separados: los agentes se entrenan (o se fijan como checkpoints) SIN la mecánica activada, o bien se entrena cada agente en su condición natal y se evalúa en ambas (decisión: ver S7); por defecto, evaluación con políticas congeladas para aislar el efecto en despliegue, no en aprendizaje.
- C4. Capacidad comparable: número de parámetros y presupuesto de cómputo por decisión igualados entre H y NH en lo posible; se documenta cualquier desviación.
- C5. Censura uniforme: T_max idéntico en todas las celdas; los episodios censurados se marcan y se analizan como datos de supervivencia censurados (no se descartan).
- C6. Contrabalanceo del orden de ejecución: las celdas se ejecutan en orden aleatorio por bloques para descartar derivas del entorno (p. ej., caché, calentamiento).
- C7. Registro completo: en cada episodio se registran semilla, celda, DS, puntuación, disparos del umbral, causa de terminación y versión del entorno/agente.

Controles estadísticos:
- C8. Análisis por semillas emparejadas (bloques) para absorber variabilidad entre condiciones iniciales.
- C9. Pre-registro del contraste primario: interacción A×B (ver §5).

5. PLAN DE ANÁLISIS
(a) Estadística principal: modelo lineal mixto (o modelo de supervivencia si hay censura apreciable; ver C5) con DS como respuesta, efectos fijos A, B y A×B, y semilla como efecto aleatorio (bloque). Contraste primario pre-registrado: el coeficiente de interacción A×B — responde directamente la pregunta "¿el disparo de la mecánica afecta diferencialmente a los tipos de agente?".
(b) Efectos simples: efecto de A dentro de cada nivel de B (ON vs. OFF para H; ON vs. OFF para NH), con corrección por comparaciones múltiples.
(c) Manejo de censura: si la proporción de episodios censurados en alguna celda supera ~20%, el análisis primario pasa a un modelo de riesgos proporcionales de Cox con los mismos términos (A, B, A×B) y la semilla como estrato.
(d) ESCENARIO DE RIESGO S5 (confusión con la habilidad) — obligatorio en el plan:
  • Verificación previa de alcanzabilidad: antes del experimento principal, fase piloto que estime, para cada tipo de agente, la probabilidad de alcanzar el umbral U con la mecánica desactivada. Criterio de procedencia: ambos tipos alcanzan el umbral en ≥ una fracción material de episodios (p. ej., ≥30%); si no, se documenta la violación y se ajusta U o se estratifica.
  • Medición como covariable: la frecuencia de disparo del umbral (y la puntuación) se incluyen como covariables en un modelo secundario. Si al ajustar por frecuencia de disparo el efecto de A×B desaparece o se reduce drásticamente, se concluye que el efecto observado está mediado principalmente por la habilidad (puntuación) y no por el tipo de agente per se; este diagnóstico se reporta explícitamente.
  • Análisis de mediación descriptivo (opcional): descomponer el efecto de B en efecto directo y efecto mediado por la tasa de disparo, solo como diagnóstico de confusión, no como confirmación causal fuerte.
  • Si solo un tipo alcanza el umbral: la comparación entre tipos bajo mecánica activada no es interpretable; el informe declarará el resultado como no identificable y presentará únicamente el análisis dentro del tipo que sí dispara la mecánica (efecto simple de A) más el contraste de habilidades en condición OFF.
(e) Robustez: análisis de sensibilidad excluyendo episodios con terminación por causas raras (<5% de frecuencia), y gráficos de supervivencia (Kaplan-Meier) por celda.

6. POTENCIA Y NÚMERO DE RÉPLICAS (razonamiento, no ejecutado)
- Sin estimaciones previas de varianza (no hay datos del entorno), se razona con tamaños de efecto estandarizados: para detectar una interacción A×B de tamaño pequeño-medio (f² ≈ 0.06, equivalente a Δ ≈ 0.25–0.35 desviaciones estándar en la diferencia de diferencias) con potencia 0.80 y α = 0.05 en un ANOVA factorial de efectos fijos con bloqueo por semilla, se requiere del orden de N ≈ 50–70 episodios por celda (≈ 200–280 episodios en total, cuatro celdas). Un efecto grande de la interacción (f² ≈ 0.25) bajaría el requisito a N ≈ 20–25 por celda.
- Recomendación operativa: presupuesto base N = 60 por celda (240 episodios), con regla de escalado: si el piloto (§5d) estima varianzas de DS altas o frecuencias de censura altas, aumentar N proporcionalmente o adoptar el modelo de Cox con más réplicas.
- El bloqueo por semillas mejora la precisión: con correlación intra-semilla moderada (ρ ≈ 0.3), el N efectivo requerido cae aproximadamente un 20–30% respecto al diseño no emparejado; N = 50–60 por celda es una meta razonable.

7. VIABILIDAD (design-only)
- El diseño es ejecutable con cómputo modesto: 240 episodios de evaluación con políticas congeladas es factible en una sola máquina si el entorno es ligero (típico en juegos tipo arcade); el entrenamiento previo de los agentes es el principal coste y queda fuera del experimento si se usan checkpoints.
- No requiere red ni GPU por diseño; es autocontenido y no depende de repositorios específicos: cualquier entorno de juego con (i) puntuación incremental, (ii) umbral U configurable, (iii) interruptor para la invasión y (iv) condición de terminación definida, es adecuado.
- Riesgos de viabilidad identificados: ausencia del interruptor (→ modificación mínima de código, C1), umbral inalcanzable (→ piloto §5d), alta censura (→ Cox, §5c).

8. SUPUESTOS (explícitos; ninguno verificado en los materiales)
- S1. "Agente jerárquico" = política de dos niveles (opciones/subpolíticas) como en §3; "no jerárquico" = política plana. Son elecciones de diseño, no definiciones canónicas de la literatura.
- S2. El entorno permite desactivar la invasión pirata mediante configuración sin alterar otras reglas.
- S3. La DS se mide con la misma regla de terminación en ambas condiciones; la invasión (cuando está activada) puede matar al agente, y ese evento queda registrado como causa de terminación "muerte por invasión" para análisis separado.
- S4. Presupuesto de ejecuciones suficiente: N ≈ 60 por celda es asumible.
- S5. Ambos tipos de agente pueden, en principio, alcanzar el umbral U (verificado empíricamente en el piloto; ver §5d).
- S6. El umbral U es un parámetro conocido y configurable del juego.
- S7. [SUPUESTO ADICIONAL de entrenamiento]: se asume evaluación con políticas congeladas entrenadas sin la mecánica; si el investigador desea capturar adaptación al aprender con la mecánica activada, se requeriría un diseño de entrenamiento factorial adicional, declarado aquí como extensión opcional.

9. INCERTIDUMBRES NO RESOLVIBLES CON LOS DOCUMENTOS DISPONIBLES
- El entorno de juego concreto, su API y la existencia real del interruptor y del umbral configurable (todo lo anterior los trata como supuestos/parámetros).
- La varianza real de DS y la tasa de censura, que afectan el N definitivo (mitigado con piloto + regla de escalado).
- Si los agentes jerárquicos/no jerárquicos de referencia existen como implementaciones disponibles o deben especificarse solo a nivel de diseño (este documento opta por la definición operativa abstracta de §3).
- La forma exacta de la invasión (mortandad, penalización, cambio del entorno) — el diseño la trata como "la consecuencia configurada de disparar U" y registra su causa de terminación sin suponer su magnitud.

RESUMEN DEL ENTREGABLE
Diseño factorial 2×2 (mecánica ON/OFF × agente H/NH), N≈60 episodios por celda con semillas emparejadas y bloqueo, DS en pasos como métrica primaria con censura a T_max, contraste pre-registrado = interacción A×B vía modelo mixto (o Cox si hay censura alta), piloto de alcanzabilidad del umbral + covariable de frecuencia de disparo para desactivar la confusión con la habilidad (S5), controles de identidad de entorno, capacidad comparable, contrabalanceo y registro completo, y todo detalle de entorno etiquetado como supuesto o parámetro, nunca como hecho verificado.

Las incorporaciones exigidas por el investigador están integradas: (1) sin ejecución ni afirmación de experimento realizado; (2) racional (§1), controles (§4), plan de análisis (§5) y viabilidad (§6–7) autocontenidos sin repositorios ni cómputo; (3) detalles no documentados como supuestos (§3, §8); (4) riesgo S5 incorporado como fase piloto de alcanzabilidad + covariable de frecuencia de disparo + rama de análisis no identificable (§5d); (5) definiciones operativas de agente jerárquico, no jerárquico y duración de supervivencia declaradas como elecciones de diseño (§3); (6) razonamiento de potencia con rangos de N por celda (§6).
assumptions: S1: Agente jerárquico = política de dos niveles (opciones/subpolíticas); no jerárquico = política plana con capacidad comparable. Elección de diseño, no definición canónica.
S2: El entorno dispone de un interruptor configurable para desactivar la invasión pirata sin alterar otras reglas.
S3: La duración de supervivencia usa la misma regla de terminación en ambas condiciones; la muerte por invasión se registra como causa de terminación separada.
S4: Presupuesto de ejecuciones de ~240 episodios (60 por celda) es asumible.
S5: Ambos tipos de agente pueden alcanzar el umbral U, verificado en piloto; si no, la comparación entre tipos bajo mecánica activada se declara no identificable.
S6: El umbral U es parámetro conocido y configurable.
S7: Evaluación con políticas congeladas entrenadas sin la mecánica; la adaptación durante aprendizaje con mecánica activada es una extensión opcional.
uncertainties: Identidad del entorno de juego, API, existencia del interruptor y del umbral configurable: no verificables con los documentos; tratados como supuestos/parámetros.
Varianza real de la duración de supervivencia y tasa de censura: afectan el N definitivo; mitigado con piloto y regla de escalado.
Disponibilidad de implementaciones concretas de agentes jerárquicos/no jerárquicos o si basta la especificación abstracta.
Forma exacta y magnitud de la consecuencia de la invasión pirata (muerte, penalización, cambio del entorno).
Magnitud del efecto A×B esperable, que determina si el N recomendado alcanza la potencia objetivo.

payload.answer:
初步检查汇报（设计前探查，未做完整方案设计）：

一、现有材料检查（逐项核实）

实际可确认存在的内容（仅两项）：
1. /workspace/task.json — 工作区唯一的文件。其中包含：
   - 研究问题原文：内置游戏机制（如达到分数阈值触发海盗入侵）是否影响分层与非分层智能体的存活时长；
   - 上下文说明："Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run."（纯设计任务，禁止声称已运行实验）；
   - 一个内嵌的 documents 字段，其中 "track.md" 以字符串形式给出，内容仅一句："Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."（纯设计任务，无需代码仓库与算力）。

实际不可见或缺失的内容：
1. 工作区中并不存在物理的 track.md 文件——其内容仅作为 task.json 中的内嵌字符串出现，且只有这一句。
2. 没有任何环境/模拟器（游戏）的规则描述文档。
3. 没有任何关于"海盗入侵/积分阈值触发"机制的官方说明、API 文档或配置项说明。
4. 没有任何源代码线索：工作区无代码、无仓库、无子目录。
5. 运行环境方面（实测确认）：Python 3.14.4 可用，但 pip 中没有任何 RL/游戏相关库（gym、pettingzoo、smac、starcraft、torch、numpy、stable-baselines 等均未安装）；网络被禁用；GPU 不可用。这与"纯设计、无需算力"的定位一致，但也意味着在本工作区内无法实际验证任何候选模拟器平台的行为。
6. 研究者侧的 topics（可澄清的源支持细节主题列表）当前为空。

二、初步构思的实验大方向（仅为思路）

1. 两类智能体的定义：
   - 分层智能体：采用"管理—执行"结构，例如一个高层策略负责任务分解/子目标选择（如选择进攻、防守、采集、撤退），低层策略执行具体动作；可用 Options 框架、Feudal 网络（FuN/ feudal manager-worker）或简单的 goal-conditioned 两级结构实现。
   - 非分层智能体：单一扁平策略直接从观测映射到动作，参数量与总交互量尽量与分层版本匹配，以控制容量这一混淆变量。
2. 游戏机制作为实验变量：
   - 主因子：机制触发状态，两水平——"开启"（达到分数阈值即触发海盗入侵）与"关闭"（同一环境但禁用该触发）。
   - 可选第二因子：阈值水平（如低/中/高三档阈值），用于检验效应是否随触发频率/时机单调变化——这可作为扩展，非必需。
   - 核心因变量：智能体存活时长（episode 内存活步数/时长）；可加次级指标如最终得分、触发入侵后的即时死亡率。
3. 环境平台思路：需要一个(a)内置该类"得分阈值触发敌袭"机制且(b)机制可开关/可调阈值的游戏环境。候选方向包括：支持海盗/袭击机制的模拟器（如 Minecraft 风格袭击、海盗游戏复刻），或自建一个含该机制的轻量网格/街机环境。具体平台选择需依赖你后续能提供的源支持信息，因为我无法在本工作区验证任何平台。

三、关键假设与不确定点（依赖但未证实）

1. 机制可配置性：假设所选环境中"海盗入侵/阈值触发"可以通过配置项或源码补丁开启、关闭或调整阈值——目前无任何官方说明支持，需你确认。
2. 存活时长定义：假设"存活时长"可从环境中直接读取（如 episode 终止原因=死亡时的步数），且分层与非分层两种智能体使用同一种终止判定；若死亡事件不可直接观测，需定义代理指标。
3. 公平比较前提：假设两类智能体可在相同观测空间、动作空间与随机种子下运行；分层结构的额外开销（决策频率、延迟）是否需要控制未定。
4. 随机性与重复：假设环境含随机性，需固定/扫种子并做多次重复（如每条件≥30 episodes）配统计检验；重复次数与功效分析未确定。
5. 训练 vs 评测：未确定是"训练后评测"（两智能体都在两条件下训练）还是"零样本迁移"（同一策略在机制开/关下评测）——这直接影响设计，需要你澄清。
6. 资源与运行时间限制：本工作区无算力、无依赖、网络禁用，任何实际运行都不可行；设计须假定在别的环境执行，其资源上限（CPU 核数、单实验时长、预算）未知。
7. 未知任务背景：若"海盗入侵/积分阈值"指向某个特定的、研究者已有的模拟器（如某课程的内置实验平台），我目前完全不可见，需要你提供其名称与机制文档线索。

以上均为事实核查与初步思路，未设计完整方案，也未声称运行任何实验。请确认方向与上述待澄清点后，我再进入完整设计。

你的初步检查与思路方向均合格，我同意按此路线进入完整方案设计。以下几点由我现在定夺，请据此完成最终实验设计（含原理、对照、分析计划与可行性说明，仍不得声称已运行实验）：

一、环境平台：本任务为纯设计，不依赖外部仓库，因此不必等待某个特定模拟器的确认。请在方案中选定一个主选环境并写明其机制假设：首选一条自建轻量环境路线（网格/街机式，内置"分数阈值触发海盗入侵"机制，且该机制的开关与阈值为一等配置项），并在可行性一节注明：若执行时存在含同类机制的现成模拟器，可替换，替换条件是机制可配置且终止判定可观测。此选择须明确标注为假设，而非已证实事实。

二、训练与评测协议（我的决定）：采用 2×2 因子设计——架构（分层 vs 非分层）× 机制（开启 vs 关闭）。每格内智能体在与评测相同的条件下以完全相同的训练预算训练至可比水平，主对比为该因子的交互效应（机制触发对两类架构存活时长的影响差异）。跨条件评测（在关闭条件训练、在开启条件评测，及反向）作为次要分析，用于区分"即时冲击"与"适应后差异"，列为扩展项而非必需项。

三、存活时长度量（我的决定）：主指标为因死亡而终止时的环境步数；设固定最大步数上限，未死亡即达上限的回合按删失处理，分析计划中须说明删失的处理方式（如生存分析或上限截断比较），并要求两类智能体使用同一终止判定。

四、机制可配置性：按你的假设处理——设计中假设开关与阈值可经配置项或少量源码修改实现，并在假设清单中如实标注未经验证。

五、重复与统计：每格不少于 30 个随机种子；主分析报告效应量与置信区间（配对或分层比较视设计而定），并包含功效/样本量的说明性核算；阈值水平（低/中/高）仅作为可选扩展因子，不作为必需。

六、公平性控制：两类智能体须匹配参数量与交互预算（决策频率、延迟），使用相同的观测与动作空间和同一套种子；若分层结构引入额外计算开销，须在设计中说明如何度量与控制。

# 最终实验设计：内置机制触发（分数阈值触发海盗入侵）对分层与非分层智能体存活时长的影响

（纯设计交付，未运行任何实验；文中所有标注〔假设〕的数值为量级估算，非实测。）

---

## 1. 研究问题重述

**主问题**：内置游戏机制——"分数达到阈值时触发海盗入侵"——的触发与否，是否对分层（hierarchical）与非分层（non-hierarchical）智能体的存活时长产生不同的影响？

**操作化**：问题被分解为一个交互效应检验。若"机制开启 vs 关闭"对存活时长的效应在两类架构间存在显著差异（即 架构 × 机制 交互显著），则回答为"是"；否则回答为"在此实验设置下未见证据"。

## 2. 环境与机制说明

**主选环境（标注为设计假设，非已证实存在）**：自建轻量网格环境 *PirateGrid*，规格如下：

- 场景：32×32 网格；智能体控制一个单位（船），可在网格中移动、采集资源（得分来源）、躲避/对抗敌方实体。
- 观测：以智能体为中心的局部网格（如 11×11，通道化 one-hot：地形/资源/敌人/自身）+ 标量特征（当前分数、距上次触发的步数、入侵是否激活）。观测空间对两类架构完全一致。
- 动作空间：离散 6 项 {上, 下, 左, 右, 停留, 采集}。对两类架构完全一致。
- 计分：每步采集成功 +1 分；分数持续累计。
- 回合终止：HP 归零（死亡）或达到最大步数上限 L = 10,000 步。
- 随机性：环境内置种子化 RNG，控制资源刷新、敌方巡逻等；同种子完全可复现。

**海盗入侵机制（一等配置项）**：

```
config["pirate_invasion"] = {
    "enabled": bool,        # 开/关总开关
    "threshold": int,       # 分数阈值 T（如 50 / 150 / 300）
    "pirates": int,         # 触发时生成的海盗数量 N（如 3）
    "duration": int,        # 入侵持续步数 W（如 500 步）或至海盗被消灭
}
```

- 触发逻辑：score ≥ T 且机制开启时，在随机位置生成 N 只追踪型海盗实体（移速快于普通敌人、接触即大量伤害）；触发后分数计数重置，可重复触发。
- 机制关闭时：除不生成海盗外，环境其他动力学完全一致（同一套代码路径，仅关闭该事件分支），确保两条件除目标机制外无差异。
- 机制内部参数（N、W、海盗强度）在主实验中固定，不作为因子。

**平台替换条款（可行性说明）**：若执行时存在含同类"得分阈值触发敌袭"机制的现成模拟器，可在满足以下全部条件时替换主选环境：(a) 机制可经配置项或少量源码修改开关并调整阈值；(b) 死亡终止原因可直接观测且可编程读取；(c) 随机种子可控。替换时其余设计不变，仅重估预算（见 §8）。

## 3. 因子设计与条件矩阵

**主设计：2×2 完全因子设计**（依研究者的既定决定）：

| 条件格 | 架构 | 机制 | 标签 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 分层 | 开启 | H-on |
| A2 | 分层 | 关闭 | H-off |
| B1 | 非分层 | 开启 | F-on |
| B2 | 非分层 | 关闭 | F-off |

- 每格 ≥30 个独立随机种子（种子集合跨四格共享：种子 s 同时决定网络初始化与环境的随机流）。
- **主对比**：同条件内训练、同条件内评测（matched-condition training），主检验为 架构 × 机制 交互效应。
- **跨条件评测（扩展项，非必需）**：将 A2/B2 训练的策略在开启条件下评测（train-off→eval-on，度量"即时冲击"），A1/B1 在关闭条件下评测（train-on→eval-off），共 4 条迁移通路。用于区分：机制的影响是"未适应时的即时打击"还是"适应后仍存在的结构性差异"。
- **可选扩展因子（不作为必需）**：阈值水平 T ∈ {低, 中, 高} 三档，仅在该扩展被启用时，在机制开启格内做 3 水平单因子分析（各 ≥30 种子则需 +90 runs；若资源受限可降为每档 10 种子的探索性分析并相应降低结论强度）。

## 4. 智体定义与匹配控制

**非分层（扁平）智能体**：单一 CNN/MLP 策略 π(a|s)，直接从观测输出动作分布；PPO 训练。目标参数量约 2×10^5〔假设的量级，实施时以分层结构定容后回配〕。

**分层智能体**：manager–worker 结构（Options/Feudal 风格）：
- Manager：每 k=10 环境步输出一次子目标（离散子目标集：进攻/采集/撤退/驻守等，embedding 形式注入 worker）；
- Worker：goal-conditioned 策略，每步输出动作；
- 训练：PPO（worker）+ 冻结/慢更新 manager（或 end-to-end PPO over options，二选一并在预注册中固定）。

**匹配控制（依研究者要求）**：
1. **参数量匹配**：分层总参数（manager+worker）与非分层差异 ≤5%，通过调节隐藏层宽度实现；报告确切数字。
2. **交互预算匹配**：两者训练与评测的环境交互步数完全相同（同一套种子、同一回合结构）。
3. **观测/动作空间一致**：同接口封装。
4. **额外计算开销的度量与控制**：分层结构的每步决策包含 manager 调用（每 k 步一次）与目标注入，可能带来更高每步延迟。处理方式：
   - 度量：在评测阶段记录两类智能体的平均每步决策延迟（ms/step）与前向计算量；
   - 控制：主匹配采用"参数量 + 环境交互步数"匹配；同时报告延迟差异，并做**敏感性检验**——若延迟差异 >2 倍，追加一组"给非分层智能体等额前向计算量"（加宽网络至延迟对齐）的小规模对照（每格 10 种子），验证结论对该混淆不敏感；
   - 说明：决策频率差异（每步 vs 每 k 步高层决策）是分层架构的固有属性，属实验操纵的一部分，不视为混淆，但将在讨论中明确。
5. **训练收敛可比性**：训练预算固定（见 §5），绘制学习曲线检查两架构是否达到可比平台期；若某架构明显欠收敛，如实报告并作为局限，不通过追加预算补救（以保持预算严格相等）。

## 5. 训练与评测流程

**训练（matched-condition）**：
- 每个条件格 × 每个种子 = 1 个独立训练 run；共 4 格 × 30 种子 = **120 个训练 runs**（扩展项另计）。
- 训练预算：每个 run 固定 5×10^6 环境步〔假设值，可按资源缩放，四格严格相等〕；PPO 超参（学习率、batch、clip 等）对两架构分别小规模调参后冻结，且调参所用的算力预算对两架构对等。
- 训练条件 = 评测条件（格 A1 在机制开启下训练并在开启下评测，依此类推）。

**评测**：
- 每个训练 run 完成后，冻结策略，评测 100 个回合（专用评测种子集，与训练种子不相交）。
- 记录：每回合的逐步事件日志（分数轨迹、触发时刻、死亡时刻或达到上限、每步延迟）。
- 评测回合数总计：120 runs × 100 = 12,000 回合。
- 跨条件评测（扩展）：复用已训练模型，仅在另一条件下评测，无需重新训练，成本仅为评测时间。

**执行前校验（设计阶段的可行性检查项，非已运行）**：
- 环境冒烟测试：能以固定种子复现同一轨迹（确定性校验）；
- 机制单元测试：构造脚本化策略（恒采集），验证分数达 T 时入侵确实触发、机制关闭时确实不触发、触发时刻与阈值一致；
- 终止一致性测试：两类智能体封装下，死亡事件返回相同的终止信号与步数读数；
- 删失率预估：用随机策略跑少量回合，估计自然达到上限 L 的比例（预期 <20%；若过高则上调 L 并重新固定）。

## 6. 指标与统计分析计划

**主指标**：因死亡而终止时的环境步数（survival time）。达上限 L 而未死亡的回合按**右删失**处理（censored at L）。两类智能体使用同一终止判定与同一上限。

**主分析（预注册式固定）**：
1. **Cox 比例风险模型**：`surv ~ architecture * mechanism + (1 | seed)`，交互项系数即主答案；报告交互项的风险比 HR 及 95% CI（可用分层 bootstrap 按种子聚类，或混合效应 Cox/frailty 模型纳入种子随机效应——两种中预注册其一，建议 frailty Cox）。删失在生存分析框架内自然处理。
2. **Kaplan–Meier 生存曲线**按四格绘制并分层展示，附 log-rank 检验作描述性补充。
3. **效应量与 CI**：交互 HR（主）；辅以存活时间中位数之比及对数存活时间上的 partial η²。
4. **删失稳健性**：另做"上限截断比较"——将删失回合按 L=10,000 计入，做两组对比（ Mann–Whitney/置换检验）作为敏感性分析；若两法结论不一致，如实报告并讨论删失机制（达到上限本身可能反映"更安全策略"，故同时报告删失比例逐格统计）。

**配对/分层比较的选择**：因种子跨格共享，采用按种子分层/聚类推断（frailty Cox 或聚类 bootstrap CI），而非简单配对 t 检验；辅助用混合效应模型对 log(存活步数) 做同构检验（删失回合截断至 L 并标记权重）。

**次级指标**：最终得分；"入侵即时冲击"= 触发后 100 步内的死亡比例（仅机制开启格）；入侵期间的移动/采集行为统计（描述性）。

**功效/样本量说明性核算（计划步骤，非已执行）**：设计阶段规定的方法——以 30 种子/格 × 100 回合/种子 为基准，假设回合级存活时间近似对数正态（删失前），用参数化模拟（在试点数据到手后以试点参数重估）估计：在 α=0.05、power=0.80 下，检出"交互效应使 HR 偏离 1 达 ~1.4"所需种子数；若模拟显示 30 种子不足，则增至 50 种子/格（预算见 §8 留有裕量）。此核算的全部参数为〔假设值〕，执行前须以试点 run 校准。

**多重比较**：主检验仅一个（交互项）；扩展分析（跨条件迁移、阈值档位）若执行，采用 Holm 校正并标注为探索性。

## 7. 假设与局限

**关键假设（均未经验证，如实标注）**：
1. 〔假设〕自建环境的"海盗入侵"机制可通过配置项实现开关与阈值调节；本设计不依赖任何尚未确认的第三方模拟器行为。
2. 〔假设〕死亡终止可观测、可编程读取，且两类智能体使用同一判定逻辑。
3. 〔假设〕该轻量环境能捕捉"突发强敌、阈值因果触发"这类机制的现象学本质；外部效度限于同类机制。
4. 〔假设〕固定 5M 步预算内两架构可达可比水平；分层结构能在此预算内学到有效分层——这本身是经验问题，结果可能部分反映"分层在短预算下学习更慢"而非机制效应本身，分析中将通过学习曲线与交互项的方向性讨论加以区分。
5. 〔假设〕回合级删失比例 <20%；若实测更高，需加长上限并重做功效核算。
6. 〔假设〕§8 中的资源上界为合理量级。

**局限**：单环境结果不能外推至所有游戏机制；若替换为现成模拟器，机制参数（海盗强度、触发频率）不同可能改变效应大小甚至方向；跨条件迁移分析属扩展项，其结论强度受限于非预注册的探索性质。

## 8. 可行性评估

**假设的资源上界（全部为假设值，非实测）**：
- 假设执行环境：约 32–224 CPU 核可用、无 GPU 依赖（小型 CNN/PPO 可纯 CPU）；若实际有单 GPU，训练可进一步加速但非必需。
- 单环境步成本：纯 NumPy 网格模拟约 0.1–0.5 ms/步〔假设〕；PPO 前向/反传使有效吞吐约每 worker 1,000–3,000 步/秒。
- 单训练 run：5M 步，16 环境并行、2 worker 进程，估计墙钟 **0.5–1.5 小时/run**〔假设〕。
- 总训练量：120 runs × ~1 h ≈ **120 CPU-小时量级**；32 路并行下墙钟约 **4–8 小时**量级；保守上界（每 run 8 h、仅 16 路并行）约 **2.5 天墙钟**。
- 评测：12,000 回合 × ≤10,000 步，向量化评测下每 run 评测 <10 分钟〔假设〕，总量可忽略相对训练。
- 存储：每 run 存最终模型 + 评测摘要（不存全轨迹），<100 MB/run，总计 <12 GB；只存摘要可压缩至 <1 GB。
- 若替换为重型现成模拟器（如 StarCraft II 级别），上述预算需按其步时重估（可差 2–3 个数量级），届时应削减训练步数或种子数并降级结论强度；替换条件见 §2。
- 明确声明：工作区当前不具备任何执行条件（无 RL 依赖、网络禁用、纯设计任务），本节所有数字仅为执行规划的上界假设，须在真正执行前以冒烟测试实测校准。

---

**结论性设计要点摘要**：2×2 因子（架构 × 机制）× 30 种子/格、matched-condition 训练与评测、主指标为删失感知的死亡存活时长、主检验为 frailty Cox 交互项（HR + 95% CI）、跨条件迁移与阈值档位为扩展项、参数量与交互预算严格匹配并对分层额外计算开销做延迟记录与敏感性对照。所有机制可配置性与资源数字均标注为假设。

## Step 1 — Workspace inspection (explicit finding)

/workspace contains **only** a `task.json` file restating the research question ("Does the triggering of built-in game mechanics, such as pirate invasions when the score threshold is reached, affect the survival durations of hierarchical versus non-hierarchical agents?"). There is **no track.md file on disk** (it is referenced only inside task.json's `documents` field, stating: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"), no game environment, no agent framework code, no dependencies, and no datasets. So the game environment (e.g., a pirate/invasion-themed simulation) and the agent implementations (hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical) exist only as described in the question — they are not available for inspection. I therefore cannot verify any engine internals from source.

## Step 2 — Proposed high-level approach

**Game scenario.** A single-agent survival game containing at least one built-in, score-triggered mechanic — canonical example: a pirate invasion that automatically launches once the agent's cumulative score crosses a fixed threshold (e.g., score ≥ N). The game runs per-episode; the episode ends when the agent "dies" (survival duration = wall-clock or game-tick count from episode start to termination).

**Agent types.**
- *Hierarchical agents*: an agent with an explicit layered policy (e.g., a high-level controller selecting sub-goals/options, and low-level controllers executing primitive actions). If a reference implementation exists in the researcher's codebase, use it; otherwise the design assumes a standard options/HRL-style architecture (e.g., manager/worker).
- *Non-hierarchical agents*: a flat policy agent matched in parameter count and training compute to the hierarchical agent (e.g., a flat policy-value network with the same total parameters and same training step budget).

Both agent types are obtained from the same training pipeline, differing only in architecture/hierarchy.

**Mechanic toggling.** A 2×2 design: {agent type: hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical} × {mechanic state: ON vs. OFF}.
- ON condition: pirate invasion triggers exactly when score ≥ threshold T (default game behavior).
- OFF condition: the invasion trigger is disabled (event never fires) via a game configuration flag — while the underlying score-reward structure is left identical so agents' score dynamics are comparable. If disabling entirely is not possible, alternative is holding the trigger at an effectively unreachable threshold (documented as a fallback).
- Triggering is fully deterministic: fixed threshold T, deterministic trigger evaluation each tick.

**Primary outcome.** Survival duration per episode — defined as the number of game ticks (or normalized in-game time) from episode start until agent death, recorded identically in all four conditions. Secondary (exploratory) measures: final score, time-to-first-invasion, deaths-caused-by-invasion vs. other causes.

## Step 3 — Key controls and analysis sketch

**Controls:**
- Fixed random seeds per replicate for environment generation, agent initialization, and any stochastic policies (matched seed sets across conditions).
- Matched difficulty: identical map/level parameters, enemy spawn rates, scoring rules, and episode time caps in all conditions; only the invasion trigger differs between ON/OFF.
- Matched agents: same training algorithm, compute, and hyperparameter tuning effort; agent checkpoints evaluated identically (same evaluation protocol, ε-greedy or deterministic evaluation policy specified).
- Deterministic trigger: threshold T fixed a priori and never adaptively changed; trigger timing logged and verified.
- Version pinning: game engine and agent code versions pinned; all episodes run on the same binary/build.

**Analysis sketch:**
- Replicates: ≥ n independent training seeds per agent type (e.g., n ≥ 5), and k ≥ 30 evaluation episodes per seed per condition (more if survival duration variance is high).
- Primary comparison: two-way design — effect of agent type, effect of mechanic ON/OFF, and crucially the **interaction** (does invasion affect hierarchical agents differently than flat agents?). Model: linear mixed-effects regression on log(survival duration) with fixed effects for agent type, mechanic state, and their interaction; random intercepts for training seed; episodes nested within seed.
- Pre-specified primary test: the interaction term (Wald test / likelihood-ratio test), with Holm correction if multiple secondary comparisons are made. Report effect sizes (difference in mean log-survival with CIs), not just p-values. Check distributional assumptions; fall back to rank-based (ART-ANOVA or permutation test on the interaction) if residuals are non-normal.

## Step 4 — Consequential assumptions and uncertainties (explicit)

**Assumptions (must hold for this design):**
1. The game engine exposes a configuration mechanism to disable or modify the invasion trigger (e.g., a flag or config value). If not, source modification is needed.
2. Survival duration is well-defined and machine-recordable per episode (tick count to death).
3. Both hierarchical and non-hierarchical agent implementations are available (or can be trained) under matched budgets; hierarchy is the only architectural difference.
4. The score-reward structure is unaffected by toggling the mechanic, so ON/OFF differences isolate the mechanic's effect on survival, not on reward shape.
5. Design-only: no repository or compute work required, and no experiment will be executed or claimed as run (per track.md).

**Uncertainties I cannot confirm (researcher must supply details if they matter):**
1. The actual identity of the game/simulation — "pirate invasions" and the score threshold mechanic are taken from the question; I have no source to verify how the trigger works, whether it can fire multiple times per episode, or whether it can be cleanly disabled.
2. What hierarchical agent implementations exist (specific framework — e.g., options, feudal, custom manager/worker) and whether pre-trained checkpoints exist vs. training from scratch.
3. Runtime budget: number of seeds/episodes feasible; the n=5 seeds × 30 episodes sketch is a placeholder pending budget guidance.
4. Whether survival duration should be measured in game ticks or wall-clock, and whether episodes have a maximum length cap (censoring implications).
5. Whether the threshold T should be fixed across agents or scaled to each agent's typical score trajectory (this choice changes interpretation; default plan fixes it).

No experiment has been run and none will be claimed; this is a proposal for your review before the full design document.

payload.answer:
# Experiment Design Document (Design-Only)

**Research question:** Does the triggering of built-in game mechanics, such as pirate invasions when the score threshold is reached, affect the survival durations of hierarchical versus non-hierarchical agents?

**Status:** Design only. No repository or compute work is required and no experiment has been run, executed, or claimed (per track.md). Workspace inspection confirmed /workspace contains only task.json restating the question; the game engine and agent implementations are therefore treated as specified-but-unverified, and every claim about them below is a design assumption, not a verified fact.

---

## 1. Rationale: linking the 2×2 interaction to the question

The question is not simply "do invasions reduce survival?" nor "do hierarchical agents survive longer?" — it asks whether the mechanic's effect **differs between agent types**. That is precisely an interaction effect, and it demands a factorial design rather than two separate experiments:

- Two one-at-a-time studies cannot estimate how the mechanic effect *changes across agent types*, because the mechanic's effect is always measured within one agent type.
- A 2×2 factorial — **Agent Type** (hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical) × **Mechanic State** (invasion trigger ON vs. OFF) — yields three estimable effects:
  1. **Main effect of agent type:** baseline survival difference between architectures (nuisance for this question, but required as context).
  2. **Main effect of mechanic:** average survival change when invasions can fire, pooled over agent types.
  3. **Interaction (primary):** whether the mechanic's effect on survival differs for hierarchical vs. non-hierarchical agents. This term *is* the answer to the research question.

**Directional rationale (to motivate, not to presuppose the result):** a hierarchical agent's high-level controller may re-plan in response to a sudden discrete event like an invasion (e.g., switching from score-accumulation sub-goals to threat-avoidance sub-goals), whereas a flat reactive policy may only adapt through low-level state features. If so, the invasion would penalize flat agents' survival more than hierarchical agents' — a positive interaction in this parameterization. The design remains two-sided: it detects differences in either direction.

**Why survival duration as the outcome:** it is the native termination criterion of a survival-style episode, is directly interpretable, and is the quantity the question names. Score is treated as a secondary measure because toggling the mechanic may legitimately change achievable score; making score primary would confound "the mechanic changed scoring opportunities" with "the mechanic changed survival."

## 2. Operational definitions

### 2.1 Agent types
- **Hierarchical agent:** an agent with an explicit two-level control structure: a *high-level controller* that selects temporally extended sub-goals/options (e.g., every k primitive steps or upon option termination), and *low-level controller(s)* that map sub-goals plus observations to primitive actions. Instantiation (options framework, manager/worker feudal style, or equivalent) is assumed to come from the researcher's agent framework; the design requires only that (a) the hierarchy is architecturally explicit and (b) it is the **sole** architectural difference from the comparator.
- **Non-hierarchical (flat) agent:** a single-level policy mapping observations directly to primitive actions, **matched** to the hierarchical agent in (i) total trainable parameters (±5%), (ii) observation and action interfaces, (iii) learning algorithm family and hyperparameter tuning budget, and (iv) total training compute (environment steps). Parameter matching prevents the interaction from being an artifact of capacity rather than hierarchy.
- Both types are trained from scratch per seed under identical protocols (or, if pre-trained checkpoints are supplied, from identically-constructed checkpoints — this is an assumption to be resolved at implementation time, not asserted).

### 2.2 Mechanic state (invasion trigger)
- **ON (default game behavior):** when the agent's cumulative episode score reaches a fixed threshold **T**, the built-in pirate invasion event fires deterministically. T is **fixed a priori, globally, across both agent types and all seeds** (per researcher resolution (1); scaling T per agent is documented below as a sensitivity analysis only, because adaptive thresholds would confound mechanic intensity with agent skill).
- **OFF:** the invasion event never fires. **Primary mechanism:** a game-configuration flag disabling the event, leaving the score function, all other mechanics, and the environment otherwise byte-identical. **Documented contingency (unverified):** if no such flag exists, set T to a value unreachable given the episode time cap and maximum attainable score rate, estimated conservatively (≥ 1.5× the highest score observed in any pilot/expected trajectory) — this holds the trigger effectively inert but is weaker (it relies on score-rate estimates) and would be reported as a deviation. **Neither mechanism is claimed verified**; confirming the disable mechanism is an implementation-time prerequisite (feasibility item F1).
- The trigger's evaluation is deterministic: checked at fixed tick boundaries against the exact threshold; trigger firings are logged per episode with tick and score.

### 2.3 Survival duration (primary outcome)
- **Definition:** number of environment **game ticks** from episode start to episode termination by agent death (per researcher resolution (2); not wall-clock, which conflates engine speed and load with gameplay).
- **Censoring:** if the environment imposes a maximum episode length cap L, episodes reaching L without death are **right-censored at L**. Two-part handling: (a) set L high enough (≥ 3× the longest survival observed in pilot/expected play) that censoring is rare (< 5% of episodes), verified in the feasibility check; (b) the primary model accommodates censoring regardless (Section 5.4). If no cap exists, no censoring arises.
- Secondary/exploratory outcomes: final episode score; tick of first invasion (ON condition); cause-of-death attribution (invasion-related vs. other), if engine logging supports it.

## 3. Experimental conditions and structure

Four cells, all evaluated on the identical environment build and evaluation protocol:

| | Mechanic ON | Mechanic OFF |
|---|---|---|
| **Hierarchical** | H-ON | H-OFF |
| **Non-hierarchical** | N-ON | N-OFF |

**Design point (recommended, per resolution (3)):** ≥ 5 independent training seeds per agent type × ≥ 30 evaluation episodes per seed per mechanic condition → ≥ 300 evaluation episodes per cell, ≥ 1,200 total. This budget is assumed to scale linearly (double seeds and/or episodes doubles compute); the qualitative feasibility assessment in Section 6 describes the compute shape without any executed run. Seeds are matched across agent types (seed s of each type uses identical environment seeds and evaluation seeds), enabling paired-seed comparisons.

**Training and evaluation separation:** each agent type is trained once per seed; each trained agent is then evaluated in **both** mechanic conditions (ON and OFF) with the same evaluation-episode seeds. This within-agent crossing of the mechanic factor reduces between-condition variance and strengthens the interaction estimate. Evaluation policy is deterministic (greedy) or fixed-ε, identical across conditions.

## 4. Controls

1. **Fixed seeds, matched across cells:** per replicate r, environment-generation seeds, agent-initialization seeds, and evaluation-episode seeds are identical across the relevant comparisons (same env seeds for H-ON/H-OFF; identical seed sets across H and N within each mechanic condition). Deterministic engine settings where available; nondeterminism that cannot be removed is treated as within-cell noise and reported.
2. **Matched difficulty:** identical level/map parameters, enemy spawn rates, scoring rules, reward function, time cap L, and all other built-in mechanics across all four cells. The **only** manipulated difference between ON and OFF is the invasion trigger; the only difference between H and N is the architecture (Section 2.1 matching).
3. **Deterministic triggering:** T fixed a priori, evaluated each tick, never adaptive, never changed after data collection begins; trigger state and firing log verified post hoc for every episode (ON episodes: firings recorded at expected scores; OFF episodes: zero firings).
4. **Reward-structure invariance:** the score function and reward signal are identical across ON/OFF so that the toggle isolates the mechanic's survival effect rather than altering what agents optimize. (If the engine ties invasion events to reward — unknown — this must be handled at implementation time and disclosed; see Limitations.)
5. **Matched training compute and tuning:** same algorithm family, tuning budget, and total environment steps for both agent types; no per-type advantage in tuning effort.
6. **Version pinning:** single pinned build of the game engine and agent framework for all cells; same hardware class if executed.
7. **Blinding/order effects:** evaluation condition order randomized per seed; outcome extraction automated to avoid analyst drift.
8. **Verification pass:** a small smoke check (few episodes per cell) confirms (i) OFF yields zero invasion events, (ii) ON yields firings at score ≥ T, (iii) logging captures tick-level survival and censoring flags — before any full data collection.

## 5. Analysis plan

### 5.1 Primary analysis
Two-way model on survival duration with fixed effects for **agent type**, **mechanic state**, and their **interaction**:

log(S) = β₀ + β_A·AgentType + β_M·Mechanic + β_AM·(AgentType × Mechanic) + random intercept for training seed + ε.

- **Primary test:** H₀: β_AM = 0 (no difference in mechanic effect across agent types) vs. two-sided alternative, via a likelihood-ratio test comparing the model with and without the interaction. This single pre-specified test answers the research question; no correction is needed for it alone.
- **Effect size:** report β_AM with 95% CI, back-transformed as a ratio-of-ratios (the mechanic's multiplicative effect on survival for hierarchical agents divided by that for flat agents).
- Seed random intercepts respect the paired structure; episodes are nested within seed (cluster-robust or mixed-model inference; observations within a seed are not treated as independent).

### 5.2 Diagnostics
Residual Q–Q plots and scale–location plots per cell; influence diagnostics (Cook's distance) at seed and episode level; variance-ratio check across cells (survival durations are typically right-skewed — the log transform is pre-specified for this reason). If diagnostics fail persistently: pre-specified fallback is a rank-based factorial test (aligned-rank transform ANOVA) or a permutation test on the interaction coefficient, using seed-level clustering (permutation across seeds).

### 5.3 Secondary and exploratory analyses
- Main effects of agent type and mechanic (descriptive with CIs; not the confirmatory target).
- Final score: same factorial model on log(score+1), flagged exploratory because the mechanic may legitimately alter score opportunities.
- Cause-of-death decomposition (ON condition): proportion of deaths attributable to invasion-related causes by agent type — mechanistic follow-up if the primary interaction is significant.
- Time-to-first-invasion distribution in ON cells, to confirm triggering behaved as specified.

### 5.4 Censoring handling
- If censored episodes are rare (< 5%, verified during feasibility/pilot per Section 4.8), the log-normal mixed model is fit with right-censoring at L (e.g., via survival-model formulation — accelerated failure-time model with log-normal distribution and seed as a frailty/cluster term — which is the natural censored analogue of the primary model and is the pre-specified primary model whenever any censoring occurs).
- Sensitivity: re-run the analysis excluding censored episodes; if conclusions change, report both and flag the cap as a limitation.
- Per resolution (2): the design prefers setting L high enough that censoring is rare **and** a model that accommodates censoring — both, not either-or.

### 5.5 Sensitivity note (threshold scaling)
As directed: a sensitivity analysis repeating the primary comparison with a per-agent scaled threshold T′ = κ × (agent-type-specific median score trajectory) is described as optional follow-up only. It is **not** part of the confirmatory design because it confounds mechanic intensity with agent skill.

## 6. Feasibility assessment

Qualitative only — no run is executed or claimed.

- **Compute shape:** cost ≈ (#agent types × #seeds × training steps) for training + (#cells × #seeds × #episodes × mean episode length) for evaluation. Training dominates; evaluation is one episode set per trained agent per condition. The recommended design point (5 seeds × 30 episodes) is stated as scalable linearly; halving seeds to 3 with ≥ 50 episodes per seed preserves episode count at the cost of seed-level (between-replicate) power, which is typically the binding constraint for interaction tests — hence the 5-seed recommendation.
- **Prerequisite verifications (F-items) before any future execution:** (F1) existence of the disable mechanism (config flag or unreachable-threshold contingency, both unverified); (F2) availability/matchability of the two agent implementations under matched budgets; (F3) tick-level survival logging and cause-of-death attribution exist in the engine; (F4) pilot establishes score trajectories to fix T a priori and to size L (censoring < 5%); (F5) episode-duration variance estimate to confirm ≥ 30 episodes/seed gives adequate precision.
- **Assumptions (design-level, stated as such):** A1 — the engine supports ON/OFF toggling of the invasion without altering the reward/score structure (primary: config flag; fallback: unreachable threshold, unverified). A2 — survival duration is machine-recordable in ticks with an identifiable death event. A3 — hierarchical and non-hierarchical agents can be instantiated and matched as in 2.1. A4 — training-from-scratch per seed is the acquisition route (or identically constructed checkpoints). A5 — the recommended replicate budget is feasible and scales linearly.
- **Limitations:** (L1) the mechanic is a single event type at a single threshold; findings may not generalize to other built-in mechanics, thresholds, or firing schedules. (L2) If the engine couples invasion events to reward, the ON/OFF contrast includes that coupling — disclosed if discovered. (L3) Results are conditional on the specific agent framework and hyperparameter regime; the interaction may vary across HRL variants. (L4) Unreachable-threshold contingency relies on score-rate estimates and would be a documented deviation. (L5) Cause-of-death attribution is only as good as engine logging. (L6) Design-only scope: no numbers in this document are measured; all magnitudes (e.g., "≥ 1.5× score," "< 5% censoring") are pre-specifications to be validated by the F-item checks.

## 7. Deliverable summary

The design answers the question through a single pre-specified interaction test (β_AM) in a 2×2 factorial (agent type × mechanic ON/OFF), with survival duration in game ticks as the outcome, a log-normal mixed/censored model with seed random effects, fixed a-priori threshold T, matched seeds/agents/difficulty across cells, deterministic trigger verification, secondary and sensitivity analyses pre-specified, and feasibility framed as qualitative with explicit unverified prerequisites. Nothing has been executed, and no experimental outcome is claimed.

Do not claim that an experiment was run," and cites track.md text "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required" — track.md itself is not present on disk. No game engine, agent framework, dependencies, or datasets exist in the workspace (system Python, network disabled, no GPU), so all environment- and agent-specific details in the design are labeled as assumptions (A1–A5) or unverified prerequisites (F1–F5), not verified facts. ### 2. Proposed approach sketch (not the full solution)
**Core design — paired bidirectional retrieval probe:**
- Build a curated set of celebrity parent-child pairs (N ≈ 100–200, e.g., child→parent and parent→child as two query directions over the *same* pairs, so accuracy is directly comparable within-pair).
- Two symmetric prompt conditions per pair:
  - **Forward (child→parent):** "Who is the parent of [celebrity child]?" (one or all parents).
  - **Reverse (parent→child):** "Name the child(ren) of [celebrity parent]." (score a hit if any/each true child is named; cap by listing behavior).
- Score with exact/fuzzy name matching plus alias handling; measure accuracy, and also "hallucination/false-child" rate in the reverse direction (plausibly the mechanism behind the asymmetry — many children per parent makes the reverse query under-determined).
- **Confound control this design must address:** the reverse direction is inherently harder (a famous parent often has multiple children, some less famous). Mitigations: (a) restrict to parents with exactly one well-known child, or (b) analyze per-child recall conditional on parent, or (c) include a "fame-matched" control where both endpoints have comparable notability. Also include a bidirectionality baseline: pairs where the child is *more* famous than the parent vs. parent more famous than the child, to disentangle fame-asymmetry from relational-direction asymmetry.

**Dataset source proposal (in order of preference):**
- A preexisting structured KG dump: **Wikidata SPARQL extracts** (property P40 "child") filtered to people with notability signals, or a derived dataset like a subset of **CELEBRITY/family-relation benchmarks** used in prior LLM fact-recall work (e.g., Relation Extraction/relation-probing sets such as those in "Language Models as Fact Checkers" style benchmarks). Curate + hand-verify a gold subset manually (design assumes manual verification effort).
- Fallback: hand-curated list from Wikipedia infoboxes for ~150–200 families, verified by the researcher.

**LLMs/conditions:**
- 2–3 models spanning capability tiers (e.g., a small open model, a mid-tier, and a frontier API model) — exact model choice is the researcher's call and an open assumption.
- Conditions: direct zero-shot QA; optionally a "name the person, not the profession" constrained-output variant; temperature 0; one prompt template per direction, order counterbalanced.

### 3. Key assumptions vs. uncertainties
**Assumptions I'm treating as working assumptions (flagged, not confirmed):**
- A verified celebrity parent-child dataset can be assembled from Wikidata/Wikipedia with high ground-truth confidence; disputed relations (e.g., contested paternity, step/adoption) would be excluded or tagged.
- Prompt wording can be made symmetric enough that direction is the only manipulated variable.
- Statistical plan: paired test (McNemar or bootstrap on per-pair accuracy differences) with the pair as its own control.

**Uncertainties I cannot resolve from materials at hand:**
- **Model access:** no API keys, no local weights, network disabled — which models will actually be available when/if the experiment is authorized is unknown.
- **Ground-truth ambiguity:** how to score half-siblings, adopted/stepchildren, multiple children, and parents with many famous children (needs your ruling).

payload.answer:
# FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — Directional Bias in LLM Retrieval of Celebrity Parent-Child Relations

**Status: DESIGN ONLY.** Per track.md (embedded in task.json: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"), nothing has been executed, no results are claimed, and all model access/keys are execution-phase dependencies, not design assumptions.

---

## 1. Motivation and Hypothesis

**Hypothesis (H1):** For real-world factual data on celebrity parent-child relationships, LLMs will exhibit directional bias: accurate retrieval of a *parent* when given a *child's* name, but weaker retrieval of a *child* when given a *parent's* name.

**Why this is plausible and worth testing:** In training corpora, a famous child's biography almost always names their parent explicitly ("child of X"), whereas a famous parent's biography often enumerates children inconsistently, partially, or not at all. Additionally, the reverse query is *structurally under-determined*: a parent typically has 0–N children while a child has ≤2 documented parents, so the model faces both an information-density asymmetry and a one-to-many output problem. H1 predicts retrieval accuracy differs by query direction on the *same* relation fact.

**Mechanisms the design separates:**
- (M1) **Relational-direction bias** — the same fact is easier to retrieve in one direction than the other (core H1 claim).
- (M2) **Fame asymmetry** — one endpoint is simply more famous, so the query names a more (or less) familiar entity regardless of direction. This is a confound, controlled by stratification (§5).
- (M3) **Under-determined reverse query / set-size effect** — parents with many children dilute per-child recall. This is controlled by the primary single-child subset and analyzed secondarily in the all-pairs strata (§5, §7).

## 2. Dataset: Pair Selection and Verification

**Source (stated as proposed source; availability is an execution-phase dependency):** Wikidata SPARQL extract using property **P40 (child)** restricted to humans with a notability signal (≥ 10 Wikipedia sitelinks, or English Wikipedia pageviews above a threshold). Each candidate relation is then cross-checked against the English Wikipedia infobox/biography of *both* endpoints. Fallback source if Wikidata extraction is unavailable: hand-curated list from Wikipedia infoboxes for ~200 families, verified manually by the researcher.

**Inclusion rules (fixed requirements):**
1. **Relations eligible:** biological *and* legal (adoptive) parent-child relations, **only if unambiguously documented in the gold source** (both endpoints' Wikipedia pages agree, or Wikidata P40/P25/P26-adjacent properties are consistent and cited).
2. **Step- and half-relations:** each candidate step/half relation is **tagged `step`/`half` and excluded from the primary scored set** — never silently scored as hit or miss. A tagged side-file is retained so a sensitivity analysis could be specified later, but it is not part of the headline estimate.
3. **Disputed/contested relations** (contested paternity, litigated parentage, unreliable tabloid-only sourcing) go to an **exclusion list documented in the deliverable** (pair ID, endpoints, reason for exclusion). Exclusions are reported as a count alongside N.
4. **De-duplication:** one record per (parent, child) dyad; families with multiple scored children appear in the secondary analysis only.

**Subset structure:**
- **Primary (S1): single-well-known-child pairs** — parent has exactly one child that meets the notability threshold (other children, if any, are either non-notable or the pair is assigned to S2). Target **N ≥ 150 verified pairs**.
- **Secondary (S2): all-pairs** — every verified pair, including multi-child parents; analyzed **stratified by number of scored children per parent (1, 2–3, 4+)** and reported separately. **S1 and S2 are never pooled into a single headline estimate.**

**Verification procedure:** each pair requires (a) a citation from the child's page naming the parent AND (b) a citation from the parent's page listing the child, or a single authoritative source (e.g., an encyclopedia/obituary) covering both. Pairs failing dual-source check are excluded with a logged reason. Gold answers store canonical names plus an alias list (stage names, transliterations, nicknames) harvested from Wikidata aliases.

**Fame proxy per endpoint (explicitly a proxy, not a claim of measurement validity):** English Wikipedia 90-day pageviews at curation time, with Wikidata sitelink count as fallback. Each endpoint is labeled `higher-fame` / `lower-fame` within the pair.

## 3. Prompt Templates (one per direction, otherwise identical)

Both templates use the same framing, instructions, and output format; only the queried role changes. Fixed maximum output length (e.g., 100 tokens), temperature 0, single turn, no system prompt beyond a neutral instruction block. Template order of presentation in the run manifest is counterbalanced (half of run A starts forward, half starts reverse) to guard against any position/sequence artifact in the logging — though with independent single-turn calls this is a procedural safeguard, not a manipulable context.

**Forward (child→parent), template F:**
> "Question: Who is the parent of {child_name}?
> Answer with the parent's name only. If you are not sure, say 'Unknown'."

**Reverse (parent→child), template R:**
> "Question: Name the child(ren) of {parent_name}.
> List each child's name on its own line. If you are not sure, say 'Unknown'. For each line, state only a child's name."

Both directions also accept the parent variant where the model may correctly answer with two parents; for the forward direction, a hit is scored if *any* named parent matches the gold parent in the pair (scoring detail in §4). "Unknown"/abstention is recorded as an explicit response category, scored as a miss but reported separately so misses can be decomposed into wrong-answer vs. abstention.

## 4. Scoring Rubric (fixed requirements)

**Matching:** alias-aware fuzzy matching — canonical name, stage names, transliterations, and Wikidata alias lists all count as correct. Normalization: case-fold, strip diacritics/particles, token-set overlap with a normalized Levenshtein/token-Jaccard threshold (e.g., ≥ 0.85) plus a manual adjudication pass on all borderline matches (borderline cases logged, adjudication rule fixed in advance: match if the entity is unambiguously the gold person).

**Forward direction (child→parent):** binary per query — correct if any named parent matches the gold parent for that pair. Report accuracy, plus decomposition into correct / wrong-name / abstention.

**Reverse direction (parent→child): scored per-child recall** as ruled: if the parent has N true scored children and the response names k of them, per-child recall = k/N (a parent naming one of three children yields 1/3). **Additionally report a separate false-child (hallucination) rate:** count of named entities that are NOT any true child, normalized per response (false named children / total named children), so over-generation is visible independently of recall. **Both metrics are reported; neither replaces the other.** In S1 (single-child), per-child recall reduces to a binary hit/miss, making S1 directly symmetric with the forward direction — this is why S1 is the headline.

**Partial credit policy:** strictly per the rule above — binary per query in the forward direction, fractional per-child recall in the reverse. No other partial credit.

**Tagged relations:** step/half and disputed pairs are excluded before scoring (never counted as hits or misses silently).

## 5. Controls

**C1 — Pair-as-own-control (core):** every pair is queried in both directions; the unit of analysis is the within-pair accuracy difference d = acc(forward) − acc(reverse-recall). This cancels pair-level difficulty (how famous the pair is at all).

**C2 — Single-well-known-child subset (S1):** removes the one-to-many set-size confound (M3); headline result computed here only.

**C3 — Fame-asymmetry stratification:** each pair labeled by which endpoint is more famous (Wikipedia pageviews proxy). Report direction-of-retrieval accuracy **within each stratum**:
- Stratum A: child more famous than parent (confound M2 favors the *reverse* query — the named entity in the query is the famous one in both directions... precisely: in stratum A the forward query conditions on a famous child and asks for a less-famous parent; the reverse conditions on a less-famous parent).
- Stratum B: parent more famous than child (mirror image).
If H1 (M1) is real, forward > reverse should hold *within both strata*; if the apparent effect is pure fame asymmetry (M2), the sign should flip or vanish across strata. This contrast is the design's key identification device.

**C4 — Set-size stratification (secondary, S2):** per-child recall by number of scored children (1, 2–3, 4+) quantifies M3 directly.

**C5 — Counterbalancing/procedural:** one template per direction, identical formatting, temperature 0, fixed max output length, response-order counterbalanced in the run manifest, all prompts and outputs logged verbatim for audit.

## 6. Models and Conditions

**Candidate models (2–3 spanning capability tiers), with substitution rule:** e.g.,
- Tier 1 (small/open): e.g., a 7–8B open-weight instruction model;
- Tier 2 (mid): e.g., a mid-tier commercial or ~70B open model;
- Tier 3 (frontier): e.g., a frontier API model.
**Substitution rule (ruled):** any model of an equivalent tier is acceptable at execution time; the design fixes *tiers*, not vendor products. Model choice and access/keys are **execution-phase dependencies**.

**Conditions:** 1 prompt template per direction × {S1, S2} × 2–3 models; temperature 0; 1 sample per cell in the base run (deterministic decoding); optional 3-sample repetition at temperature 0.7 as a robustness check only if execution resources allow.

## 7. Statistical Analysis Plan

- **Primary test (S1):** paired comparison of forward vs. reverse accuracy on the same N ≥ 150 pairs — **McNemar's test** on the discordant pairs (forward-correct/reverse-wrong vs. forward-wrong/reverse-correct), α = 0.05, two-sided; effect size reported as the within-pair difference and its bootstrap 95% CI (e.g., 10,000 resamples, percentile CI).
- **Power rationale (stated without claiming a computation has been run):** with a paired binary design, the McNemar test's power depends on the discordant-pair proportion; a target of N ≥ 150 is chosen so that a within-pair difference of roughly 15–20 percentage points with a moderate discordance rate is detectable at α = 0.05 with power ≈ 0.80. The exact power figure must be recomputed once pilot discordance rates exist — this is an execution-phase calculation, not asserted here.
- **Secondary analyses:** (a) S2 per-child recall by direction within set-size strata; (b) fame-stratum analysis (C3) — direction effect within stratum A and within stratum B, with the sign-consistency check described in §5; (c) false-child rate by model and direction; (d) abstention rates by direction (tests whether the asymmetry manifests as confident errors vs. hedging).
- **Multiple comparisons:** primary test is single and pre-registered as headline; secondary analyses reported with nominal CIs and labeled exploratory.
- **Model-level reporting:** direction effect estimated per model; H1 is about LLMs generally, so report consistency across models (e.g., sign of the effect in all tiers) rather than pooling models into one estimate.

## 8. Confound Discussion (explicit)

| Confound | Mechanism | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Fame asymmetry (M2) | One endpoint more famous → retrieval asymmetry independent of relation direction | C3 stratification; within-stratum sign-consistency test |
| One-to-many reverse query (M3) | Parent has N children; per-child recall diluted | C2 single-child subset (primary); C4 set-size strata (secondary) |
| Name-ambiguity asymmetry | Common surnames/names cause false matches | Alias-aware matching + manual adjudication; wrong-name vs. abstention decomposition |
| Temporal drift / post-training-cutoff events (deaths, new children) | Ground truth changes after training data | Curate pairs stable over the past decade; exclude recent or changing relations; note cutoff date of each model as metadata |
| Prompt-format asymmetry | Templates differ subtly in difficulty | Identical templates differing only in role; fixed max length; single format |
| Scoring-asymmetry artifacts | Reverse inherently scored fractionally | Headline analysis on S1 where both directions are binary |
| Cross-sibling leakage | Model lists another pair's child | Per-child scoring handles this naturally; false-child rate quantifies it |

## 9. Feasibility and Execution-Phase Dependencies

**Design-only constraint honored:** no code has been run, no data extracted, no model called, and no numbers in this document are measurements.

**If authorized for execution, the design assumes (execution-phase dependencies, not design assumptions):**
- API or local inference access to 2–3 models spanning the stated tiers (keys/weights NOT available in the current environment; network is disabled here).
- Wikidata SPARQL + Wikipedia access for curation (also network-dependent; fallback is manual curation by the researcher).
- Curation labor: ~1–2 researcher-days for N ≈ 150 dual-source-verified pairs with alias lists and fame proxies.
- Compute: trivial — a plain-Python harness (no GPU needed for API-based evaluation; local open models would need one inference GPU per model, which is out of scope for this environment).
- Statistical analysis: standard Python (SciPy/StatsModels McNemar, NumPy bootstrap).

**Limitations (design-level):**
1. Fame proxy (pageviews/sitelinks) is a crude notability measure; stratification reduces but cannot eliminate fame confounding — hence conclusions are stated as *conditional on the proxy*.
2. "Celebrity" scope limits external validity to well-documented, high-frequency entities; the bias may differ for long-tail facts.
3. Single-template, single-language (English) design; wording sensitivity is a known LLM artifact and is not fully explored.
4. Training-data contamination cannot be directly measured; the direction asymmetry is inferred, not attributed to a specific corpus mechanism.
5. The reverse-direction per-child recall metric conflates set-size difficulty with true directional bias in S2 — which is precisely why S1 is the headline and S2 is stratified secondary analysis.
6. Model roster is tier-specified, not vendor-pinned; results may vary by execution-time substitution.

## 10. Deliverable Checklist (what execution would produce)
- Gold pair file: pair ID, parent, child, relation type (bio/adoptive), source citations, alias lists, fame values, stratum labels (S1/S2, fame stratum, set-size bin), exclusion list with reasons.
- Run manifest: model IDs + versions, decoding params, full prompt/response logs, counterbalance order.
- Results tables: per-model, per-stratum forward vs. reverse accuracy/recall, false-child rates, abstention rates; primary McNemar result + bootstrap CI on S1; all secondary analyses labeled exploratory.
- Reproduction script specification: deterministic seeds for bootstrap, fixed normalization/adjudication rules as implemented.

No experiment has been run; this document is the complete design deliverable.

REPO INSPECTION FINDINGS:
- /workspace contains only task.json (537 bytes). The public hypothesis and context are embedded there; track.md exists only as an inline string in task.json reading: "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."
- No datasets, no celebrity data, no constraints files, no scripts anywhere in the workspace (verified via ls and find).
- Environment: Python 3.14.4, no LLM packages (openai/anthropic/transformers/torch absent), network disabled, no GPU — consistent with a paper-design task. Nothing about the experiment needs to be run now.

PROPOSED APPROACH SKETCH:
1) Dataset: a curated list of ~100–150 verified celebrity parent-child pairs, sourced from public records (Wikidata/Wikipedia claims with citations), stored as CSV with fields: child, parent, source_url, birth years (disambiguation), knownness proxy (e.g., Wikipedia pageviews/edit counts), and flags (adoption, multiple famous parents, multiple famous children). Inclusion criteria: both parties independently notable; unambiguous, well-documented relation; alias table for name variants.
2) Two mirrored conditions, paired design: C->P ("Who is the father/mother of {child}?") and P->C ("Name a child of {parent}."); each pair appears in both conditions, so analysis is within-pair (McNemar test on discordant pairs; bootstrap CI on the accuracy difference).
3) Accuracy: exact-match after normalization plus fuzzy matching against an alias table; separately log refusals and "I don't know"; hypothesis test: accuracy(C->P) > accuracy(P->C).

KEY CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS (mine, not fixed task requirements):
- "Real" data = publicly documented celebrity relationships from Wikidata/Wikipedia with citations; the sample is treated as representative of celebrities broadly.
- One canonical parent per child (the more famous one) and a defined child target per parent, to avoid one-to-many asymmetry contaminating P->C.
- Models: assumed to be API-accessible LLMs (e.g., GPT-4-class, Claude, or open models); none are actually available in this design-only sandbox, so the design must specify model-agnostic prompting/scoring.
- Sample size: 100–150 pairs x 2 conditions x 1 model (~200–300 queries) is realistic; x3 for a 3-model robustness check.

UNCERTAINTIES (to resolve in the full design):
- Directional difficulty confound: a famous parent may have many children while a child has exactly two parents; the P->C prompt must be "name any child" and analysis should stratify by cardinality (only-child vs multi-child parents).
- Fame confound: C->P may win simply because parents are more famous than children; knownness proxies must be measured and included as covariates/strata.
- Prompt-format sensitivity: name ordering, phrasing templates, and possible memorized list artifacts; counterbalancing of templates is needed.
- Ground-truth adjudication: fuzzy name matching and alias handling require an explicit alias table plus manual review of borderline answers; negative-control probes (non-existent relations) to detect guessing.
- Contamination: famous pairs may appear verbatim in training data; consider including moderately-known pairs and reporting accuracy by fame tier.
