═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. MODEL AND COMPARISON-ARM SPECIFICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════
1.1 Base architecture [DESIGN CHOICE]
SiT (Scalable Interpolant Transformers) video variant: a DiT-style transformer over spatiotemporal patch tokens, with (i) self-attention over spatial tokens within each frame block, and (ii) a "time attention" mechanism operating across the diffusion-time axis — i.e., the axis indexing the trajectory frames/steps that a single denoising step conditions on. The control arm A1 keeps this module exactly as in the reference implementation. Model scale: the smallest configuration that learns the chosen dataset reliably (see §2), to keep matched-compute training feasible; exact scale is parameterized, not fixed, because no source prescription exists.

1.2 Treatment arm A2 — Hyena replacement [DESIGN CHOICE, constrained by the fixed statement "replace the time attention mechanism"]
• Which blocks: every block in which the original time attention operates (the temporal mixing sublayers only). Spatial self-attention, MLPs, adaLN conditioning, patch embedding, and the interpolant training objective are untouched. This isolates the effect of the temporal operator.
• Operator: non-causal Hyena (long explicit/implicit convolution with data-controlled gating: y_t = Σ_k K_Δ(t, k) · gates; implemented as an FFT convolution over the diffusion-time axis with exponential-modulation kernels and a diagonal, data-dependent gating MLP, per the Hyena/HyenaDNA design). Non-causality is standard for non-autoregressive diffusion and is fixed by the question statement.
• Position encoding over the diffusion-time axis — the ordering-vs-set semantics issue, resolved and justified: SiT's time axis indexes the trajectory's temporal frames, which are ordered in physical time (frame 1 occurs before frame 2), even though the model processes them as a set-like token block in parallel. I adopt the ORDERED interpretation: positions are the frames' physical time indices on a regular grid, encoded with Hyena's implicit position encoding (learned sinusoidal-style embedding z_t of position, conditioning the kernel K(z_t, z_{t−k})). Justification: (a) the hypothesis is about trajectory dynamics over physical time, so temporal ordering is the inductive bias we deliberately inject and test; (b) Hyena's length-generalization via implicit kernels depends on continuous position encoding, which only has the intended meaning under the ordered interpretation; (c) the "set" interpretation would discard the very structure the hypothesis is about, making the experiment uninformative. This is the single most consequential conceptual choice in the design and is documented as Assumption AU-1 (§5).
• Parameter/FLOP matching strategy: (i) primary match — total trainable parameters within ±2% between A1 and A2, achieved by tuning the Hyena channel-expansion width (the gating MLP width) and filter-order projection dimensions; time-attention layers are typically a small fraction of DiT parameters, so the Hyena branch is width-scaled to absorb the difference; (ii) secondary reporting — per-step training FLOPs and wall-clock per 1k steps for both arms, reported openly (exact parity is not forced; matched optimization budget in steps is, i.e., both arms train for the identical number of steps and samples seen). Learning rate and schedule are tuned once per arm on a short proxy run with identical budget, then frozen.

1.3 A3 — scaled-attention control [SUGGESTED ADDITION, clearly optional]
A third arm: the original time attention with position encodings extended/interpolated (e.g., RoPE-style frequency scaling) to the long generation length at inference, and optionally fine-tuned briefly at an intermediate length. Purpose: to separate the hypothesis "Hyena's receptive field/implicit kernels generalize in length" from the trivial confound "attention with rescaled positions also generalizes." If budget allows, A3 is trained at the same cost as A1/A2; if not, A3 runs only at inference-time adaptation from the A1 checkpoint. It is NOT required for the hypothesis test; omitting it weakens interpretation but not validity of the A1-vs-A2 comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. DATASET AND OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
2.1 Dataset [DESIGN CHOICE]
Primary: 2D Kolmogorov-flow / forced incompressible Navier–Stokes simulation data (or equivalently the PDE-bench-style turbulence trajectory sets). Justification: it exhibits cleanly separated timescales — a slow, coherent large-scale vortex/energy-envelope dynamics and fast small-scale vortical fluctuations — with an exact ground truth available for arbitrarily long rollouts from a cheap reference solver, so spectral ground truth at any length is available without annotation. Secondary (robustness check): a multiscale ODE system (e.g., Lorenz-96 two-tier, F = fast variables coupled to X = slow variables), which is cheap enough to run the full protocol many times and provides analytic timescale separation (slow mode decay times vs. fast oscillation periods). Training set: trajectories of length L_train frames, sampled from long simulations; held-out set: longer trajectories from the same simulator for evaluation up to the maximum evaluated length.
Trajectory representation for SiT: frames are the "time axis"; each frame's spatial field is patchified as in the base SiT video model.

2.2 "Extremely long" [operational definition]
A generated trajectory of length L_gen such that L_gen = r · L_train with r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} evaluated systematically, plus a search upward in ×2 steps until the failure criterion (§3.2) triggers. "Extremely long" concretely means r ≥ 4 with full metrics reported at every r. The length-generalization claim is evaluated at generation time only: both arms are trained exclusively at L_train; no length curriculum, no length conditioning changes (if the base SiT uses any length embedding, both arms share it identically).

2.3 "Consistency" [operational definition, three layers]
C1 — Per-frame quality across the rollout: per-frame FID/KID-style distributional distance (or field-space RMSE in physical units for PDE data) computed in non-overlapping windows along the trajectory; a trajectory is consistent if the windowed metric does not degrade by more than a pre-registered tolerance (e.g., median window metric stays within 1.5× its value over the first window, for windows covering ≥80% of L_gen). This turns "no degradation along the rollout" into a falsifiable criterion rather than an average.
C2 — Temporal coherence / no drift or collapse: (a) rolling-window FVD (video datasets) or windowed two-sample statistics on field statistics (energy, enstrophy, vorticity histograms for PDE data) — flatness of these statistics over time is required; (b) feature-persistence: correlation of a fixed object/structure descriptor between consecutive windows (e.g., dominant vortex positions for Kolmogorov flow) must not decay to chance level; (c) drift metric: absolute difference between first-window and last-window summary statistics.
C3 — Trajectory-level distributional match: FVD (or the PDE analogue: distributional distance over trajectory-level statistics) between generated sets of length-L_gen trajectories and ground-truth sets of the same length.

2.4 "Multi-timescale dynamics" [operational definition]
M1 — Band-resolved spectral fidelity: per-trajectory power spectral density (2D field spectra time-resolved, or 1D temporal spectra per spatial mode); compare generated vs. ground truth separately in a LOW band (frequencies below the characteristic slow-mode frequency) and a HIGH band (above it), via band-integrated spectral RMSE and log-spectral distance. The two-scale claim requires BOTH bands to match within tolerance; success in only one band is reported as partial.
M2 — Lagged correlation structure: auto-/cross-correlation functions of key observables (e.g., large-scale vorticity mode for the slow timescale; a high-wave-number energy proxy for the fast timescale) compared between generated and true trajectories; metric = integrated L1 difference of the correlation curves, reported per lag band so short-lag (fast) and long-lag (slow) fidelity are separately visible.
M3 — Timescale extraction: fitted characteristic timescales (e.g., decay time of the slow mode's autocorrelation, mean period of the fast oscillation) from generated vs. true trajectories; report relative error per timescale. This gives an interpretable, one-number-per-timescale summary.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. TRAINING AND EVALUATION PROTOCOL
═══════════════════════════════════════════
3.1 Training [matched compute]
• Both arms trained on identical data order (shared seed), identical batch size, identical number of optimizer steps, identical interpolant/flow objective and sampler schedule.
• Optimization budget parity: identical step count and samples seen; FLOP differences reported, not equalized (see §5).
• LR/schedule tuned on short proxy runs per arm under identical proxy budget; then frozen for the full run.
• ≥3 seeds per arm (3 minimum; 5 preferred) for error bars on every headline metric.

3.2 Evaluation
• Generate N ≥ 256 trajectories per arm per evaluated length r ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, …} with identical samplers/steps.
• Failure criterion (defines the generation-length limit): the smallest evaluated r at which C1 tolerance is violated, or C2 shows drift beyond threshold, or trajectory-level C3 degrades beyond a pre-registered margin. Report the limit curve — generation-length limit as a function of arm.
• All metrics (§2.3, §2.4) computed at every evaluated r; paired comparisons arm-by-arm at each r.
• Hyena ablation (A2 only): sweep kernel filter order (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and effective kernel length/positional-encoding frequency range; measure whether the generation-length limit and long-lag correlation fidelity scale with the operator's receptive field, holding parameters matched per A2-config. Purpose: test the mechanism (receptive-field-driven length generalization), not just the end-to-end score.

3.3 Statistical treatment
• Metric comparisons at each r: paired-by-seed mean ± std, plus a distributional two-sample test on trajectory-level metrics; pre-registered tolerances (from §2.3) fixed before any generation run.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. ANALYSIS PLAN — DECISION CRITERIA
═══════════════════════════════════════════
The hypothesis is SUPPORTED only if ALL of the following hold (with seed-level error bars, paired across seeds):
 (i) Length: A2's generation-length limit ≥ A1's limit by at least one evaluated doubling step (r = 4 or beyond for A2), with A1 failing at or before r = 2 under the same criteria; or, if both arms pass all r, A2 shows no degradation where A1 does.
 (ii) Consistency: at every evaluated r where both arms pass, A2's C1/C2/C3 metrics are statistically non-inferior to A1's (non-inferiority margin pre-registered, e.g., 10% relative); if A1 fails first, A2's metrics remain inside tolerance at the larger r.
 (iii) Multi-timescale: A2's M1 band-integrated spectral errors and M2 lagged-correlation differences are non-inferior to A1's in BOTH bands, and M3 relative errors of extracted timescales are comparable or better for both slow and fast timescales.
The hypothesis is REFUTED if A2 is non-inferior on at most one of (i)/(ii)/(iii), or fails earlier than A1 on the length-limit criterion, or shows spectral fidelity in only one band (indicating it captures one timescale but not multi-timescale structure).
A MIXED result (e.g., equal length limits but A2 better on long-lag correlation) is reported as such — the design pre-registers the primary criterion as the conjunction of (i)–(iii), so no post-hoc re-interpretation is needed.
Fairness controls: matched parameters/steps/schedule/sampler; identical data seeds; identical evaluation code path; A3 (if run) isolates operator type from position-scaling effects; the Hyena ablation ties any observed gain to receptive field rather than parameter placement.

Predictions (explicitly predictions, not findings): if Hyena's implicit-kernel length extrapolation transfers to the diffusion-time axis, A2 should degrade more gracefully at r ≥ 4 and maintain long-lag correlation structure better; if the diffusion-time axis's ordered semantics are mis-specified or the interpolation objective does not exercise the long receptive field, both arms should behave similarly and the hypothesis would be refuted. These are stated as expectations to be tested, with no claimed outcome.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. FEASIBILITY AND ASSUMPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
5.1 Cost accounting (feasibility)
• Attention over the diffusion-time axis costs O(L²·d) at sequence length L (number of trajectory frames processed per denoising step); non-causal Hyena costs O(L log L) FFT convolution + O(L·d) gating. For small L (training, L_train frames, typically tens to a few hundred), attention is cheap and Hyena's FFT overhead means A2 may train slower per step — hence step-count parity, with FLOP/wall-clock parity reported but not forced. For long L (generation at r = 8+), Hyena's advantage grows; generation cost at extreme lengths favors A2, which should be reported as a practical benefit separate from the quality hypothesis.
• Memory: attention materializes L² score maps (or flash-attention reduces memory but not asymptotics); Hyena needs O(L) activations plus FFT workspace. Feasible on single-node multi-GPU for the proposed scales; the design keeps model scale minimal deliberately.
• Engineering risk: Hyena's FFT convolution over a non-standard axis (frame axis within a DiT token grid) requires careful reshaping and may need a custom kernel; a fallback is a long-convolution implementation in PyTorch FFT primitives, which is sufficient for design-scale experiments.

5.2 The length-extrapolation mechanism question
The core mechanism being tested is Hyena's ability to generalize beyond training sequence length via implicit, continuously-parameterized position encodings (as demonstrated in HyenaDNA-style settings), whereas softmax attention with learned/rotary positions typically degrades beyond training length. The design makes this the explicit object of measurement (the r-sweep and the A3 scaled-attention control). Key open risk: it is not established from the source that the diffusion-time axis in SiT is even treated as a length-extrapolatable sequence — if the reference implementation conditions on diffusion time in a way that is invariant to trajectory length (e.g., fixed-size frame blocks), the "generation length" manipulation must be defined at the frame-block level, and this definition is [DESIGN CHOICE] documented below.

5.3 Explicit assumptions section
Assumptions (design choices I make, not source-supported claims):
 AS-1: The base model is a SiT video/dynamics variant whose "time attention" mixes information across the trajectory-frame (diffusion-time) axis; its exact layer placement follows the standard DiT-block layout (time attention as an additional temporal sublayer alongside spatial attention). No source specifies otherwise.
 AS-2: Ordered (not set) semantics for the diffusion-time axis, for the reasons in §1.2 — the central conceptual assumption (AU-1).
 AS-3: Dataset is Kolmogorov-flow/Navier–Stokes simulation data (primary) + Lorenz-96 (secondary); chosen for clean timescale separation and cheap ground truth. Not source-prescribed.
 AS-4: Matched-parameter (±2%) and matched-step training; FLOP/wall-clock parity reported, not enforced.
 AS-5: Model scale, tolerance thresholds, r-grid, seed count, and sample counts are chosen to make the protocol feasible on a modest single-node compute budget; they are parameters, not prescriptions, and would be scaled up if the compute budget were larger.
 AS-6: Non-causal (bidirectional) kernels are used, per the question statement; causality is irrelevant because the diffusion-time axis is not autoregressive.
Uncertainties (cannot be resolved from the source; flagged, handled by design):
 AU-1: Diffusion-time-axis semantics (ordered vs. set) — resolved by assumption AS-2 with justification; if the researcher's intent differs, the position-encoding design and interpretation of "long trajectory" change.
 AU-2: Exact paper integration details and prescribed Hyena hyperparameters are unavailable; kernel order/width are swept in the ablation rather than fixed.
 AU-3: Compute budget unspecified; the protocol is sized to be modestly feasible and reports costs so it can be rescaled.
 AU-4: Whether length generalization should be tested at training time (curriculum) or only at inference; design assumes inference-only extrapolation (strictest and most informative test).
 AU-5: Whether "consistency" should be judged distributionally or per-trajectory; the design uses both (C1/C2 per-trajectory windowed, C3 distributional).
 AU-6: Hyena position-encoding frequency range must cover the evaluated generation lengths; if it does not, apparent length generalization could be an artifact of encoding range — handled by evaluating at lengths within and beyond the encoding range and reporting both.

Deliverable status: this is a complete design specification. No code was run, no model was trained, no trajectories were generated, and no results exist; all outcome statements are framed as pre-registered predictions and decision criteria.

FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment executed, no results claimed)

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND HYPOTHESES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
RQ: Does the adversarial game setup in SPAG (Adversarial Taboo self-play with imitation learning of a strong teacher) yield superior reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial game setups (20-Question and Guess-My-City) run through the same pipeline?

H1 (primary, transfer): The Adversarial-Taboo arm shows a larger gain over its no-training baseline on held-out standard reasoning benchmarks than the 20-Question and Guess-My-City arms show over theirs.
H2 (secondary, in-game): The Adversarial-Taboo arm shows a larger gain on held-out game-instance success than the non-adversarial arms.
H0: Arm gains do not differ beyond seed-level noise.
H3 (mechanism, auxiliary): The imitation-only control improves less than any self-play arm, isolating self-play as the active ingredient.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. ARMS (fixed by requirements: setup_2, setup_32, setup_33)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
All arms share an identical pipeline skeleton; ONLY the game differs across the three game arms.

- A1 — Adversarial Taboo (SPAG): meta-prompt generates two-role episodes (defender must convey a target word without saying it; attacker/critic adversarially probes and flags failures). The critic explicitly attacks weaknesses and identifies inferior responses, producing preference pairs (better/worse defender behavior). Trained with a DPO-style preference optimization (EPO-style in SPAG — recollection, unverified).
- A2 — 20-Question: same meta-prompt template structure and episode volume, but the critic gives cooperative/neutral feedback (guesser asks yes/no questions; no adversarial attack objective). Preference pairs constructed with the same criterion: which response better advances cooperative success.
- A3 — Guess-My-City: same constraints; descriptive/cooperative game, neutral critic feedback.
- C1 — No-training control (base model, same checkpoints/decoding).
- C2 — Imitation-only control: teacher-generated preference data with NO self-play episodes (single-pass supervised/DPO data from the teacher), matched in pair count to the game arms. This separates imitation learning from self-play effects.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. CONTROLLED VARIABLES AND CONFOUND PREVENTION (explicit controls)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Confounds and their controls:
(a) Teacher/critic quality → SAME fixed judge/critic model in all arms (default: a fixed strong open-weights model at a frozen checkpoint; GPT-4 variant see §7). The critic prompt differs only in the adversarial instruction; an identical system prompt skeleton is used. Critic identity and temperature are logged and frozen.
(b) Data volume → Matched budgets: identical number of generated episodes, extracted preference pairs, and optimizer updates across A1–A3 and C2. If one game yields fewer valid pairs per episode, keep training pairs matched by generating more episodes only up to the fixed episode cap and record the shortfall — do not silently top up.
(c) Training hyperparameters → identical optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and schedule; one shared pilot sweep on A1, then frozen for all arms (avoids per-arm tuning bias).
(d) Prompt/format leakage → no game-format text in evaluation prompts; evaluation prompts are benchmark-native.
(e) Rater bias → all free-text judging automated with the same fixed judge; judge never sees the arm label; spot-check a sample with human raters for judge-drift.
(f) Selection bias in episodes → games drawn from a shared entity/word pool split into disjoint train/held-out sets; no entity appears in both.
(g) Seed variance → ≥3 independent training seeds per arm (A1–A3, C2), same seeds across arms for paired comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. MODELS AND EVALUATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Base models (ASSUMPTION — recollection of SPAG, unverified): LLaMA-2-7B-Chat and LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct; if resource-constrained, run the primary model first (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) and add the second only in the extended budget. One model is sufficient for the primary claim; the second tests generality.

Evaluation, per fixed decision (1):
- PRIMARY: transfer to held-out standard reasoning benchmarks. Proposed suite (ASSUMPTION — unverified list; substitute the paper's suite if topics provide it): 3–4 benchmarks spanning distinct reasoning types, e.g., BBH (multi-task reasoning), GSM8K (math), ARC-Challenge (science reasoning), MMLU (knowledge/reasoning). Held-out splits only; no benchmark data used anywhere in training. Decoding and prompting templates frozen across arms.
- SECONDARY: in-game held-out performance — win/success rate on held-out game instances for each arm's own game, plus a cross-game probe (A1's model evaluated on A2/A3 games) to measure generality of the trained behavior.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. SELF-PLAY BUDGET AND CONFIGURATIONS (per fixed decision (2))
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Iteration structure: R rounds of (episode generation → critic labeling → preference-pair extraction → DPO-style training), identical R for all arms.

PRIMARY (feasible at paper-like scale, ASSUMPTION on scale):
- R = 2 rounds; ~2,000 episodes per round per arm; target ≥2,000 preference pairs per arm; ~1,000 optimizer updates total.
- Seeds: 3 per arm. Arms trained: A1, A2, A3, C2 (4 arms × 3 seeds = 12 training runs) + 2 base models evaluated (no training).
- Cost driver: critic/teacher labeling (≈8k+ episode judgments). Estimate ~O(10⁷) teacher tokens per arm.

REDUCED-BUDGET VARIANT:
- 1 base model (Llama-3-8B-Instruct only), R = 1 round, ~800 episodes/arm, ≥800 pairs/arm, 3 seeds for A1–A3 but 1 seed for C2 (its role is directional, not the headline test).
- Sensitivity note: with R=1 and fewer pairs, absolute gains shrink and CIs widen; conclusions should be reported as "direction of effect with CI" not significance-claimed if power is low. A pre-registered minimum detectable effect (e.g., ≥2 points benchmark accuracy) should be stated; if the reduced budget's power falls below detecting that MDE, the reduced variant supports only qualitative ordering.

Budget sensitivity statement: because the true budget is unknown, the design is robust in structure (matched budgets, same controls) at any scale; what degrades with budget is statistical power and the second-model generality check, not the internal validity of the comparison.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- Per arm and seed: Δbenchmark = mean held-out benchmark accuracy(post − pre). Primary contrast: Δ(A1) − max/mean of Δ(A2), Δ(A3); report per benchmark and pooled.
- Statistics: paired comparisons across matched seeds; bootstrap CIs (10k resamples over benchmark items) plus a seed-level paired permutation test. Alpha = 0.05, Holm correction across the primary contrasts (A1 vs A2, A1 vs A3).
- Also report effect sizes and CIs (not just p-values), and per-seed spread to expose self-play variance.
- H3 check: Δ(C2) vs Δ(A1..A3) with the same procedure.
- Pre-registration of the primary endpoint (pooled benchmark delta) before any training run to prevent benchmark-shopping.
- Failure modes to report explicitly: invalid episode yield per game, preference-pair shortfall, critic rejection rates — these are evidence about whether games are comparably trainable, part of the answer, not noise to hide.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
7. JUDGE/CRITIC CONFIGURATION (per fixed decision (3))
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- CONTROLLED DEFAULT: a single fixed open-weights strong model (frozen checkpoint) as critic and imitation target in every arm, including C2. Rationale: removes API-cost uncertainty and guarantees identical teacher across arms; limitation: weaker teacher may cap imitation quality identically in all arms (does not bias the contrast).
- ALTERNATIVE (paper-faithful variant): GPT-4 as critic in all arms, if access exists. Same matched-budget controls apply. If both are run, this becomes a teacher-strength factor in a 2×3 sub-design.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
8. FEASIBILITY AND DESIGN-ONLY STATUS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Feasibility (if ever executed): 12 fine-tuning runs of ≤8B models are modest; the binding constraint is teacher labeling volume, mitigated by the fixed-critic default. The current environment (network disabled, no GPU, no ML packages) could not execute any part of this — as required, this is a design only.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
9. ASSUMPTIONS (separate from fixed requirements)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
[ASSUMPTION] Base models LLaMA-2-7B-Chat / Llama-3-8B-Instruct reflect SPAG's setup (recollection; researcher confirmed no source support is available).
[ASSUMPTION] SPAG trains via EPO-style (DPO-family) preference optimization on GPT-4-critic-labeled self-play episodes (recollection; the design only requires "some preference optimization," so substituting the paper's exact method changes nothing structurally).
[ASSUMPTION] Benchmark list (BBH/GSM8K/ARC/MMLU) is a stand-in for the paper's suite.
[ASSUMPTION] "Non-adversarial" is operationalized as cooperative/neutral critic feedback — this is the design's operationalization, not a verified paper fact.
[ASSUMPTION] Paper-scale episode/round counts (§5 primary) are rough; the matched-budget control makes conclusions robust to their exact values.

FIXED REQUIREMENTS (from task and researcher): adversarial arm = SPAG/Adversarial Taboo; non-adversarial arms = 20-Question and Guess-My-City; matched data/training budgets across arms; no-training baseline; imitation-only control; ≥3 seeds with paired statistical comparison; explicit critic and data-volume confound controls; both transfer (primary) and in-game evaluation; primary + reduced-budget configurations; no execution or fabricated results. All satisfied as specified above.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTIES: exact paper benchmark list and iteration counts unverifiable (no source access); reduced-budget variant may be underpowered for significance testing; GPT-4 variant availability unknown; single-model reduced variant limits generality claims. These affect power and generality, not the internal logic of the comparison.

payload.answer:
# Final Experiment Design (design-only deliverable)

**Research question.** Does the adversarial game setup used in SPAG (imitation learning on GPT-4 followed by self-play on game episodes, instantiated as Adversarial Taboo) provide *superior* reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial setups (20-Question, Guess-My-City)?

**Scope note.** This is a design document only. No experiment was executed, no results are reported, and no paper details are asserted as facts beyond what the task materials confirm. All source-derived facts are explicitly labeled; everything else is flagged as an assumption or a to-be-confirmed parameter.

---

## 1. Setup inventory: confirmed vs assumed

**Confirmed (from task materials):**
- Design-only task; `track.md`: "repositories and compute are not required." `/workspace` contains only `task.json`.
- The comparison structure is fixed by the question: adversarial arm = IL on GPT-4 + self-play on Adversarial Taboo episodes (SPAG-style); non-adversarial arms = 20-Question and Guess-My-City; outcome = reasoning improvements.
- Authoritative source for SPAG setup details is the NeurIPS 2024 paper #93638, available to the researcher via topics `setup_2`, `setup_32`, `setup_33`. Any paper-specific configuration below is marked **[ASSUMED — confirm via topic]**.

**Assumed (not confirmed by any available source):**
- Base model of LLaMA-2-class (7B/13B) **[ASSUMED]**; evaluation benchmarks BMATH and GSM-Hard **[ASSUMED — confirm via topic]**; two-role IL (guesser + word-giver) **[ASSUMED]**; iterative self-play with episode selection/filtering **[ASSUMED]**.
- The mechanics of 20-Question and Guess-My-City and whether their published training pipelines used IL+self-play — not available; the design *imposes* a symmetric pipeline on all arms (see §3, Assumption A2).

---

## 2. Arms (arm structure retained from approved skeleton)

| Arm | Game | IL (GPT-4) | Self-play | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Adversarial Taboo (SPAG) | yes | yes | core |
| A2 | 20-Question | yes | yes | core |
| A3 | Guess-My-City | yes | yes | core |
| C0 | no game training (control) | no | no | core |
| A1b | Adversarial Taboo, self-play only (no IL) | no | yes | **optional, priority 1** |
| A1c | Adversarial Taboo, IL only (no self-play) | yes | no | **optional, priority 2** |
| C0b | neutral SFT (matched token count, non-game data) | — | — | **optional, priority 3** |

Rationale for decomposition arms: A1b isolates the contribution of adversarial self-play per se; A1c isolates the contribution of GPT-4 imitation. If budget is tight, A1b first (it most directly tests "adversarial self-play is the active ingredient"), then A1c, then C0b. If even one optional arm is dropped, the conclusion must be phrased as "SPAG pipeline vs non-adversarial pipelines" rather than "adversarial self-play is the mechanism."

---

## 3. Justification of key design choices

**(a) Identical episode/token/iteration budgets across arms.** Training quantity is a confounder: more game episodes or more fine-tuning tokens mechanically improves benchmark performance regardless of game type. If arms differed in budget, any observed difference would be attributable to scale of training, not to adversarial vs non-adversarial structure. Therefore: identical number of self-play iterations, identical total fine-tuning tokens (IL + self-play combined), identical data-selection procedures, identical learning-rate schedule, identical decoding parameters at evaluation. Token budgets are matched at the *fine-tuning token* level (not episode count), because average episode length differs across games and episode-count matching would silently create token-count differences.

**(b) GPT-4 imitation held symmetric across arms.** The question fixes IL-on-GPT-4 only for the SPAG arm. Applying IL to all game arms is **Assumption A1** — a deliberate design choice, not a source claim. Justification: if IL were asymmetric, arm differences would conflate (i) game type with (ii) teacher-trajectory exposure. Symmetric IL makes the contrast a clean test of the game structure (adversarial opponent vs cooperative/informational game) under an otherwise identical curriculum. Consequence to acknowledge: a negative result would mean "adversarial games are not superior *under symmetric IL conditions*," not that SPAG's exact recipe (which may rely on the adversarial game specifically for IL) fails. If the researcher's topics reveal that IL is structurally tied to the adversarial game (e.g., GPT-4 trajectories exist only for Taboo), the fallback is to generate GPT-4 trajectories for 20-Question and Guess-My-City under the same prompting template — this becomes a stated assumption to validate in the pilot.

**(c) Superiority test paired with an equivalence check (TOST).** The question is phrased "does A provide superior improvements?" A one-sided superiority test alone cannot distinguish "no difference" from "underpowered study." Pairing a superiority test (one-sided, corrected for multiplicity) with two one-sided tests (TOST) against a pre-registered equivalence margin δ yields a complete 2×2 decision structure: (i) superiority demonstrated; (ii) equivalence demonstrated (adversarial offers no meaningful advantage); (iii) inconclusive (increase power or report honestly). δ should be set a priori, e.g., δ = 1 percentage point accuracy on the primary benchmark composite, or justified by the smallest effect that would matter for a practitioner.

---

## 4. Addressing the cross-game difficulty/length confounder head-on

The games differ in episode complexity, turn structure, and utterance length; without control, a "better" arm may simply train on more informative or longer text.

**Primary control — difficulty/quality matching of training episodes:**
- Define a per-episode quality/difficulty score common to all games: e.g., number of informative turns, episode outcome quality (win/loss plus margin), and a learned or heuristic measure of linguistic complexity (token length distribution, vocabulary level). Match the *distributions* of these statistics across arms by stratified sampling of training episodes (quantile matching on length and outcome rates), so each arm consumes episodes with comparable statistical profiles.
- Additionally match outcome-rate targets: cap each arm's training set so that (for example) the fraction of successful episodes is equalized, preventing one arm from learning mostly from wins and another mostly from losses.

**Secondary control — matched token budgets** (§3a) at both SFT and self-play stages.

**Fallback if distribution matching is not feasible** (e.g., a game's episode distribution cannot reach the target profile): (i) reweight episodes (importance weights) instead of hard matching, and report both reweighted and unmatched results; (ii) if reweighting also fails, include game difficulty as a covariate in the analysis model (ANCOVA-style: benchmark gain ~ arm + episode-difficulty covariates) and pre-register that the primary conclusion uses the covariate-adjusted comparison; (iii) in all fallback cases, report the achieved distribution mismatch statistics transparently as a limitation. The pilot phase (§7) measures whether matching is feasible before full scale-up.

---

## 5. Metrics

**Primary metric:** Δaccuracy on a pre-registered reasoning benchmark composite vs arm C0 (benchmark set is a to-be-confirmed parameter; candidate set BMATH + GSM-Hard is **[ASSUMED]**). The composite is the pre-weighted mean across benchmarks; per-benchmark deltas are secondary to avoid cherry-picking.

**Secondary metrics:**
- pass@k and self-consistency accuracy (reasoning robustness, not just greedy accuracy);
- CoT quality: step-verifiability rate (programmatic verification where possible, e.g., final-answer consistency; human/LLM-judge audit on a fixed sample), CoT length and repetition statistics;
- in-game performance: win rate per game for each arm playing *its own* game (verifies each pipeline actually improved at its game — a manipulation check), plus cross-game win rate where rules allow (transfer probe);
- mediator measures: fraction of utterances that are information-seeking questions vs disinformation-resistant behavior, to interpret *why* an arm gains.

**Manipulation checks (pre-registered):** (i) training loss/episode-selection statistics comparable across arms; (ii) matched-budget verification (token counts within tolerance); (iii) every trained arm must improve at its own game over C0 — if not, the pipeline failed and the arm's benchmark result is interpreted cautiously.

---

## 6. Analysis plan

1. **Seeds and power:** ≥3 independent seeds per arm (training seeds; evaluation is deterministic given decoding params). Pre-compute power from pilot variance estimates; target ≥80% power for the equivalence margin δ and for the primary pairwise contrast.
2. **Primary analysis:** per-benchmark-item paired comparison of each arm vs C0 (items are the pairing unit; cluster-robust or bootstrap CIs over items × seeds). Family of primary contrasts: {A1, A2, A3} vs C0 — Holm correction across the three.
3. **Key contrast (the question itself):** A1 vs max(A2, A3) — one-sided superiority test, plus TOST equivalence at margin δ. Decision rule: superiority claimed only if both Holm-corrected significance and practical magnitude (≥δ) hold; otherwise report "no demonstrated superiority" with the equivalence verdict.
4. **Decomposition (if optional arms run):** planned contrasts A1 vs A1b (self-play effect), A1 vs A1c (IL effect), both vs C0, Holm-corrected.
5. **Covariate-adjusted analysis** if the fallback in §4 triggers: arm effect adjusted for episode-difficulty covariates.
6. **Sensitivity analyses:** leave-one-benchmark-out; effect of episode-matching method (matched vs reweighted vs unmatched); seed-level leave-one-out to detect driver seeds.
7. **Reporting:** all contrasts with effect sizes (accuracy deltas, CIs), no outcome-dependent metric selection; null/negative results reported with CIs, not suppressed.

---

## 7. Feasibility and parametrized budget plan (design-only; no execution claimed)

Scope is design-only per `track.md`; the following is a planning framework, not performed work. All quantities are parameters (P1–P5) to be fixed once source topics confirm the SPAG configuration:

- **P1 — base model & scale** [ASSUMED: LLaMA-2-class 7B]: sets GPU cost per fine-tune; 4 core arms × 3 seeds = 12 fine-tune runs minimum (plus optional arms).
- **P2 — GPT-4 teacher budget**: cost driver for IL trajectories; scales as (games × episodes per game × tokens per episode). Symmetric IL (Assumption A1) triples teacher cost relative to SPAG-only IL; if budget-constrained, the first concession is to reduce teacher-episode count uniformly across arms, never asymmetrically.
- **P3 — self-play iterations** [ASSUMED: iterative, with filtering]: each iteration requires generation + selection + fine-tune; total cost = arms × seeds × iterations. Pilot (reduced scale: 1 seed, 2 arms, 1/10 episodes) validates the pipeline and estimates variance for the power calculation before full scale-up.
- **P4 — evaluation budget**: benchmark inference is comparatively cheap and cacheable; fixed decoding parameters.
- **P5 — pilot gate**: difficulty-matching feasibility (§4) and per-arm in-game improvement (§5 manipulation check) must both pass in the pilot before committing full budget.

**Practical constraints acknowledged:** environment has no GPU and no preinstalled dependencies; if execution were ever commissioned, infrastructure (fine-tuning stack, game servers for the three games, benchmark harness) must be built first — this is explicitly out of scope here.

---

## 8. Assumptions (separate from fixed task requirements)

- **A1 (stated per researcher comment #2):** GPT-4 imitation learning is applied symmetrically across all game arms; the question fixes it only for the SPAG arm. This is a design choice for causal cleanliness, not a source claim.
- **A2:** 20-Question and Guess-My-City can be trained with an IL+self-play pipeline analogous to SPAG's; their rules are implementable in the same interface.
- **A3:** Base model is LLaMA-2-class; benchmarks include BMATH/GSM-Hard **[ASSUMED — confirm via topic]**.
- **A4:** Reasoning improvement is operationalized as benchmark accuracy gain (not in-game skill per se).

## 9. Limitations and open uncertainties

1. **Unconfirmed SPAG specifics** (model, iteration/episode counts, data filtering, benchmark set): resolved only via topics setup_2/32/33; until then, all paper-derived parameters above remain assumptions.
2. **Non-adversarial game pipelines:** the imposed symmetric pipeline may not match how these games were trained in their original works; results speak to the symmetric-pipeline comparison, not to a reproduction of any original non-adversarial method.
3. **Residual difficulty confounding:** even with matching/reweighting, "episodes of equal statistics" need not be "episodes of equal learning value"; the covariate adjustment and sensitivity analyses mitigate but do not eliminate this.
4. **Teacher-quality confounder:** if GPT-4 trajectories are naturally higher-quality for one game (e.g., Taboo is better within GPT-4's strengths), arm differences partly reflect teacher fit, not adversariality; a game-teacher cross table (best-effort, optional) would be needed to probe this.
5. **Generalization:** conclusions hold for the chosen base model and benchmark composite; transfer to other scales or benchmark families is untested within this design.
6. **Equivalence margin δ** is a judgment call; the design pre-registers it but its defensibility depends on domain input.
7. **Statistical power with few seeds:** with 3 seeds, seed-level variance estimates are noisy; item-level bootstrap mitigates but power claims must be re-validated from pilot data.

**2) Detalles de la configuración SPAG — soportados vs. supuestos**

⚠️ **Ningún documento de SPAG existe en el entorno.** Lo único "soportado por fuentes" dentro de este entorno es lo que diga task.json/track.md. Todo lo que recito del paper NeurIPS 2024 #93638 (*SPAG: Self-Playing Adversarial Language Game Enhances LLM Reasoning*) proviene de **conocimiento externo no verificable aquí**, y debe tratarse como provisional hasta contrastarlo con los topics setup_2/32/33:

- *(conocimiento externo, confianza alta)* SPAG usa el juego **Adversarial Taboo** con dos roles asimétricos: un atacante que debe inducir que el adversario diga una palabra objetivo sin pronunciarla, y un defensor que debe adivinar la palabra; ambas partes razonan activamente.
- *(conocimiento externo, confianza media-alta)* Pipeline en dos etapas: **imitación de GPT-4** (SFT sobre un número pequeño de episodios de juego generados por GPT-4) seguida de **autojuego** (self-play) del propio modelo para generar nuevos episodios, y ajuste posterior (DPO sobre comparaciones de episodios ganados/perdidos).
- *(conocimiento externo, confianza media)* Las configuraciones no adversariales (20-Question, Guess-My-City) se presentan como contraste para mostrar que el beneficio del autojuego depende del carácter adversarial del juego, no solo del autojuego en sí.
- **Suposición explícita (no respaldada por nada en el entorno):** modelos base, tamaño del corpus de imitación, hyperparámetros exactos, benchmarks de evaluación y métricas exactas del paper — todos pendientes de confirmación vía topics.

**3) Esqueleto conceptual del experimento comparativo**

- **Arms (factores):** (a) modelo base sin entrenar; (b) SPAG adversarial: imitación GPT-4 + self-play (Taboo); (c) no adversarial 1: 20-Question; (d) no adversarial 2: Guess-My-City; opcionalmente (e) solo-imitación y (f) solo-self-play para descomponer la contribución de cada etapa.
- **Controles de comparabilidad:** mismo modelo base y tokenizer; mismo presupuesto de entrenamiento (tokens/episodios/updates) entre arms b/c/d; misma receta de ajuste (p. ej., SFT+DPO con hyperparámetros idénticos); mismos prompts de evaluación y parámetros de decodificación; ≥3 semillas; chequeo de contaminación (palabras de juego vs. benchmarks).
- **Métricas de resultado:** precisión pre/post en suite de razonamiento (p. ej., GSM8K/MATH, BBH, ARC); efecto Δ = post − pre por arm; medida de calidad de razonamiento por proceso (judging paso a paso) como métrica secundaria; rendimiento en el juego propio como manipulación-check (confirma que el fine-tuning "pegó" en cada arm).
- **Criterio de respuesta:** el arm adversarial supera a los no adversariales en Δ de razonamiento con significancia estadística y robustez (tamaño de modelo, semilla); comparaciones pareadas entre arms.
- Solo esqueleto; el diseño completo vendría tras su aprobación.

**4) Suposiciones e incertidumbres con consecuencias de diseño**

- **Presupuesto de cómputo no declarado** → limita nº de arms × semillas × tamaños de modelo; sin esto no puedo fijar potencia estadística.
- **Detalles de evaluación desconocidos** (benchmarks exactos, métricas, uso de jueces LLM) → determinan si Δ es comparable entre arms y si hace falta un judge con costo adicional.

- **Suposición:** puedo pedirle el contenido de los topics setup_2/32/33 (presupuesto de 6 preguntas) para anclar la configuración a la fuente real; recomiendo hacerlo antes del diseño completo.
- **Suposición:** "mejora de razonamiento" = Δ de precisión en benchmarks estándar; si usted define razonamiento de otra forma, el diseño cambia.
- **Incertidumbre:** acceso a un profesor GPT-4 (o sustituto) para la imitación, y disponibilidad de pesos del modelo base.

Pido su aprobación del enfoque (y, si lo desea, puedo gastar presupuesto de preguntas para recuperar los tres topics de la fuente).

# DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL COMPLETO (solo diseño — nada se ejecutó ni se afirmará haberse ejecutado)

## 0. Anclaje de fuentes
- **Requisitos fijos (fuente, confirmados por usted):**
  - `setup_2`: "Investigate whether the adversarial game setup in SPAG (using the Adversarial Taboo game for self-play) leads to superior reasoning improvements compared to non-adversarial setups (e.g., 20-Question and Guess-My-City)."
  - `setup_32`: "- adversarial setup using SPAG"
  - `setup_33`: "- non-adversarial setups: 20-Question and Guess-My-City"
  - Del entorno: `task.json` (pregunta y contexto) y `track.md` = "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."
- Todo lo demás (hiperparámetros, benchmarks exactos, tamaño del corpus de imitación, receta DPO) se etiqueta **[EXT: conocimiento externo / suposición]**.

## 1. Pregunta de investigación
¿La configuración adversarial de SPAG (imitación de GPT-4 + autojuego en Adversarial Taboo) produce mejoras de razonamiento superiores a las configuraciones no adversariales (20-Question y Guess-My-City), bajo un protocolo de entrenamiento igualado? *(Anclado a setup_2.)*

## 2. Hipótesis
- **H1 (principal, dirección del paper [EXT]):** el arm adversarial (SPAG/Taboo) logra un Δ de razonamiento (post − pre) mayor que los arms no adversariales, con diferencia estadísticamente significativa.
- **H0:** Δ_adversarial ≤ Δ_no-adversarial (o diferencia no distinguible de ruido).
- **H2 (opcional):** en los arms no adversariales el autojuego produce mejoras menores o nulas — consistente con la tesis del paper de que el carácter adversarial, no el autojuego per se, impulsa la mejora [EXT].

## 3. Arms
**Núcleo (aprobado, requisito):**
- **(a) Base:** modelo sin fine-tuning. Control negativo/ancla de medición.
- **(b) SPAG adversarial [EXT pipeline]:** imitación de GPT-4 sobre episodios de Adversarial Taboo (SFT) → self-play del propio modelo para generar nuevos episodios → ajuste de preferencia (DPO) sobre episodios ganados vs. perdidos, en ambos roles (atacante/defensor).
- **(c) No adversarial 1:** 20-Question (preguntador vs. respondedor; sin oposición de objetivos — cooperativo/consultivo).
- **(d) No adversarial 2:** Guess-My-City (adivinanza descriptiva sin conflicto de intereses).

**Extensión opcional [sugerencia del investigador, NO requisito]:**
- **(e) Solo-imitación** (SFT Taboo sin self-play) y **(f) Solo-self-play** (sin etapa GPT-4): descomponen la contribución de cada etapa. Inclúyase solo si el presupuesto lo permite; si no, quedan como diseño planeado no ejecutado.

## 4. Controles y comparabilidad
1. **Modelo base y tokenizer idénticos** en todos los arms entrenados; mismo punto de partida (checkpoint).
2. **Igualación de presupuesto de entrenamiento** entre (b), (c), (d) [y (e), (f)]: mismo nº de episodios de juego, tokens de entrenamiento, updates, épocas. La receta de ajuste (SFT + DPO con hyperparámetros idénticos) se aplica simétricamente a cada juego; lo único que varía es el juego fuente de los episodios. **[EXT: la receta exacta es suposición; el principio de igualación es decisión de diseño.]**
3. **Episodios generados bajo el mismo protocolo** (mismas semillas de muestreo, misma temperatura, mismo nº de episodios por rol donde aplique).
4. **Evaluación idéntica:** mismos benchmarks, prompts, parámetros de decodificación (temperatura 0 o media sobre k muestras), mismo parser/extractor de respuestas, mismo juez si se usa LLM-judge, aplicado a pre y post de todos los arms.
5. **Semillas:** ≥3 semillas de entrenamiento por arm (o, si el cómputo no alcanza, ≥1 + intervalos bootstrap sobre ítems de evaluación; declarar la limitación).
6. **Chequeo de contaminación:** solapamiento léxico entre palabras/temas de juego y ítems de benchmark; excluir o reportar.
7. **Manipulation-check:** rendimiento en el juego propio de cada arm (tasa de victoria/éxito) pre y post — confirma que el fine-tuning mejoró el juego en cada arm, sin que esto implique mejora de razonamiento general.

## 5. Procedimiento [EXT — suposiciones marcadas]
1. **Imitación GPT-4:** generar N episodios de cada juego con un profesor GPT-4 [suposición: N pequeño, "algunos cientos de episodios" según el paper]; SFT del modelo base sobre las trayectorias ganadoras/de referencia.
2. **Self-play:** el modelo SFT juega consigo mismo (roles asignados) para generar M episodios nuevos por juego; se etiquetan ganados/perdidos según las reglas del juego.
3. **Ajuste por preferencias:** DPO sobre pares de episodios (ganado preferido sobre perdido) [EXT]; mismo procedimiento para los tres juegos, igualado en tokens.
4. **Evaluación:** suite de razonamiento pre/post (ver §6).
- Nota: si no se dispone de profesor GPT-4 real, el diseño admite un sustituto claramente etiquetado (p. ej., un modelo más grande open-weights), lo que cambia la interpretación de "imitación de GPT-4" — declararlo.

## 6. Plan de evaluación y métricas [benchmarks concretos = EXT/suposición]
- **Primaria:** Δ precisión (post − pre) en benchmarks de razonamiento estándar — p. ej., GSM8K, MATH, BBH, ARC-Challenge [EXT]. Métrica agregada: media de Δ sobre la suite.
- **Secundaria:** calidad de razonamiento por proceso (validez de pasos, juzgada por PRM/LLM-judge o evaluación humana en submuestra) [EXT]; consistencia (self-consistency k=…).
- **Terciaria/manipulación:** rendimiento en juego (tasa de éxito por rol).
- **Covariables:** longitud de respuesta, tokens generados (descartar que las ganancias sean artefactos de verbosidad).

## 7. Análisis estadístico
- Comparación pareada por ítem entre Δ_adversarial y Δ_no-adversarial (bootstrap pareado o test de permutación sobre ítems; corregir por comparaciones múltiples, p. ej. Holm).
- Tamaño de efecto (d de Cohen o diferencia de Δ con IC 95%).
- Modelización opcional: modelo mixto con ítem como efecto aleatorio y arm como efecto fijo.
- Criterio de decisión para responder la pregunta: **"superior" = Δ_adversarial > Δ_(c) y Δ_adversarial > Δ_(d), con significancia tras corrección y efecto positivo en la mayoría de benchmarks de la suite.** Si solo supera a uno de los dos, respuesta parcial/matizada.
- Análisis de robustez razonado en papel [sugerencia suya, incluido como opcional]: si el juez LLM sesga la evaluación (p. ej., favorece respuestas más largas o con formato del estilo del juego adversarial), los Δ se distorsionan diferencialmente entre arms. Detección: (i) comparar juez vs. métricas deterministas (exact-match) en los benchmarks que las permiten; (ii) submuestra de doble anotación humana; (iii) test de sensibilidad: reevaluar con un segundo juez distinto y comprobar la estabilidad del ranking de arms; (iv) reportar Δ con y sin ítems sensibles al formato.

## 8. Viabilidad (argumentación en abstracto — sin ejecución)
- Costes relativos: la generación de episodios (self-play) es lo más caro por arm; los tres juegos son conversacionales de coste comparable; el fine-tuning es SFT+DPO sobre cantidades pequeñas [EXT], asumiendo modelo ≤ 13B [EXT].
- Presupuesto ilustrativo [suposición]: con ~10⁴–10⁵ episodios por arm y evaluación de ~10³ ítems × 4 arms × 3 semillas, el cómputo es del orden de decenas de horas-GPU — factible en un clúster medio; inviable aquí (sin GPU, red deshabilitada), por lo que el entregable es el diseño, no la ejecución.
- Riesgos de factibilidad: equilibrio de episodios entre juegos (20-Question puede requerir más turnos/episodio para igualar tokens) — mitigable igualando por tokens, no por episodios.

## 9. Suposiciones e incertidumbres etiquetadas
**Anclado a fuente:** la comparación adversarial (SPAG/Taboo) vs. no adversariales (20-Question, Guess-My-City); naturaleza de solo diseño.
**Suposiciones [EXT]:** receta imitación→self-play→DPO; benchmarks y métricas exactos; tamaño del corpus de imitación; modelo base y disponibilidad de profesor GPT-4 (o sustituto); "razonamiento" = precisión pre/post + calidad de proceso.
**Incertidumbres con consecuencias:** presupuesto de cómputo (limita semillas/arms — afecta potencia); detalles de evaluación del paper (si difieren de los elegidos, los números no son directamente comparables con los reportados); reglas exactas de los juegos no disponibles (la implementación de (c)/(d) podría divergir); nº de semillas alcanzable; posible sesgo del juez LLM (mitigado por §7-robustez).

**Recordatorio explícito:** este documento es un diseño; no se ejecutó ningún experimento y no se reporta ningún resultado.

payload.answer:
# 完整实验设计：对抗性自博弈（SPAG 式）是否优于非对抗性自博弈的推理提升

**设计性质声明**：本文件为纯实验设计，未执行任何实验，不包含任何结果。源相关声明仅依据固定要求 setup_2（题述：SPAG 包含对 GPT-4 的模仿学习 + 对抗性 Taboo 游戏回合上的自博弈）与合理假设；setup_32/setup_33 的具体内容在材料中不可见，设计中所有不依赖其细节的选择均已显式标注为假设。

## 0. 统一信息结构框架（回应"不依赖具体规则细节"的要求）

将三种游戏统一抽象为五元组 **G = ⟨T, C, B, W, X⟩**：
- T（target）：仅防御方/回答方可见的隐藏目标实体；
- C（channel）：信息通道（Taboo=受限自然语言描述；20-Question=是非题问答；Guess-My-City=城市提示对话）；
- B（budget）：每局回合/消息/token 预算（三臂统一换算后对齐，见 §2）；
- W（success predicate）：良性猜测者在预算内正确识别目标；
- X（adversarial observer，可选）：额外可见受限信息的第二猜测者（Taboo 对抗版中为"可见 taboo 词列表并抢先猜词"的猜测者；**此结构为假设**）。

在此框架下，"对抗性 vs 非对抗性"被操作化为**单一变量：是否存在 X**，而非三种游戏的具体规则文本。这样即使 20-Question/Guess-My-City 的确切规则细节未知（假设），设计的因果逻辑仍可成立；执行前只需按实际规则填充 B/W 的参数。

## (a) 各臂详细流程与数据生成规格

**公共底座**（假设）：7B 级开源基座模型（如 Mistral-7B / Llama-2-7B 类），统一微调配置（全参或 LoRA，同一超参网格取一个固定配置）。

**数据生成规格（每局 episode 记录：目标实体、完整对话轨迹、双方输出、胜负判定、token 数）**：
- 目标实体池：三池（常见名词/概念池供 Taboo 与 20-Question 复用；城市池供 Guess-My-City），按基线模型首轮成功率分层（易/中/难），各层等额采样；
- 每臂 SFT 阶段：~3,000–5,000 条 GPT-4 生成并按 W 判定的获胜轨迹，转成指令微调样本；
- 每臂自博弈阶段：~20,000–50,000 局自生成 episode，回合/总 token 预算与 GPT-4 蒸馏数据量对齐。

**各臂流程**：
- **B（基线）**：基础模型零/少样本直接评估。
- **A2（仅模仿学习）**：B + SFT（GPT-4 生成的**对抗性 Taboo** 获胜轨迹）。即题述"imitation learning of GPT-4"成分本身，不含任何自博弈。这是 A1 的前置检查点。
- **A1（SPAG 完整）**：A2 检查点 + 对抗性 Taboo 自博弈阶段——防御者生成描述，良性猜测者与对抗性猜测者（可见 taboo 列表，假设）同时作答，奖励采用"良性猜中 − 对抗者抢先猜中"的差值型奖励（差值形式为合理假设，具体实现允许在执行前对齐源）；由元提示/控制器驱动的迭代自博弈优化。
- **A3（非对抗 20-Question 自博弈）**：B + SFT（GPT-4 20-Question 获胜轨迹，等量）+ 同一套自博弈优化循环，但奖励仅含良性猜测成功项、无 X 成分。
- **A4（Guess-My-City 自博弈）**：同 A3 构造，游戏通道换为城市提示对话。
- **A5（推荐追加的消融臂）**：B + SFT（同一批 GPT-4 Taboo 轨迹，与 A2 完全相同）+ **非对抗版** Taboo 自博弈（移除 X）。A1 vs A5 在"游戏相同、数据相同"下仅差对抗性成分，是对 A3/A4（跨游戏比较）的关键内证。

## (b) 难度匹配与混杂控制的具体化

1. **游戏难度**：统一回合预算 B（换算规则：以基线模型在每游戏上的基线成功率校准，使三游戏在 B 上的平均成功率先对齐到 ±5% 内再定预算）；实体池分同等额采样；GPT-4 蒸馏时固定温度与提示模板。
2. **训练量**：SFT 样本数、自博弈 episode 数、训练 token 数在 A1/A3/A4/A5 间逐一对齐（差 <10%）；微调超参统一。
3. **评估混杂**：评估提示模板、解码（greedy）、判定器（规则判分 + 抽样 10% 用 LLM-judge 交叉验证一致性 ≥95% 才采用）全部固定；评估集对训练分布隔离。
4. **随机性**：每个含随机成分的臂 ≥3 个独立种子（数据采样 + 训练 + 自博弈初始化），逐种子配对比较。
5. **任务迁移混淆**：评估基准中不含与游戏实体池直接重合的题目（如不用城市知识题评估 GMC 臂的优势），或对所有臂报告"含/不含重叠题"两种口径。

## (c) 统计计划

- **主结果**：各臂相对 B 在推理基准套件（假设清单：GSM8K、MATH、ARC-Challenge、BBH 子集）上的逐题准确率增量 Δ。
- **主对比（预注册）**：H1: A1>A2（自博弈增量）；H2: A1>A3；H3: A1>A4；H4: (A1−A2)>(A5−A2)（同游戏下对抗性成分的净效应）。
- **方法**：混合效应 logistic 回归（题目随机效应 + 臂固定效应 + seed 层级），并辅以逐题配对 bootstrap（10,000 次重抽）的 95% CI；效应量报告为准确率差（百分点）与 Cohen's d。
- **多重比较**：四个主对比用 Holm–Bonferroni 校正，α=0.05；消融与机制性分析（如按难度层、按对抗压力强度的分层）仅作探索性报告，不作确证性结论。
- **检验力（量级）**：在 N≈1,000–2,000 题/基准、3 seeds 下，对 ≥1.5 个百分点的组间差具有 >80% 检验力（按常规基准题目量与题间相关性的典型假设估算，标注为假设）。

## (d) 预设判据（执行前锁定）

- **"对抗性提供更优推理提升"成立**当且仅当：H2、H3 校正后均显著为正，且 H1 为正；并具实际意义阈值 Δ≥1 个百分点且 CI 下界 >0。
- **部分支持**：H1 显著为正但 H2/H3 仅一项显著（游戏特异性效应）。
- **不支持**：H1 不显著或方向为负；此时区分"对抗性无益"与"对抗性仅在该数据/预算下无益"的边界条件讨论。
- 任何"SPAG 优于 X"的表述仅在对应对比通过判据后作出。

## (e) 假设与不确定性清单（及对解释的影响）

| # | 内容 | 类型 | 若不成立的影响 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SPAG = 先 GPT-4 轨迹模仿学习、后自博弈（两阶段顺序） | 假设（源自题述方向，未验证） | 若顺序相反，A2 不再是 A1 的严格前置，归因逻辑改为成分分解式 |
| 2 | 对抗性猜测者可见 taboo 列表并抢先猜词 | 假设 | 影响 X 的实现；框架允许替换 X 定义，因果设计不变 |
| 3 | 20-Question / Guess-My-City 的具体规则 | 假设（框架化处理规避） | 仅影响数据生成实现细节，不影响 A1 vs A3/A4 的比较逻辑 |
| 4 | 基座模型 7B 级、基准清单、GPT-4 可用 | 假设 | 规模改变会影响绝对增益与检验力，不改变设计结构 |
| 5 | 预期方向：对抗 > 非对抗 | 待检验假设 | 设计允许零/负结论（判据 d 已覆盖） |
| 6 | setup_32/setup_33 的具体内容不可见 | 未知 | 执行前须核对是否引入额外语义约束；若与 §(a) 冲突，以固定要求为准修订 |
| 7 | 差值型自博弈奖励、难度校准阈值 ±5% | 实现层假设 | 敏感性分析：更换奖励形式/阈值做稳健性检验 |

## (f) 资源量级可行性（量级估计，非虚构预算）

- 模型：7B 级 ×6 个模型状态（B + A1–A5）；SFT 每臂 3k–5k 样本，单臂数十 A100 GPU 小时；
- 自博弈：每臂 2–5 万局，含在线推理，单臂约 10²–10³ A100 GPU 小时（A1 因对抗双方互动最重）；
- GPT-4 蒸馏数据：约 10⁶–10⁷ token 总量（API 调用）；
- 评估：5 套基准 × 6 臂 × 3 seeds ≈ 数千至万级评估项，量级 10² GPU 小时；
- 总量级：全部臂约 10³–5×10³ A100 GPU 小时，属单实验室中大型规模；若资源受限，可先裁剪至核心四臂（B/A1/A2/A3）与单基准套件，保留全部主判据。

**结论性陈述**：本设计通过 A2（剥离自博弈）与 A5（同游戏剥离对抗性）双重建模，可将"对抗性成分"的因果贡献从"模仿学习"与"自博弈本身"中分离；核心问题"A1 是否在 H2/H3+H1 判据下显著优于非对抗自博弈"即为该实验的直接回答。设计中未运行任何步骤，所有量级均为估计。

payload.answer:
PLAN — Experiment design skeleton for "Does SPAG's adversarial setup (Adversarial Taboo: GPT-4 imitation → self-play) yield superior reasoning gains vs. non-adversarial setups (20-Question, Guess-My-City)?"

INSPECTION REPORT (repository /workspace):
- Contents: only `task.json` (580 bytes). No SPAG code, paper text, game implementations, datasets, or checkpoints anywhere on the filesystem. No ML stack (no torch), no GPU. track.md says: design-only; repositories and compute not required.
- Therefore NO paper-derived details are confirmable from the repository. Setup details I can state (roles: attacker sees target word and must elicit it from the defender without saying it; two-stage training — SFT imitation of GPT-4-played episodes, then self-play between student copies with transcripts distilled back; open ~7-8B instruct base model; GPT-4 as teacher/opponent/judge; cooperative Q&A baselines 20-Question and Guess-My-City) come from prior knowledge and are flagged as ASSUMED, not verified.

PROPOSED APPROACH (high level):
1. Conditions (single shared base model, e.g., Llama-3-8B-Instruct):
   A. Adversarial: Adversarial Taboo — stage 1 imitation learning on GPT-4-played episodes (both roles), stage 2 self-play on self-generated episodes + distillation.
   B. Non-adversarial: 20-Question (questioner asks yes/no questions, answerer responds truthfully) — identical two-stage pipeline.
   C. Non-adversarial: Guess-My-City — identical pipeline.
   D. Controls: (i) GPT-4-imitation only, no self-play; (ii) self-play against a fixed/random opponent (isolates the effect of adversarial pressure vs. mere extra game data); (iii) optional no-game SFT baseline on matched generic instruction data.
2. Matching across A/B/C: same episode count, same total training tokens and optimizer steps, same GPT-4-generated vs. self-play transcript ratio, identical SFT hyperparameters, decoding settings, and judge prompts.
3. Measurement: pre/post on held-out reasoning benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K-style and MATH-style suites) + out-of-domain transfer tasks; in-game win rate as a manipulation check. Primary endpoint: mean accuracy delta (post − pre). Secondary: transfer to unseen words/topics; pass@1 vs. majority-vote.
4. Analysis: paired bootstrap CIs on deltas; mixed-effects/ANOVA over condition × benchmark × seed; report effect sizes and variance across ≥3 seeds. Contamination check between game vocabularies and benchmark items.

CONSEQUENTIAL CHOICES I WOULD LIKE THE RESEARCHER TO CONFIRM (topics setup_2, setup_32, setup_33):
- Exact base model and whether GPT-4 acts as judge, opponent, or both.
- Whether imitation covers both roles or one role per episode, and the imitation→self-play transition criterion (fixed episodes vs. win-rate threshold).

FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only deliverable; no execution performed, no results reported)

Research question: Does SPAG's adversarial setup (Adversarial Taboo: GPT-4 imitation learning followed by self-play on game episodes) yield superior reasoning improvements versus non-adversarial setups (20-Question, Guess-My-City)?

Primary contrast (fixed by task context): SPAG/adversarial vs. each non-adversarial arm. The no-game / imitation-only arms are SECONDARY comparisons guarding against a "more game data of any kind" confound.

──────────────────────────────────────────
A. ASSUMED DESIGN PARAMETERS (not source-verified; each flagged [A#], each with a justified default and sensitivity note)
──────────────────────────────────────────
[A1] Base model: Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Default because SPAG-class work targets open ~7–8B instruct models with GPT-4 as teacher. Sensitivity: repeat the best-contrast arm pair on a second family (e.g., Mistral-7B-Instruct or Qwen2-7B-Instruct) at reduced episode budget; conclusions should be treated as preliminary if only one model family is affordable.
[A2] GPT-4 role: teacher/opponent generating stage-1 episodes for BOTH game roles (via persona prompts), plus a judging function in stage 2 (rule-based verifier for hard constraints — e.g., "did the defender utter the target word" — with GPT-4 as arbiter for ambiguous cases only, to cut cost). Sensitivity: a fully rule-based judge variant; if conclusions flip, judge noise is a threat.
[A3] Imitation covers both roles per arm (attacker+defender for Taboo; questioner+answerer for 20-Question and Guess-My-City). Sensitivity: single-role imitation would halve stage-1 data; note as a limitation if budget forces it.
[A4] Stage transition criterion: FIXED episode budget (not a win-rate threshold) — stage 1: 8,000 GPT-4-played episodes per arm; stage 2: 4 self-play rounds × 10,000 episodes with distillation after each round. Fixed budgets guarantee cross-arm comparability. Sensitivity: under a smaller budget (see F), scale to 2,000 + 4×2,500; all arms scale identically, so contrasts remain internally valid; absolute gains will shrink.
[A5] Word/topic lists: Taboo target-word list and city list are public/common-noun and world-city lists (e.g., ~500 items each) matched on corpus frequency and familiarity; 20-Question uses the same noun list as Taboo's target words as question topics. 80/20 train/held-out split of lists.
[A6] SFT hyperparameters: full fine-tune, 3 epochs, lr 2e-5 cosine, batch 128 episodes-equivalent, identical across arms; self-play distillation uses rejection-filtered transcripts (judge-verified legal episodes only).
[A7] Compute assumption for feasibility: 8×A100-80GB (or equivalent ~640 GPU-hr budget) plus limited GPT-4 API budget (~$500 default, ~$150 reduced variant).
[A8] Evaluation decoding: greedy (temperature 0), fixed 3-shot prompts, identical across arms.

──────────────────────────────────────────
B. CONDITION MATRIX (all arms share [A1], [A6], [A8] and matched budgets)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Data/compute matching rule: identical number of training episodes, identical total fine-tuning tokens, identical GPT-4-transcript share, identical optimizer steps. Because episode lengths differ across games, the binding constraint is TOTAL TOKENS: each arm is padded/truncated (by repeating or sampling episodes) to the same token budget T ≈ 29M tokens (≈5M imitation + ≈24M self-play per [A4]).

| Arm | Game | Stage 1 (GPT-4 imitation) | Stage 2 (self-play) | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (PRIMARY) | Adversarial Taboo (SPAG-style) | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | adversarial |
| 2 (PRIMARY) | 20-Question | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | non-adversarial |
| 3 (PRIMARY) | Guess-My-City | 8k episodes, both roles | 4 rounds × 10k episodes + distill | non-adversarial |
| 4 (secondary) | Taboo, imitation-only | 8k episodes | none (train on stage-1 only, token-matched by padding with stage-1 data) | control |
| 5 (secondary) | Taboo self-play vs. fixed/random opponent (frozen stage-1 snapshot as opponent; opponent rotates among snapshots to avoid trivial exploitation) | 8k episodes | 4 rounds × 10k vs. fixed opponent | control |
| 6 (secondary, optional) | No-game SFT on generic instruction data token-matched to T | — | — | control |

Interaction-step matching: all self-play arms (1,2,3,5) run the same number of game turns per episode (Taboo capped at 12 turns; 20-Question at 20 yes/no turns but token-normalized so total interactive tokens match; Guess-My-City capped at 12 turns). Judge calls counted uniformly.

──────────────────────────────────────────
C. PER-ARM PIPELINE SPECIFICATION
──────────────────────────────────────────
Stage 0 (setup): build word/city/topic lists [A5]; split 80/20; pre-register prompts (system prompts define roles and rules identically templated across games).
Stage 1 (imitation, all arms 1–5): generate GPT-4-played episodes [A2][A3]; filter illegal/degenerate episodes (rule verifier); SFT on transcripts (loss on assistant-role tokens only).
Stage 2 (self-play, arms 1,2,3,5): each round — (i) sample held-out and train-list items; (ii) student copy A vs. student copy B play N episodes (arm 5: vs. frozen snapshot); (iii) judge scores episodes [A2]; (iv) distill judge-passing transcripts back into the single student via SFT (same lr/epochs [A6]); (v) log win rates and language-quality stats (repetition, degeneration) for stability monitoring [E3].
Stage 3 (freeze final checkpoint; identical eval pipeline for all arms).

──────────────────────────────────────────
D. EVALUATION PLAN
──────────────────────────────────────────
D1. Primary reasoning benchmarks (primary endpoint): GSM8K full test and MATH-500 — metric: exact-match accuracy, greedy decoding [A8]. Rationale: multi-step reasoning where SPAG-class claims concentrate.
D2. In-domain transfer / generalization: (i) held-out 20% of game lists — in-game win rate vs. a frozen GPT-4 opponent (manipulation check: confirms the adversarial arm actually learned the adversarial skill); (ii) unseen-topic game variants to test that gains are not list-memorization.
D3. Out-of-domain transfer (secondary): Big-Bench-Hard 3-task subset and ARC-Challenge, same decoding.
D4. Contamination check (pre-training, blocking): n-gram (8-gram) and embedding-similarity screen of every game target word/city and every system prompt against GSM8K/MATH/BBH/ARC items; any game item whose surface form appears in a benchmark item is removed from training lists and logged. Report contamination rates per arm.
D5. Style-control probe (secondary): a "GPT-4-style matching" diagnostic — measure response-style divergence (length, hedging, formatting) of each arm vs. its stage-1 teacher data, to detect whether gains track style imitation rather than reasoning [E1].

──────────────────────────────────────────
E. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
──────────────────────────────────────────
E1. Primary endpoint: Δaccuracy = post-training accuracy − same-checkpoint pre-training accuracy on D1 (pooled GSM8K+MATH-500, and reported per-benchmark). Primary hypotheses: H1: Arm1 > Arm2; H2: Arm1 > Arm3 (two co-primary comparisons).
E2. Seeds: 3 independent training seeds minimum (5 preferred for arms 1–3 only, given budget); pre/post evaluated per seed.
E3. Tests: per seed, question-level paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples) for Δaccuracy CIs; across seeds, mixed-effects logistic regression (correct ~ arm + (1|question) + (1|seed) + benchmark fixed effect) with planned contrasts; report Hedges' g effect sizes with seed-level CIs. Multiplicity: Holm correction across the two co-primary comparisons at α=0.05; all other comparisons (arm1 vs. 4/5/6; D3; D2-i) labeled exploratory. Decision rule: adversarial superiority claimed only if both H1 and H2 survive Holm correction in the predicted direction; if only one survives, report as partial evidence with explicit caveat.
E4. Secondary analyses: mediation-style check — does arm 1's in-game win-rate gain (D2-i) correlate with reasoning Δ across seeds (tests the hypothesized mechanism); arm 4 vs. arm 1 isolates the self-play contribution; arm 5 vs. arm 1 isolates the adversarial-opponent contribution; arm 6 bounds generic-data effects.

──────────────────────────────────────────
F. CONTROLS AND VALIDITY
──────────────────────────────────────────
E1 — Teacher-style leakage: all stage-1 data come from the same GPT-4 teacher with matched token budgets in every arm [B], so imitation-style content is equated; the D5 style probe detects residual style-driven gains; arm 6 (generic GPT-4-distilled SFT) bounds pure style distillation.
E2 — Topic-distribution differences across games: Taboo words and 20-Question topics are drawn from the SAME noun list [A5]; city list matched on frequency/familiarity; the same 80/20 split indices are reused across arms; token-budget matching removes length confounds.
E3 — Self-play instability: fixed episode budgets (not adaptive stopping) [A4]; rejection filtering of degenerate transcripts; KL-to-SFT-init anchor in distillation (implicit via SFT-only updates on filtered data); monitor per-round win rate, response length, and repetition rate; pre-registered early-stop rule only if degeneration is detected (applied symmetrically to all self-play arms).
E4 — Data-quantity confound: token-matched [B]; arm 4 shows imitation-only ceiling at the same tokens.
E5 — Judge bias across game types: rule-based hard-constraint checks where possible [A2]; judge prompts identical in structure; a 200-episode human-audit of judge agreement reported per arm.
E6 — Decoding/prompting confounds: identical eval prompts, few-shot exemplars, decoding [A8]; eval harness blind to arm identity.

──────────────────────────────────────────
G. FEASIBILITY (bounds under [A7]; NOT executed here — this workspace has no GPU, no ML stack, and no repository content)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Rollout volumes per arm: stage 1 ≈ 8k episodes × ~600 tokens ≈ 5M tokens; stage 2 ≈ 40k episodes × ~600 tokens ≈ 24M tokens; total ≈ 29M generated tokens per arm; ×5 arms ×3 seeds ≈ ~435M inference tokens. At ~1,500–2,500 tok/s aggregate on 8×A100 with vLLM-class serving, self-play generation is ≈ 50–80 GPU-hours total; SFT (≈29M tokens × 3 epochs per arm, 8B model full FT) ≈ 10–15 GPU-hours per arm → overall ≈ 200–400 GPU-hours, within the [A7] 640 GPU-hour budget. GPT-4 API: only stage 1 (≈5M tokens × 3 game arms + judge arbiter calls) ≈ 16–20M tokens ≈ $300–600 at GPT-4-class pricing; reduced-budget variant (2k episodes) ≈ $150.
Sensitivity note (per researcher instruction): under a 4× smaller budget, scale [A4] to 2k + 4×2.5k episodes; all contrasts remain internally valid because matching is preserved, but absolute effect sizes shrink and seed-level CIs widen — the design then detects only large (>2–3 point) accuracy differences; report as underpowered rather than null.
Environment constraint: this workspace (no GPU, no torch, network disabled, only task.json present) cannot execute any part of this design; the deliverable is a specification executable in principle by a team with the [A7] resources. No experiment was run and no results are claimed.

Assumption register recap: [A1]–[A8] are assumed defaults with sensitivity notes; the only fixed (task-context) requirement is the primary adversarial-vs-non-adversarial contrast. No SPAG mechanics in this document should be cited as source-verified.
