payload.answer:
EXPERIMENT DESIGN DOCUMENT — CycleNet for forecasting time series with periodic patterns (design-only; no experiments run, no results claimed)

Source-marking convention used throughout: [K] = claim from researcher's prior knowledge of CycleNet (Lin et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2409.18479; official RRWCycleNet repo) — "per paper (unverified against workspace)"; [W] = verified workspace/environment observation; [A] = design assumption needing no external source.

1) GOAL AND HYPOTHESIS
Goal: show that a CycleNet-style model — a learnable, cyclically reused recurrent cycle component (RCF) combined with a simple residual forecast head — can be implemented and trained to forecast time series with explicit periodic patterns, and attribute any accuracy gain specifically to the RCF module.
H1 (primary): On periodic data, CycleNet-style (RCF + linear residual head) outperforms cycle-agnostic linear-family baselines (vanilla Linear, DLinear) at horizons aligned with the cycle.
H2 (attribution): The gain is attributable to the cyclic reuse of the learnable component: "CycleNet minus RCF" ablations (including the per-position non-reused bias added per researcher request) should lose most of the advantage, especially at horizons spanning ≥1 full cycle.
H3 (sensitivity): Performance degrades gracefully when the specified cycle length is mismatched (±1, ±half-cycle), consistent with the cycle length being a hyperparameter [K].
Falsification criteria: if the RCF model fails to beat naive seasonal on hourly synthetic weekly-cycle data, or the minus-RCF ablation matches full CycleNet within seed noise, H1/H2 are not supported.

2) CYCLENET MECHANICS (all [K] "per paper, unverified against workspace"; workspace contains only task.json [W])
- RCF: a learnable parameter Q of shape [cycle_length, n_channels], globally shared across the whole series, indexed cyclically (position t → Q[t mod C]). [K]
- Removal/restoration, two experimental branches (per researcher instruction):
  • Branch "Removal-first" (Forecast-with-RCF): subtract Q[t mod C] from the look-back window; forecast the residual with the head; add Q back at forecast positions. Loss on the residual or on the final output; Q is trained jointly. [K]
  • Branch "Restoration-style" (model-first): train the head on the raw series, subtract the model's cyclic prediction at training positions and fit Q to the cyclic remainder; predict = head output − Q-style correction at target positions. [K — described as the alternative training variant in the paper]
- Cycle length C: per-dataset hyperparameter from domain knowledge (hourly → 24 daily or 168 weekly); not estimated from data in the primary track. [K]
- Head: deliberately minimal — single Linear (main) or 1–2-layer MLP (variant); this is a "linear-family" model where RCF carries the signal. [K]
- Normalization: instance normalization (per-window mean/std computed on the look-back, inverted after restoration; RevIN-style). Channel-independent multivariate processing. [K]
- Decoding: direct multi-step (one shot per horizon) is primary; iterated/recurrent decoding is out of scope, see §8/limitations. [A per researcher instruction]

3) DATA — SYNTHETIC IS THE PRIMARY TRACK (per researcher instruction)
3.1 Synthetic generator (primary, fully reproducible offline):
For each channel i: y_i(t) = trend_i(t) + Σ_{k=1..K} A_ik · sin(2π·k·t/C_i + φ_i) + ε(t), with
- Base periods: C ∈ {24 (daily), 168 (weekly)}; multi-period series combine both harmonics.
- 3 harmonics with random amplitudes/phases per channel (fixed seed); optional slow linear trend; Gaussian noise with controllable SNR ∈ {high, medium, low}; optional random phase shift per channel; optional amplitude modulation (slow multiplicative envelope) to break perfect stationarity.
- Grid: n_channels ∈ {1 (univariate), 7, 21}; series length 10,000–20,000 steps; deterministic seeds so every model sees identical data.
- A "phase-shift stress set": same periodicity but the phase of the cycle shifts midway — probes robustness of a globally shared Q [A].
3.2 Real benchmarks (optional extension, only "if data are provided" — network is disabled [W]): Electricity (C=168), Traffic (C=168), Solar (C=24/144), Weather (C=24), ETT family (C=24); official chronological splits and look-backs [K]. Not required for the core deliverable.

4) MODELS, BASELINES, ABLATION MATRIX
All models share: direct multi-step linear-style mapping, instance norm [K], channel independence, identical look-back and loss.
M1 Full CycleNet (Removal-first branch), Linear head — primary model.
M2 Full CycleNet (Restoration-style branch) — second branch per researcher instruction.
M3 Head variant: M1 with MLP head.
M4 Ablation A (no RCF): instance norm + Linear head only (= DLinear-equivalent). Isolates "anything cyclic at all".
M5 Ablation B (static bias, no cycle structure): learnable scalar/vector bias per channel added to the forecast, never indexed by position. [per original design, retained]
M6 Ablation C (per-position non-reused bias — researcher's addition): learnable per-position bias of shape [look-back+horizon, C] trained per position WITHOUT cyclic reuse across windows. This separates "there is a trainable offset" (M5) from "the offset is cyclically recycled" (M1). If M6 ≈ M1 and both ≫ M4/M5, the gain is from cyclic reuse specifically; if M6 ≈ M1 but M5 fails, any trainable offset suffices — a discriminating outcome either way. [A]
M7 Naive seasonal baseline: ŷ(t+h) = y(t+h−C) — the must-beat periodic floor; and naive seasonal-drift variant.
Baselines beyond ablations: vanilla Linear (M4 covers it), DLinear [K]; optional full LTSF backbones (PatchTST/TimesNet) only if compute/data permit — not required.
Ablation matrix (run for every dataset × horizon × seed): {M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M7} = 7 models.

5) PROTOCOL
- Splits: chronological 60/20/20 (train/val/test) for synthetic; identical across all models; cycle-aligned boundaries where feasible (split points at multiples of C) [A].
- Normalization: z-score per channel using train statistics only; instance (per-window) norm inside the model per [K]; identical pipeline for every model; no leakage (val/test never touched by scaler fitting or cycle fitting).
- Horizons: {24, 48, 96, 168} for C=168 data; {12, 24, 48, 72} for C=24 data. Look-back: 336 default, 96 as a secondary (sensitivity to look-back ≥ C matters for RCF indexing).
- Seeds: ≥3 seeds per cell (report mean ± std); paired comparisons on identical data/splits.
- Metrics: MSE and MAE per horizon; per-channel MSE on multivariate; also "cycle-phase" breakdown (error by h mod C) to verify errors concentrate where the cycle is mis-specified [A]. Primary metric: test MSE at horizon = C (168 or 24), where cyclic reuse should matter most.
- Training: Adam, MSE loss (Huber as robustness variant [K]), early stopping on val MSE with fixed patience, fixed max epochs, identical batch size/LR schedule for all models; cycle length recorded per dataset.
- Success criterion (confirmation): M1 beats M4 and M5 beyond seed std at h=C on ≥2 of 3 main synthetic configurations, and beats naive seasonal on at least the high-SNR config; M6 discriminating result reported as in §4. Refutation: M1 ≤ naive seasonal or M6 ≈ M4 (no attributable gain).

6) ANALYSIS PLAN
- Attribution of the RCF gain: (a) paired deltas M1−M4, M1−M5, M1−M6 with per-seed bootstrap CIs; (b) phase-resolved error curves — if RCF works, errors at forecast positions should follow the cycle profile of Q, so plot learned Q against the true generative harmonic (synthetic advantage: ground-truth cycle is known — direct visual/quantitative recovery check, e.g., correlation between learned Q and generative A·sin terms per channel); (c) branch comparison M1 vs M2 to see whether removal-first vs restoration-style training matters [researcher's requested branch design].
- Cycle-length sensitivity: run M1 with C′ ∈ {C−1, C, C+1, C/2, 2C, 12 (mismatched)} on one representative synthetic config; expect a valley at C = true period [H3]. Also report behavior of a "wrong-period" naive seasonal as a control.
- Phase-shift stress: compare M1 vs M4 on the phase-shift set; a globally shared Q should degrade more — this is an honest potential negative result, reported as such.
- Univariate vs multivariate: main track multivariate channel-independent; univariate as a robustness slice (M1 vs M4 only, to bound compute).

7) FEASIBILITY (verified environment facts [W]: 224-core Xeon Platinum 8570, ~2 TB RAM, CPU-only, Python 3.14.4; torch, numpy, pandas NOT installed; no local wheel cache; network disabled)
- Compute estimate (minimal grid): 3 synthetic configs × 4 horizons × 3 seeds × 7 models ≈ 250 runs; linear-family models at look-back 336 are tiny (thousands of parameters); on CPU, ~1–5 min/run for training + seconds for baselines ⇒ roughly 10–20 CPU-hours serially, trivially parallelizable across 224 cores ⇒ wall-clock well under 1 hour if parallelized. Cycle-length sensitivity adds ~7 × 3 = 21 runs; phase-shift set ~2 × 4 × 3 = 24 runs. Total budget ≈ 300 runs, comfortably within one CPU day even serially.
- Key risks and mitigations:
  R1 (highest): no torch/numpy and no network ⇒ pip install impossible in this sandbox. Mitigations: (a) researcher provisions wheels/dependencies; (b) otherwise implement the linear models + Adam + synthetic generator in pure Python (feasible: models are linear; Adam and backprop for a linear layer are ~100 lines; slow but the grid is small — estimate ~5–10× slowdown, still feasible); (c) as last resort restrict to M1/M4/M7 (the minimum that still answers H1/H2).
  R2: Python 3.14.4 may lack compatible wheels even if provided. Mitigation: prefer pure-Python path or a supplied older-interpreter environment.
  R3: RCF details mis-recalled [K unverified]. Mitigation: both branches implemented (M1/M2) and all cycle/head/norm choices exposed as config flags, so a wrong recall changes one flag, not the design; document explicitly as "per paper (unverified)".
  R4: Phase-shift stress produces a negative result for CycleNet — acceptable, report honestly; the design's contribution is attribution, not advocacy.
  R5: Seed noise swallows small effects on low-SNR synthetic data. Mitigation: ≥3 seeds, bootstrap CIs, high-SNR config as the primary confirmation cell.
- Smoke tests actually permitted and performed during design: NONE beyond environment probes above (CPU count, RAM, package absence). Any future run must be labeled "shape checks, not experiments".

8) ASSUMPTIONS AND UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTIES
Assumptions (explicitly not facts):
- A1: All CycleNet mechanics in §2 are correctly recalled from the paper/repo; per researcher instruction they are marked "per paper (unverified against workspace)" and cannot be confirmed from the workspace, which contains only task.json [W].
- A2: Cycle length is a hyperparameter (domain-given), with sensitivity scan secondary — not estimated from data.
- A3: Primary track is multivariate channel-independent with direct multi-step decoding; iterated/recurrent decoding is a limitations/future-work paragraph only (per researcher instruction): it changes error accumulation dynamics and could interact with RCF indexing, but is out of scope for this design.
- A4: Synthetic data with known generative cycles is an acceptable and sufficient basis for answering the research question; real benchmarks are an optional extension.
- A5: Budget is the minimal grid of §7 unless the researcher enlarges it; CPU-only execution is accepted, including the pure-Python contingency if dependencies cannot be provisioned.
Unresolved uncertainties:
- U1: The exact removal-vs-restoration formulation and loss placement in the original paper cannot be verified here; both branches are implemented, but neither is claimed to be the canonical one.
- U2: No researcher-supplied datasets exist; if real data later arrives, split/look-back conventions must be matched to the official benchmark protocol [K], which may shift absolute numbers relative to published results.
- U3: Whether the researcher requires exact reproduction of published CycleNet numbers (unlikely, given synthetic primary track) or only the attribution experiment (assumed).
- U4: Dependency provisioning (torch/numpy wheels) is outside my control; the pure-Python fallback path is designed but its runtime estimate is approximate.

INSPECCIÓN INICIAL — respuesta a los cuatro puntos solicitados (solo propuesta de enfoque, sin diseño final ni ejecución):

(1) ALCANCE según track.md
- El archivo track.md NO existe como archivo en el repositorio; su contenido está incrustado en task.json → "documents": {"track.md": "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."}
- Alcance confirmado: tarea de SOLO DISEÑO. No se requiere ejecutar experimentos, ni clonar/crear repositorios, ni usar cómputo para entrenamiento. No debo afirmar que se ejecutó ningún experimento.
- Detalles del entorno especificados: runtime bubblewrap (sandbox aislado), red DESHABILITADA (sin pip install ni descargas), repositorio /workspace (solo contiene task.json, 395 bytes), Python del sistema (verificado: Python 3.14.4, sin torch/pandas/numpy instalados), datasets: ninguno provisto, GPU deshabilitada, 224 CPUs disponibles (irrelevantes si no hay cómputo), presupuesto de pasos: 60, presupuesto de preguntas: 6. Nota explícita del entorno: "comandos exploratorios exitosos no constituyen prueba de un experimento completado".

(2) FUENTES SOBRE CYCLENET
- En el repositorio NO hay ninguna fuente, documento, paper o código que describa CycleNet. Lo único disponible es task.json con la pregunta de investigación.
- Consecuencia: la descripción técnica de CycleNet (residuo cíclico modelado con FCN/learnable queue indexada por periodicidad, combinación con modelo de fondo como MLP o modelo lineal, y el ciclo de periodicidad configurado —p. ej., cycle=24 para datos horarios, 7 para diarios) NO está documentada localmente. Todo detalle de configuración entraría como SUPUESTO, salvo que la investigadora aclare detalles por tópico (contexto: "The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic", y quedan 6 preguntas disponibles).

(3) ESQUELETO CONCEPTUAL DE DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL
- Datos: (a) sintéticos con periodicidad controlada (estacionalidad múltiple: p. ej., ciclo 24 y 168; ruido y tendencia ajustables) para validación controlada de que el residuo cíclico captura la estacionalidad; (b) dataset de referencia estándar del área si la investigadora lo autoriza/identifica (p. ej., benchmark tipo ETTh/ETTm, electricity, traffic — suponiendo disponibilidad, ya que no hay datasets locales y la red está deshabilitada).
- Implementación: módulo de residuo cíclico (cola aprendible de longitud = ciclo, indexada por fase t mod cycle) + modelo de fondo (baseline interno: modelo lineal y MLP) entrenado sobre el residuo; ventana de entrada→horizonte de salida estándar.
- Baselines para comparación: modelo lineal puro, MLP puro, y (opcional, según fuentes autorizadas) seasonal-naive y variantes sin descomposición cíclica.
- Métricas: MSE/MAE sobre horizontes de predicción definidos (96/168/336/720 pasos son los estándares del área, sujetos a confirmación); comparación por horizonte y por dataset; múltiples semillas para robustez.
- Plan de análisis: (i) verificar que CycleNet supera a sus propios backbones sin módulo cíclico (prueba de valor del residuo); (ii) análisis de ablation (cycle correcto vs. cycle incorrecto); (iii) análisis de sensibilidad a la longitud de ciclo declarada.

(4) SUPUESTOS CONSECUENTES E INCERTIDUMBRES
Supuestos (no exigidos por la tarea, adoptados por defecto):
- Longitud de ciclo conocida por dataset (p. ej., 24 en horario); el paper original de CycleNet (ICLR 2025) usa cycle configurable — este valor queda como supuesto.
- Horizontes estándar del benchmark (96/168/336/720) y ventanas de entrada tipo 96–720 pasos.
- Arquitectura del residuo como FCN/cola aprendible y backbones lineal/MLP.
- Presupuesto de cómputo no declarado: asumo entrenamientos pequeños/feasibles sin GPU si algún día se autoriza ejecución.
- Resultado empírico esperado (hipótesis, no resultado): CycleNet ≥ sus backbones puros en series con estacionalidad fuerte; ventaja mayor en ciclos correctos.
- Instalación de dependencias: imposible en este entorno (red deshabilitada), por lo que cualquier ejecución futura requeriría entorno distinto o fuentes puras-Python.

Incertidumbres abiertas:
- ¿Qué fuentes se consideran autorizadas para fijar la configuración (paper original, repositorio oficial, otra referencia)?
- ¿Se desea incluir datos reales de referencia o solo sintéticos?
- Presupuesto de cómputo y horizontes/ciclos a fijar definitivamente.
- ¿Qué backbones y datasets son preferidos por usted antes del diseño final?

Quedo a la espera de su aprobación del enfoque o de aclaraciones por tópico antes de redactar el diseño completo (stage=result).

payload.answer:
DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL COMPLETO — Implementación y entrenamiento de CycleNet para pronóstico de series temporales con patrones periódicos (tarea de SOLO DISEÑO; nada fue ejecutado y no se afirma lo contrario).

════════════════════════════════════════════
0. ALCANCE Y REGLAS DE LA TAREA
════════════════════════════════════════════
- track.md (contenido incrustado en task.json): "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required." → No se ejecutan experimentos, no se clonan repositorios, no se usa cómputo de entrenamiento. Este documento es únicamente un diseño experimental.
- Entorno verificado: Python 3.14.4 del sistema, sin torch/pandas/numpy, red deshabilitada, GPU deshabilitada, sin datasets locales. Consecuencia: toda configuración se especifica a nivel de diseño y las decisiones tomadas por conocimiento general del método se etiquetan como [SUPUESTO].
- Prohibición estricta: en ninguna parte de este diseño (ni en entregables futuros derivados) se afirmará que se ejecutó, entrenó o midió algo. Todos los "resultados esperados" son hipótesis.

════════════════════════════════════════════
1. PREGUNTA DE INVESTIGACIÓN
════════════════════════════════════════════
¿Cómo implementar y entrenar un modelo CycleNet para pronosticar series temporales con patrones periódicos, y qué valor aporta el módulo de residuo cíclico frente a sus backbones sin él?

════════════════════════════════════════════
2. DESCRIPCIÓN DEL MÉTODO (CON ETIQUETADO DE SUPUESTOS)
════════════════════════════════════════════
2.1 Componente central: residuo cíclico [SUPUESTO — por conocimiento general del método, p. ej., CycleNet (ICLR 2025); sin confirmación documental local]
- Se modela la estacionalidad de período fijo W (cycle) mediante una cola de parámetros aprendibles Q ∈ R^{W×D} (W = longitud del ciclo; D = dimensionalidad de canal, D=1 en univariado).
- Para el paso de tiempo t, la componente estacional estimada es Q[t mod W]. En ventana, el índice de fase de cada posición se obtiene del módulo de su índice temporal absoluto (o del offset de inicio de ventana), garantizando que la fase sea consistente entre entrenamiento y prueba.
- Pronóstico: ŷ(t+h) = Q[(t+h) mod W] + f_θ(ventana de entrada), donde f_θ es el backbone que modela el residuo x(t) − Q[t mod W] (y, si se habilita, la tendencia).
- Justificación: en series con estacionalidad fuerte y periódica, la mayor parte de la señal es predecible por fase; separarla en parámetros dedicados (uno por fase del ciclo) reduce la carga del backbone y evita que este "gaste" capacidad en memorizar el patrón repetitivo.
2.2 Backbones [SUPUESTO en cuanto a que CycleNet admite backbones intercambiables]: lineal (capa afín sobre ventana aplanada) y MLP (2–3 capas ocultas, activación ReLU/GELU). Ambos son estándar, baratos y permiten aislar el efecto del residuo.
2.3 Entrenamiento: pérdida MSE (o MAE) sobre horizonte H; optimizador Adam/AdamW; normalización z-score por serie (estadísticas del tramo de entrenamiento); parada temprana por MSE de validación. [SUPUESTOS: hiperparámetros concretos — lr, batch, epochs — se fijan en el diseño con valores típicos, no derivados de fuentes locales.]

════════════════════════════════════════════
3. DATOS
════════════════════════════════════════════
3.1 Núcleo (obligatorio): series SINTÉTICAS con estacionalidad controlada.
  - S1 (ciclo 24, diario-simulado): x(t) = A·sin(2πt/24 + φ) + β·t + ε(t), ε ~ N(0, σ²).
  - S2 (ciclo 168, semanal-simulado): x(t) = A1·sin(2πt/24) + A2·sin(2πt/168) + ε(t) (estacionalidad doble, para probar la capacidad del residuo con un único cycle declarado).
  - S3 (estacionalidad no-senoidal): forma de onda tipo "diente de sierra" o escalonada con ciclo 24, para evaluar residuos no triviales.
  - Factor de diseño controlable: A (amplitud), σ (ruido), β (tendencia), φ (fase). Longitud: p. ej., 8·168 = 1.344 puntos por serie (≥8 ciclos semanales), partición train/val/test 70/10/20 preservando orden temporal. [SUPUESTO: longitudes y proporciones.]
  - Justificación del núcleo sintético: la estacionalidad verdadera es conocida por construcción, lo que permite verificar en diseño que el mecanismo (fase t mod W) es el correcto y definir criterios de decisión sin ambigüedad — y es 100 % factible sin red ni GPU.
3.2 Rama opcional (condicionada a disponibilidad externa, NO accesible en este entorno): datasets de referencia estándar del área (ETTh1/h2/m, electricity, traffic, con particiones y protocolos estándar ya publicados). Se describe el protocolo idéntico al de 3.1, pero se declara explícitamente que en este entorno (red deshabilitada, sin datasets provistos) esta rama NO es ejecutable y queda condicionada a que la investigadora provea los datos o autorice otro entorno.

════════════════════════════════════════════
4. VARIABLES DE COMPARACIÓN Y CONTROLES
════════════════════════════════════════════
4.1 Sistemas en comparación:
  (A) CycleNet-lineal (residuo cíclico + backbone lineal)
  (B) CycleNet-MLP (residuo cíclico + backbone MLP)
  (C) Lineal puro (mismo backbone sin módulo cíclico)
  (D) MLP puro (idem)
  (E) Seasonal-naive (piso de referencia: predicción = valor observado hace exactamente W pasos; si supera a los modelos entrenados, el pipeline está mal)
4.2 Controles principales (requisito fijo 2):
  - Control 1 — backbone puro vs. backbone+residuo: (A) vs. (C) y (B) vs. (D), mismos datos, misma ventana/horizonte, mismas semillas. Aísla el valor del módulo cíclico.
  - Control 2 — ciclo correcto vs. incorrecto: CycleNet con W=24 en S1/S3 (correcto) vs. W=7, W=12, W=48 (incorrectos) y con W=168 en S2 vs. W=24 (correcto vs. insuficiente). Verifica que la ganancia proviene de la fase correcta y no solo de parámetros extra.
4.3 Justificación de los baselines: (C)/(D) responden "¿sirve el residuo?"; (E) establece el piso mínimo que todo modelo entrenado debe superar en series fuertemente estacionales; el par lineal/MLP responde "¿el residuo hace innecesaria la no-linealidad del backbone?".

════════════════════════════════════════════
5. MÉTRICAS Y PLAN DE ANÁLISIS (requisito fijo 3)
════════════════════════════════════════════
5.1 Métricas: MSE y MAE por horizonte, calculadas sobre el test set con datos des-normalizados (o normalizados, pero de forma consistente entre sistemas). Horizontes fijados: H ∈ {96, 168, 336, 720} pasos [decisión de la investigadora]; ventana de entrada L = 96 [SUPUESTO].
5.2 Semillas: 5 semillas independientes por celda del diseño (sistema × dataset × configuración de W); reporte de media y desviación estándar; comparación por intervalos/errores estándar de la media (prueba t pareada por semilla oWilcoxon, según se definan). [SUPUESTO: 5 semillas por presupuesto modesto.]
5.3 Criterios de decisión (pre-registrados):
  - D1 (valor del residuo): CycleNet-lineal supera a lineal puro y CycleNet-MLP supera a MLP puro en ≥ 3 de 4 horizontes, con mejora relativa ≥ 5 % en MSE [umbral SUPUESTO].
  - D2 (correcta identificación de fase): la caída de desempeño con W incorrecto debe ser ≥ 10 % en MSE respecto de W correcto; si no, el residuo no está capturando fase.
  - D3 (piso): todo modelo entrenado debe superar a seasonal-naive; si no, revisar pipeline antes de cualquier conclusión.
  - D4 (ablation de sensibilidad): curva MSE vs. W ∈ {7, 12, 24, 48, 168} con mínimo esperado en el W verdadero.
  - D5 (doble estacionalidad, S2): se analizará si un solo cycle (168) captura o no el patrón de 24; resultado descriptivo, sin criterio de éxito binario.
5.4 Diagnóstico cualitativo (diseño): visualización del vector Q aprendido contra la estacionalidad verdadera de S1 (correlación fase a fase) — verificación directa del mecanismo, sin requerir cómputo real para el diseño.

════════════════════════════════════════════
6. FACTIBILIDAD Y LIMITACIONES DEL ENTORNO (requisito fijo 4)
════════════════════════════════════════════
- Red deshabilitada: no es posible instalar torch/pandas/numpy (verificado: ModuleNotFoundError) ni descargar datasets. Escenario por defecto: implementación concebible en NumPy puro si algún día se autoriza ejecución, o implementación PyTorch solo como pseudocódigo/especificación en el diseño.
- Sin GPU: los modelos propuestos (lineal y MLP pequeño, series de ~1.500 puntos, ventanas de 96) son entrenables en CPU en minutos por corrida; estimación de cómputo del diseño completo: ≈ 3 datasets sintéticos × 5 sistemas × ~4 configuraciones de W × 5 semillas ≈ 250–300 corridas cortas; en CPU modesto, del orden de horas en total [SUPUESTO de factibilidad, no verificado por ejecución].
- Sin datasets locales: la rama de datos reales (3.2) queda bloqueada en este entorno.
- Límite de pasos del actor (60) y de preguntas (6): no limitan este entregable de diseño, pero condicionarían cualquier ejecución futura.

════════════════════════════════════════════
7. RESUMEN DE SUPUESTOS (TODOS EXPLÍCITOS)
════════════════════════════════════════════
[S1] Descripción técnica de CycleNet (cola aprendible indexada por t mod W + backbone sobre residuo) proviene de conocimiento general del método; sin fuente local que la confirme.
[S2] Backbones intercambiables lineal/MLP son admisibles en CycleNet.
[S3] Hiperparámetros de entrenamiento (lr, batch, epochs, early stopping) son valores típicos, no verificados.
[S4] Longitudes de series sintéticas, particiones 70/10/20 y ventana de entrada L=96 son elecciones de diseño.
[S5] 5 semillas y umbral de mejora del 5 % en D1 son convenciones adoptadas.
[S6] La estimación de factibilidad (horas de CPU) es un cálculo a priori, no una medición.
[S7] En la rama opcional, los protocolos de ETT/electricity/traffic se asumen según práctica estándar del área.
Ningún supuesto se presentará como confirmado documentalmente; el diseño declara que no se ejecutó nada y que toda expectativa (p. ej., que CycleNet supere a sus backbones) es hipótesis a validar solo si se autoriza ejecución futura en un entorno con dependencias.

payload.answer:
# 实验设计：实现并训练 CycleNet 以预测具有周期性的时间序列（设计型任务，不含已执行实验）

**标注约定**：【文件】= task.json / track.md 已写明的内容；【推断】= 基于公开文献与我的既有知识；【假设】= 设计中自行声明、需研究者确认或后续验证的合理默认值。

---

## 0. 任务边界（全部【文件】）

- task.json 明确：design-only 任务，不要求运行实验；"repositories and compute are not required"；track.md（其已知内容仅此一句）同义。
- 环境【文件】：bubblewrap 运行时、网络禁用、无 GPU、系统 Python、项目依赖未预装、datasets 为空。
- 因此本设计的交付物是：方法规格、可运行代码框架（结构级）、协议、分析计划，以及可行性边界说明。**本设计不声称任何实验已被执行。**

---

## 1. 研究问题与假设

**问题**（【文件】）：如何实现并训练 CycleNet 模型以预测具有周期模式的时间序列？

**可检验子假设**（【推断】，源自 CycleNet 公开论文 NeurIPS 2024 的核心主张）：
- H1：将长度为 Q 的可学习 recurrent cycle 分量从序列中显式建模后，通道独立线性残差头即可达到或超过同等容量复杂基线（DLinear）在强周期数据上的精度。
- H2：周期分量的收益随数据周期强度上升而增大（强周期 Electricity > 弱周期合成噪声数据）。
- H3：残差头近似为恒等/近恒等映射（CycleNet 的一个消融变体），在强周期数据上已能解释大部分精度。

---

## 2. CycleNet 方法规格（全部【推断】，关键细节列为 §9 待验证项）

给定多变量序列 X ∈ R^{T×D}，通道独立处理（对每个通道 d）：

1. **周期索引**：位置 t 的周期槽位为 `(t + offset) mod Q`。offset 为数据起点相对周期相位的偏移【推断：官方实现含起始相位偏移处理，具体方式待验证，见 V2】。
2. **Recurrent cycle 分量**：可学习参数 C ∈ R^{Q×D}（每通道一份）。前向：输入窗口 x 加上（训练时）对应槽位的 C；输出侧从预测 y 中减去对应槽位的 C。训练目标等价于：模型预测去除周期分量后的残差，推理时再加回。槽位映射对输入窗口的每个时间步与预测窗口的每个未来步分别计算【推断：预测窗口的槽位按其在原始时间轴上的绝对位置取模，需按切分与窗口起始对齐方式确定，见 V3】。
3. **残差预测头**：单个线性层（输入维度 L，输出维度 H），通道间共享或逐通道独立【推断：论文主结果为共享线性层；逐通道为可选变体，作为消融 A3】。
4. **初始化**：C 初始化为 0【推断：待验证，见 V1】，使初始模型等价于纯线性模型。
5. **损失**：MSE；优化器 Adam/AdamW，学习率约 1e-3~1e-2 范围网格【假设】，早停基于验证集。
6. **复杂度**：参数量约 Q×D + L×D（共享头）或 Q×D + L×D×C_head，为极轻量模型；单 CPU 可训练【推断：参数量级算术】。

**周期长度 Q 的选择依据**（【推断】+【假设】）：
- 小时级数据（Electricity、ETTh1/2）：主设置 Q=24（日周期）；敏感性分析 Q=168（周周期）。
- 15 分钟级（ETTm1/2）：Q=96（日周期）。
- 依据：领域常识 + 论文默认；正式设计中补充 ACF/FFT 峰值检测作为数据驱动验证步骤【假设：若数据可得则执行，否则纸面论证】。

---

## 3. 数据场景

| 数据 | 频率 | Q（主设置） | 用途 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Electricity (ECL) | 小时级 | 24 | 主数据集，日周期强【推断：公开基准惯例】 |
| ETTh1/ETTh2 | 小时级 | 24 | 次要，跨域稳健性 |
| ETTm1/ETTm2 | 15 分钟 | 96 | 频率泛化 |
| 合成周期数据 | 任意 | 24/96 | 禁网环境下的概念验证与机制消融（见 §7） |

**数据可得性（如实声明）**：【文件】datasets 为空且网络禁用，真实 Electricity/ETT 无法在本环境获取。设计按两条轨道：轨道 A（纸面完整协议，面向有数据的环境）；轨道 B（本环境可执行的降级验证：合成数据 + 纯 Python/极小依赖实现，验证周期分量学习机制，非精度主张）。

**切分协议**（【推断】：沿用 LTSF 公开基准惯例）：Electricity 按 12/4/4 个月、ETTh1/2 按 8/1/1（切分点 12/20月、13/14月边界日期）、ETTm 按 10/2/2 个月固定切分；标准化仅用训练集统计量。

---

## 4. 对比设置

**基线**（【推断】公开方法，超参沿用各论文默认，列为待核对项 V4）：
1. Seasonal-naive（周期 s=Q 的朴素预测）——下界。
2. DLinear——同为线性、通道独立，最直接可比（无显式周期建模）。
3. PatchTST——强 CNN/Transformer 代表，检验轻量模型的竞争力。
4. Naive repeat（最后值重复）——另一弱基线。

**消融**（对应假设检验）：
- A1：CycleNet 完整 vs 去除周期分量（仅线性头）——直接检验 H1，等价于"DLinear 变体 + 相同协议"。
- A2：C 固定为 0（不可学习）vs 可学习——检验周期分量是否确实被学习而非冗余。
- A3：共享线性头 vs 逐通道头。
- A4：Q 取 24 vs 168 vs 96（敏感性）；另设故意错配 Q（如 Q=12）检验错配退化。
- A5（合成数据专用）：不同周期强度（信噪比梯度）下 A1 差距的变化，检验 H2。

**控制变量**：所有模型使用相同的窗口/预测长度（L=96；H∈{96,192,336,720}）、相同的标准化、相同的早停与随机种子集合（≥3 个种子报均值±标准差）【假设：种子数与预算相关，见 §7】。

---

## 5. 训练与评估协议（【推断】+【假设】）

- 输入窗口 L=96；预测长度 H∈{96,192,336,720}；滑动窗口步长 1 生成样本，训练/验证/测试窗口互不泄漏（按切分点独立生成）。
- 优化：AdamW，lr ∈ {5e-4, 1e-3, 5e-3}，batch size 32~256，epoch ≤ 30，早停 patience=5（验证 MSE）【假设：默认预算，见 §7】。
- 指标：MSE 与 MAE，逐通道平均；报告每个 (数据, H) 组合。
- 显著性：对每组合做种子间配对比较（CycleNet vs DLinear，Wilcoxon 或配对 t 检验）【假设】。
- 溯源：记录每个数字对应的模型、种子、数据版本与代码提交号（设计中规定，未执行）。

---

## 6. 分析计划

1. 主表：各数据 × H 的 MSE/MAE（CycleNet vs 4 基线）。
2. 消融表：A1–A5。
3. 机制分析：可视化学习到的 C 的一个周期剖面（如 Electricity 某通道的 24 点曲线），检查是否符合已知日周期形态【推断：论文中做过类似可视化】。
4. 残差诊断：训练后残差的 ACF，检验周期是否被移除。
5. 失败模式：弱周期/非平稳段上 CycleNet 与纯线性的差距方向。

---

## 7. 可行性边界（禁网、无 GPU）

【文件】环境限制 → 三层可行性声明：
- **完整实验（轨道 A）**：不可在本环境执行；仅作为面向有数据、有 GPU 环境的协议。算力估算【假设】：CycleNet/DLinear 参数量 1e4–1e6 级，Electricity 全配置（4 基线 × 4 H × 3 种子）在单张消费级 GPU 上估计数小时内完成；该数字为推断性估算，非实测。
- **降级验证（轨道 B，本环境可行）**：用 numpy 若不可得则纯 Python 实现极简 CycleNet（合成 y = 周期分量 + 线性趋势 + 噪声），验证 (a) 周期索引与 offset 逻辑正确性（单元测试级）、(b) 梯度下降能学到 C。**这仅验证机制，不构成对 H1–H3 的实证**。依赖方面：本环境当前无 numpy【文件-实测】，轨道 B 需离线获取依赖或降级到纯 Python 小规模实现。
- **单 CPU 规模估算**：224 核 CPU【文件】下，若研究者提供数据，DLinear/CycleNet 级别的单次训练在 CPU 上可行（线性模型，分钟级/次），PatchTST 则不现实——设计中将 PatchTST 标注为"仅在有 GPU 的外部环境执行"。

**合规声明**：本设计未运行任何实验，未产生任何结果性主张。

---

## 8. 交付物清单

1. 本设计文档（含【文件】/【推断】/【假设】标注）。
2. CycleNet 最小实现代码框架（结构级：cycle index 计算、C 参数、残差头、训练循环骨架）。
3. 轨道 B 的合成数据概念验证脚本骨架（不执行）。
4. 待验证项清单（§9）与证据摘要（随本 handoff 一并提交）。

## 9. 待验证项（仅凭既有知识无法核对，禁网所致）

- **V1**：C 是否以 0 初始化、以及是否同时作用于输入端（加）与输出端（减）。
- **V2**：起始相位 offset 的确切处理方式（窗口起点对齐 vs 绝对时间戳对齐）。
- **V3**：预测窗口未来步的周期槽位映射规则（是否需要日历特征辅助跨切分边界对齐）。
- **V4**：DLinear/PatchTST 引用超参与官方仓库是否一致。
- **V5**：Q=168 等非主设置在论文中的报告情况。
- 缓解：若研究者可提供论文/官方仓库副本（离线拷贝），先核对 V1–V3 再定稿实现；否则在设计中明确标注这些为"按合理推断实现，需对照官方实现复核"。

---

## 证据摘要（所依据的事实）

1. 【文件】task.json 原文：问题、design-only 声明、track.md 引用内容（"Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."）。
2. 【文件/实测】/workspace 目录仅含 task.json；无 track.md 文件实体、无代码、无数据。
3. 【文件/实测】环境：network disabled、gpu_enabled=false、cpu_affinity_count=224、datasets=[]、系统 Python。
4. 【实测】`python3 -c "import numpy, pandas, torch"` 失败（ModuleNotFoundError: numpy），依赖未预装。
5. 【推断】CycleNet 结构、DLinear/PatchTST 基线设定、LTSF 切分与评估惯例：来自公开文献既有知识，禁网下无法在线核对，已在 §9 列为待验证项。

(2) Proposed high-level experimental approach:
- CycleNet components to specify: (a) Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) module — a learnable cycleLen × d parameter matrix indexed by cyclic position (t mod cycleLen), added at the input and subtracted from model output, with normalization/instancenorm around it; (b) a lightweight residual backbone (Linear/DLinear-style, optionally small MLP) mapping lookback window L → horizon H in direct multi-step mode; (c) RevIN-style normalization for distribution shift.
- Baselines: the same backbone without RCF (isolates the cycle component's contribution), Seasonal-Naive, and a Fourier-feature/periodic-average baseline; optionally RCF+MLP.
- Data: synthetic periodic series with controllable period/amplitude/trend/noise (for controlled validation of the cycle component) plus, if permitted, a standard public periodic benchmark (e.g., hourly electricity/traffic) — flagged as assumed, not confirmed.
- Split/backtesting: chronological 70/10/20 split aligned to period boundaries; expanding-window backtesting with rolling origins and a fixed horizon (e.g., H=96 steps).
- Evaluation: MSE and MAE per horizon and averaged, ≥3 seeds with mean ± std; ablations for RCF on/off and correct vs. shuffled cycle index; robustness checks for phase shift and multiple coexisting periods.

(3) Consequential assumptions and uncertainties:
- CONFIRMED from repository: design-only task; no repos/compute required; no datasets or starter code present; no dependencies preinstalled.

payload.answer:
CYCLENET FOR PERIODIC TIME SERIES — FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (paper design; no experiment run or claimed)

SCOPE STATUS: Design-only. CONFIRMED workspace facts: /workspace contains only task.json; embedded track.md states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"; Python 3.14.4 system environment with no ML packages installed; network disabled; no GPU. Everything below beyond these facts is a design assumption or a stated default, labeled as such.

=====================================================================
1. HYPOTHESIS
=====================================================================
Primary hypothesis: adding a Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) component — a cycle-indexed learnable periodic matrix — to a lightweight residual backbone improves multi-step forecasting accuracy on series with periodic patterns, relative to the same backbone without RCF, with the improvement growing with (a) the strength of the periodic component and (b) longer forecast horizons.

=====================================================================
2. MODEL: CYCLENET COMPONENTS TO BE SPECIFIED
=====================================================================
All components are design specifications (assumed architecture follows the published CycleNet/RCF description; no reference implementation exists in the workspace — assumption flagged).

2.1 Residual Cycle Forecasting (RCF) module
- Learnable parameter matrix W_c ∈ R^{cycleLen × d} (cycleLen = period length in time steps; d = number of channels/series).
- At training and inference, for each sample with lookback window covering timestamps t₀ … t₀+L−1 and forecast horizon t₀+L … t₀+L+H−1:
  - Input augmentation: x_input = x_raw + W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the lookback window]
  - Output correction: ŷ = y_backbone(x_input) − W_c[(t mod cycleLen) indices of the horizon window]
  i.e., the periodic component is added back for the forecast region; the backbone only models the residual (trend/noise/irregular part).
- W_c is trained jointly with the backbone by backprop (it is a plain parameter tensor — gradient flows through both the input-add and output-subtract paths).
- Initialization: zeros (so at step 0 the model reduces to the plain backbone; the periodic structure is learned). Rationale: avoids a random-periodicity prior corrupting early training; assumption, stated as a default.

2.2 Normalization wrapper (RevIN-style instancenorm)
- Per-window: subtract the lookback-window mean, divide by its std (per channel), run backbone+RCF, then de-normalize the output (add mean, multiply std). Applied around the whole model. Mitigates level shifts; standard practice; assumed default.

2.3 Residual backbone (two variants)
- B1 "Linear": single learnable linear map from flattened L·d input to H·d output (per-channel shared or channel-independent; default: channel-independent linear, matching DLinear-style simplicity).
- B2 "MLP": L·d → hidden (256) → H·d, one hidden layer, ReLU. Rationale for keeping both: tests whether RCF's benefit is orthogonal to backbone capacity.

=====================================================================
3. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (1): PERIOD / CYCLE-LENGTH SELECTION
=====================================================================
Primary strategy:
- Synthetic data (primary protocol): cycleLen is KNOWN a priori by construction (it is a generation parameter) and supplied to the model. This removes period-estimation error from the primary comparison, isolating the RCF mechanism.
- Real-data extension (optional, clearly labeled): cycleLen estimated from data by FFT periodogram + ACF confirmation on the training split only (no test leakage). Primary estimator: dominant FFT peak over the training series after detrending, validated by checking ACF local maximum at the candidate lag; ties broken toward the shorter candidate consistent with domain priors (e.g., 24 for hourly data). This is a stated default procedure, not an executed result.

Fallback behavior under mis-specified periods:
- Robustness experiment (in-scope, synthetic): inject the model with a deliberately wrong cycleLen (true period p, supplied period p' ∈ {p/2, 2p, p±1}) and measure degradation. Expected (hypothesis-supporting) pattern: graceful degradation when p' is an integer multiple/divisor of p (RCF can still express the true period) and larger degradation when p' is an incompatible near-neighbor (p±1).
- If period estimation is uncertain on real data, the design prescribes selecting cycleLen on the validation split by grid over ACF/FFT candidates (validation-set model selection — no test-set tuning), with the fallback default cycleLen = 24 for hourly / 7·24 for daily-aggregated data when no dominant peak is found (assumed defaults).

=====================================================================
4. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (2): DATASET SCOPE
=====================================================================
PRIMARY — synthetic protocol (no external data needed, consistent with confirmed "repositories not required"):
- Generator: y_t = trend_t + A·sin(2π t / p + φ) + optional secondary harmonic + AR(1) or iid noise + optional level shift mid-series.
- Grid over factors: period p ∈ {24, 48, 168}; amplitude-to-noise ratio SNR ∈ {0.5, 2, 10} (low/medium/high periodicity); trend strength ∈ {none, linear}; n_channels d ∈ {1, 7}; series length 10,000 steps (≈ 5,600/800/3,600 train/val/test at 70/10/20, period-boundary-aligned). Full grid = 3×3×2×2 = 36 configurations; each run is cheap (Section 9).
- Seeds: 3 generation seeds × 3 training seeds per configuration (generation seed controls phase φ and noise realization; training seed controls init/order).

OPTIONAL EXTENSION (clearly labeled; described but not required and not executed): one public hourly dataset (electricity or traffic, standard long-horizon TSF benchmarks) with 70/10/20 chronological split, H ∈ {24, 48, 96}, cycleLen from Section 3 estimator. This requires data the workspace does not have; it is included as a design addendum only.

=====================================================================
5. RESOLVED DESIGN CHOICE (3): HYPERPARAMETER DEFAULTS (stated defaults with rationale)
=====================================================================
- Lookback L = 2·cycleLen (e.g., L=48 for p=24). Rationale: two full periods give the RCF index enough coverage of all cycle positions while keeping the backbone input small; ablation over L ∈ {1·p, 2·p, 4·p} is included.
- Horizon H = 96 (4 periods for p=24), with per-horizon reporting at H ∈ {24, 48, 96}. Rationale: standard long-horizon TSF convention; multiple horizons let us test the "benefit grows with horizon" prediction.
- Model sizes: Linear backbone L·d → H·d (per channel); MLP hidden width 256. Parameter counts are small (<0.5M) by design — the claim under test is that periodicity handling, not capacity, drives improvement.
- Training: Adam, lr = 1e-3 (Linear) / 5e-4 (MLP), cosine decay to 1e-5, batch size 64 (sliding windows), max 20 epochs with early stopping on validation MSE (patience 5). Loss: MSE (matches primary metric). These are conventional defaults; a small lr sweep {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} is prescribed on one synthetic config only, to bound tuning cost.
- All hyperparameters fixed across model variants so comparisons are apples-to-apples; validation split used for early stopping only.

=====================================================================
6. CONTROLS AND COMPARISONS (distinct sections, per researcher instruction)
=====================================================================
6.1 Baseline comparisons (external references — different methods, same data/protocol):
  A. Backbone-only (Linear, no RCF) — the critical comparison; identical backbone isolates the cycle module.
  B. Backbone-only MLP.
  C. Seasonal-Naive: ŷ_{t+h} = x_{t+h−k·p} (repeat last observed period); strong periodic-data baseline.
  D. Periodic-mean baseline: per-(position-in-cycle) training-split mean, extended over the horizon.
  E. (Optional extension only) published numbers / standard implementations on the real benchmark.
6.2 Ablations (internal to CycleNet — same architecture, one factor changed):
  A1. RCF removed (≡ baseline A; included in both lists for completeness).
  A2. RCF present but with cycle index randomly shuffled per batch (destroys the period↔position alignment while preserving parameter count) — tests that the benefit comes from correct cycle indexing, not extra parameters.
  A3. Correct cycleLen vs. mis-specified cycleLen (Section 3 fallback study).
  A4. Lookback length L ∈ {1p, 2p, 4p} with RCF fixed.
  A5. Normalization wrapper on/off.
6.3 Controls on the data protocol itself: SNR=0.5 (near-dominant noise) configurations serve as an "adversarial" control where RCF should help little or not at all; a pure-noise (no periodicity) control configuration verifies RCF does not hallucinate periodic structure when none exists (performance should match baseline A within noise).

=====================================================================
7. ANALYSIS PLAN
=====================================================================
Primary metric: MSE on the test split; secondary: MAE. Reported per horizon and averaged, mean ± std over 3 training seeds; generation seeds pooled or reported separately (decision: report both; per-generation-seed pairing is used for significance testing).
Statistical testing: paired comparison across the 9 (3 gen × 3 train) seeds per configuration; Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-test (whichever is appropriate after checking seed-pair differences), α = 0.05, with Holm correction across the 3 horizons.

Result patterns SUPPORTING the hypothesis:
  (i) A (backbone+RCF) beats A1 (backbone alone) on MSE at all horizons on medium/high-SNR configs, with the gap widening in H and in SNR — the dose–response signature.
  (ii) A beats A2 (shuffled index) by a margin similar to the A vs. A1 gap — confirming the cycle alignment is the active ingredient.
  (iii) On the no-periodicity control, A ≈ A1 (no spurious harm) — specificity.
  (iv) A3 fallback pattern: mild degradation at p' ∈ {p/2, 2p}, larger at p' = p±1 — consistent with the RCF mechanism.

Patterns REFUTING / weakening the hypothesis:
  (i') A ≈ A1 across all SNRs and horizons (RCF adds nothing beyond what L=2p lookback already provides).
  (ii') A2 ≈ A (benefit is from extra parameters, not alignment).
  (iii') A < A1 only at low SNR or shows instability across seeds (high variance) — benefit not robust.
  (iv') Mis-specified periods cause catastrophic failure rather than graceful degradation — fragility undermines the method's practical value.
Decision rule: the hypothesis is supported only if (i) holds with Holm-corrected significance at H=96 on ≥2 of 3 SNR levels AND (ii) holds directionally; otherwise the design treats RCF's benefit as unestablished.

=====================================================================
8. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN (to be written, not executed)
=====================================================================
Deliverables: (a) single-file NumPy/PyTorch-CPU implementation of RCF + backbones + generator + evaluation loop; (b) config file enumerating the 36-configuration grid + ablations; (c) results schema (per-run JSON: config, seed, horizon, MSE/MAE, parameter count, wallclock); (d) aggregation/plotting script (per-horizon MSE vs. SNR curves, ablation tables).
Code structure: `rcf.py` (module), `backbones.py`, `data.py` (generator + windowing + splits), `train.py`, `evaluate.py`, `aggregate.py`. Windowing must compute cycle indices from absolute timestamps so phase is consistent across train/test windows (a common subtle bug the design explicitly guards against; a unit check is prescribed: RCF output on a noise-free pure sinusoid should equal the sinusoid up to backbone error).

=====================================================================
9. FEASIBILITY STATEMENT (consistent with confirmed environment)
=====================================================================
- Confirmed: CPU-only, 224 cores, no GPU, no preinstalled packages; network disabled. Therefore the design mandates dependency installation as an explicit setup step (torch CPU, numpy, pandas — assumption: permitted install; if not, a pure-NumPy fallback implementation of the Linear backbone + RCF is specified, which is fully feasible since RCF is a learnable matrix trained by least squares/gradient descent and the Linear backbone is a single affine map trainable with closed-form ridge or simple SGD).
- Scale estimate (design estimate, not a measurement): per synthetic run — ~7,000 training windows, model <0.5M params, 20 epochs max; a NumPy implementation should train in <1–2 minutes per run; a PyTorch-CPU run in <30 s per epoch worst case, so minutes per run. Full grid (36 configs × 3 gen × 3 train seeds × ~4 model variants incl. ablations ≈ 1,300 runs) at ~2 min each ≈ 43 CPU-hours, trivially parallelizable across 224 cores → well under 1 hour wallclock with process-level parallelism. Memory per run is dominated by the window tensor (≈ 7,000 × 48 floats ≈ a few MB) — negligible.
- Optional public-benchmark extension would need external data acquisition and is therefore explicitly out of the guaranteed scope given the confirmed network-disabled environment; it is feasible only if data files are supplied.
- Everything above is a feasibility estimate based on standard complexity reasoning; no run has been performed and no runtime has been measured.

=====================================================================
10. CONFIRMED vs. ASSUMED — SUMMARY TABLE
=====================================================================
CONFIRMED (from workspace inspection):
  • Design-only scope; repositories and compute not required (track.md in task.json).
  • No datasets, code, or CycleNet references in /workspace.
  • CPU-only (224 cores), no GPU, network disabled, Python 3.14.4, no ML packages installed.

ASSUMED / STATED DEFAULTS (require no further confirmation for a paper design, but are not workspace facts):
  • CycleNet architecture follows the published RCF description (learnable cycleLen×d matrix, add-at-input/subtract-at-output, joint training).
  • Hyperparameter defaults in Section 5 (L=2p, H=96, lr, epochs, batch size).
  • Synthetic generator parameterization in Section 4; public benchmark as optional extension.
  • Period-selection procedure and mis-specification behavior (Section 3).
  • Runtime estimates in Section 9 are analytical, not measured.

This design makes no claim that any experiment, training run, or measurement has been performed.

payload.answer:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design only — no execution, no results claimed)

Title: Ablation study of dynamic memory lookup and unit representations in InfLLM

=====================================================================
1. RATIONALE
=====================================================================
Question decomposed: "How critical are X (dynamic context memory lookup) and Y (choice of unit representations) to InfLLM's performance?" Criticality is operationalized as the performance drop each component's degradation causes, and whether the two components interact.

Mapping of the assumed InfLLM mechanism to the two factors:
- Factor A targets the *selection policy*: which memory blocks a query token attends to. InfLLM (as assumed) computes, per query token, a key and scores it against block keys, selecting top-k blocks, plus an always-on local sliding window. Removing or degrading this policy changes the information routing without changing what is stored.
- Factor B targets the *content of the routing signal*: how each block is compressed into a unit representation (assumed: a block reader using a representative token plus learnable gating). Changing this changes the fidelity of the key/value signal used for both selection (via block keys) and reading (via block contents). B alone changes representation; A alone changes selection; A×B captures whether a good representation is only useful when selection is query-conditioned (the hypothesized interaction).

Independent vs. joint contributions: a 4×4 factorial (4 levels of A × 4 levels of B) lets us estimate (i) main effect of lookup policy, (ii) main effect of representation scheme, and (iii) the A×B interaction — e.g., whether mean-pooled keys are nearly as good as block-reader keys under full top-k selection but collapse under k=1, which would indicate the representation's criticality is contingent on lookup precision.

EXPLICIT ASSUMPTIONS ABOUT INFLLM (unverified; to be confirmed from the paper/reference implementation before any run):
(A1) Base model: Llama-2-7B with InfLLM's trained adaptation parameters. Unverified — scale and base checkpoint are assumptions.
(A2) Mechanism: context split into fixed-size memory blocks (block size assumed in the thousands of tokens; exact value unverified); per-block unit representation computed by a block reader using a representative token + learnable gating; query-conditioned top-k selection (k small, exact value unverified) over block keys; local sliding window always active.
(A3) Training-free inference: block-selection machinery is learned on short sequences (~8k tokens, assumed) and applied zero-shot to long contexts; therefore factor manipulations are implementable at inference time without retraining.
(A4) Tasks: long-context LM perplexity and retrieval/QA suites are the standard evaluation surface.
Any mismatch between these assumptions and the actual implementation (e.g., learned top-k thresholds, different block-reader construction) requires arm redefinition but not redesign of the factorial structure.

=====================================================================
2. FULL ARM SPECIFICATION
=====================================================================
Factor A — dynamic memory lookup policy (4 levels):
- A1 (reference): Full InfLLM. Query-conditioned top-k selection over block keys + local sliding window. Everything as assumed from the paper.
- A2 (removal / dense): No dynamic lookup. Attention over ALL blocks uniformly — i.e., naive long-context attention restricted to the same block partition, same local window. This isolates the value of selective routing given the same stored memory.
- A3 (static/position-based, budget-matched): Select the same number of blocks as A1 (top-k), but by position (blocks nearest the query) or by a fixed, query-independent pattern. Same compute and same number of attended blocks as A1 — this is the key OOD-confound control (see §3).
- A4 (random, budget-matched): Select k blocks uniformly at random per query token (fixed seed per example). Same budget as A1, selection signal destroyed.
- A5 (budget sweep, optional secondary): top-k ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} with A1's policy, to map the sensitivity curve of selection precision. Analyzed as a dose-response sub-study, not part of the 4×4 core.

Factor B — unit representation scheme (4 levels):
- B1 (reference): Original block-reader unit representations (representative token + learnable gating), as assumed.
- B2: Mean-pooled block encodings — mean over block token hidden states, projected to the key space.
- B3: Single-token keys — the block's representative token's hidden state only, no gating.
- B4 (floor control): Degenerate keys — frozen random projections of block content (or even fixed random vectors per block index), refreshed per seed. Establishes the selection-signal floor: performance when block keys carry no task-relevant signal.

Nuisance scale-matching (critical for clean B attribution): substituting keys changes their norm/scale, which after softmax temperature acts as an effective temperature change, not just a signal change. For B2–B4, normalize replacement keys to match the L2 norm distribution of B1 keys (per-layer, per-head if applicable), and verify empirically that the top-k selection entropy distribution over blocks is comparable for B1 vs. B2 on a calibration subset before the main run. Additionally: value/pathway (what is actually attended to after selection) is held IDENTICAL across B arms — only the routing key changes — so B isolates the representation's role in routing, not in reading. (If the assumed block reader also affects the read-out pathway, add a B1-read/B2-route cross arm to decompose this; treat as a design contingency.)

Core factorial: A1–A4 × B1–B4 (16 arms) + A5 sweep (5 extra runs at B1, optionally one at B2). All arms share identical block partitioning, block size, local window size, KV storage, sampling/decoding settings.

=====================================================================
3. CONTROLS
=====================================================================
- Sliding-window-only baseline: local window active, memory machinery disabled entirely. Establishes what the memory adds at all.
- Short-context reference: base model (or InfLLM within its trained context length, assumed 8k) evaluated on truncated versions of the same inputs — separates "long-context ability" from "short-context competence."
- Fixed geometry: block size, number of stored blocks, local window, and total attention budget held constant across all arms so effects are attributable to policy/representation, not to compute or coverage.
- OOD-regime confound control: A2 (uniform attention over all blocks) both removes selection AND changes the attention distribution regime. A3 and A4 keep the regime (same sparse top-k structure, same budget) and change only the selection signal; the contrast A1 − A3/A4 measures the value of *informed* selection, while A1 − A2 additionally includes any regime shift. If A2 performs similarly to A3/A4, the regime confound is negligible; if A2 performs markedly differently, interpret its effect as "selection + regime" jointly and rely on A3/A4 for the pure selection effect.
- Seeds: ≥3 seeds per arm where stochasticity exists (A4 explicitly seeded; decoding greedy/deterministic for generation tasks). Report seed-level variance; for deterministic arms, replicate over dataset subsamples.
- Order/position sanity check: verify block scores vary with query position across contexts in A1 (a positive control that selection is actually dynamic and non-degenerate before ablations).
- Calibration gate (from §2): key-scale matching verified on a held-out calibration slice; if B2/B4 entropy distributions are wildly different, re-tune normalization before main runs.

=====================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN
=====================================================================
Metrics per suite:
- Long-context LM: per-token perplexity / NLL as a function of context length (bucketed, e.g., 4k–64k+), plus local vs. distant token NLL splits (distant-token NLL is the most sensitive to memory behavior; local should be nearly flat across arms — an internal sanity check).
- Needle-in-a-haystack: exact retrieval accuracy by depth × context-length grid.
- QA/summarization (LongBench/ZeroSCROLLS-style): task metric (F1/EM/ROUGE), with input-length stratification.

Statistical analysis:
- Two-way factorial ANOVA-style decomposition (or mixed-effects model with seed/dataset random effects) on each metric: main effect of A, main effect of B, A×B interaction, with bootstrap CIs (cluster bootstrap over documents).
- Effect sizes reported as absolute deltas vs. A1×B1 and as Cohen's d-style standardized effects; paired comparisons (same inputs across arms) to maximize power.
- Interaction interpretation: e.g., if B2 ≈ B1 under A1 but B2 ≪ B1 under A4/A3, representation quality matters only when selection is dynamic — the joint-contribution answer. If main effect of A is large and B effects are flat, lookup is critical and representation is redundant; if B4 (random keys) ≈ B1, the selection signal itself is not doing the work (suspicious — triggers a mechanism audit); if A3/A4 ≈ A1, "dynamic" lookup per se adds nothing beyond budget-matched static selection.
- Decision criteria (pre-registered thresholds, to be finalized once baseline variance is known): a component is "critical" if its ablation costs >10% relative on retrieval accuracy or >0.2 nats/token on distant-token NLL with CIs excluding zero, across ≥2 task suites; "redundant" if deltas are within noise (<2% / <0.05 nats); intermediate results reported as graded sensitivity rather than forced into binary labels. The A×B interaction is deemed meaningful only if its effect size exceeds the sum of marginal main-effect predictions with CI excluding zero.
- A5 sweep analyzed as monotonic sensitivity of performance to k; the k at which performance saturates indicates how much selection precision is needed.

=====================================================================
5. FEASIBILITY AND RISKS
=====================================================================
- Primary design is inference-only: justified because (per assumption A3) InfLLM is trained for short contexts and applied training-free to long ones, so ablations of the selection policy and key construction are implementable by modifying inference code, not weights. Cost: 16 core arms + 5 sweep runs + 2 controls ≈ 23 configurations; at 7B, 32k-token contexts, a few hundred to a few thousand examples per suite — nontrivial but tractable on a single A100-class GPU over days. If any ablation requires retraining (e.g., if the block reader is entangled with read-out in the actual implementation), cost grows by orders of magnitude; the trained-variant path (re-fitting adaptation parameters per arm on the assumed 8k training recipe) is listed as an extension, not the primary design.
- Scale assumptions: 7B primary. A small proxy (e.g., 1B-class model with the same mechanism re-implemented) may be used for smoke tests only (verifying arm implementations, calibration gates); it is explicitly NOT conclusion-supporting, because block-selection behavior may not transfer across scales.
- Benchmark availability offline: datasets (PG19/proof-pile subsets, NIAH generators, LongBench/ZeroSCROLLS) are not present in the sandbox and network is disabled; obtainability in the execution environment is unconfirmed and is a gating feasibility item.
- Compute/runtime budget is an unknown: no GPU here, no dependency environment; the numbers above are planning estimates, not verified runtimes.
- Main risks: (i) architecture assumptions wrong → arms redefined (factorial structure survives); (ii) OOD confound on A2 → mitigated by budget-matched A3/A4; (iii) key-scale nuisance in B → mitigated by normalization + entropy calibration gate; (iv) B4 floor control may be too degenerate (uniform selection) making it partially an A-arm — mitigated by seeding random keys with content-correlated noise (random projection retains some signal) and interpreting B4 as a floor, not a pure B level; (v) interaction effects may be small relative to seed/document variance → paired designs and clustering over documents.

=====================================================================
6. SCOPE STATEMENT
=====================================================================
This is a design-only deliverable. No experiment has been run, no data collected, and no results are claimed. The expected empirical outcome — which of dynamic lookup and unit representations is critical, redundant, or interacting — is unknown a priori; the design is built to distinguish these outcomes rather than anticipate them. All InfLLM-specific details (base model, scale, block size, top-k, block-reader construction, training recipe) are assumptions from background knowledge, flagged above, and must be verified against the paper and reference implementation before execution.

ПЛАН (design-only).

1) Инспекция /workspace: в репозитории только task.json (формулировка вопроса + пометка «Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required»). Кода InfLLM, конфигов, чекпоинтов и данных нет; окружение без GPU и сети. Дизайн опирается на общедоступное описание метода: InfLLM нарезает длинный префикс на блоки, по сходству токенов запроса с block representations выбирает top-k блоков (memory units) для attention; выбор агрегации block representations — второй исследуемый компонент; механизм training-free.

2) Набросок подхода — факториальная компонентная абляция:

payload.answer:
ФИНАЛЬНЫЙ ДИЗАЙН ЭКСПЕРИМЕНТА (design-only; запуск не выполнялся, результаты не заявляются)

ЦЕЛЬ
Количественно оценить критичность для InfLLM (a) динамического контекстного memory lookup (similarity-based block selection) и (b) выбора unit representations (способа агрегации block representations) на длинноконтекстных задачах; проверить, растёт ли критичность с длиной контекста.

1. УСЛОВИЯ (факторная матрица + базлайны)
Базовый метод: блоки фиксированного размера B токенов; block representation — max-pooling токен-эмбеддингов блока (оригинал); на каждом шаге top-k блоков по сходству токенов запроса с представлениями блоков; k блоков попадает в memory units.

Фактор LOOKUP (при фиксированном memory budget = k блоков, один и тот же объём во всех условиях):
- L1 dynamic — оригинальный similarity-based top-k.
- L2 window — слайдинг-окно: последние k блоков без поиска (локальность без содержательного выбора).
- L3 random — k случайных блоков (уничтожает содержательность выбора, сохраняет объём).
Контрасты: L1 vs L2 — «даёт ли поиск больше, чем локальность»; L1 vs L3 — «даёт ли поиск больше, чем случайность»; L2 vs L3 — есть ли нетривиальная локальная эвристика. Если L3 ≈ L2 ≈ L1, критичность lookup низкая и эффект определяется объёмом памяти.

Фактор REPR (при L1, а в полной матрице и при других lookup):
- R1 max (оригинал), R2 mean, R3 first-token блока, R4 random/фиксированная проекция.

Полная матрица: 3 lookup × 4 repr = 12 условий. Минимальная версия при ограниченном бюджете: ядро {L1,L2,L3} × {R1} + полный столбец repr только при L1 (6 условий), затем достройка.

Базлайны:
- B0: базовая модель без экстраполяции (короткий контекст / усечение) — нижняя опорная точка.
- B1: полный InfLLM (L1×R1) — верхняя опорная точка; также sanity-check.
- B2 (где физически возможно): плотный attention на том же токен-бюджете — контекст «объём без компрессии».

2. ЧУВСТВИТЕЛЬНОСТЬ К ГИПЕРПАРАМЕТРАМ
Чтобы выводы не держались на одном наборе гиперпараметров: на полной конфигурации (L1×R1) прогон k±1 (и один альтернативный block size B′) на двух контрастных задачах LongBench (одна QA-типа, одна summarization/code). При выявленной высокой чувствительности — расширить сетку на ядро {L1,L2,L3}×R1.

3. БЕНЧМАРКИ И МЕТРИКИ
- LongBench: NarrativeQA, Qasper, QMSum, HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, GovReport, LCC, RepoBench (QA одно-/много-хоповые, summarization, code) — стандартные метрики (F1, ROUGE, accuracy, edit similarity по протоколу датасета).
- Streaming-перплексия (PG-19 / стриминговый протокол) — непрерывная метрика, чувствительная к деградации памяти без порогов задач.
- Опционально при наличии бюджета: ∞-Bench для сверхдлинных диапазонов.
- Длины: per-length buckets 4k / 16k / 32k / 64k+ (по доступному диапазону датасетов).

4. КОНТРОЛЫ
- Равный memory budget: во всех lookup-условиях ровно k блоков (одинаковое число токенов памяти); декодер, позиционные манипуляции и прочее — идентичны.
- Greedy decoding, фиксированные сиды; парные сравнения на одних и тех же примерах во всех условиях.
- Подвыборки фиксированного размера: 100 сэмплов на задачу (50 при экономии) с заранее записанным списком ID.
- Sanity-check (критерий зафиксирован ДО абляций): воспроизведение заявленных в статье LongBench-чисел полного InfLLM (L1×R1) в пределах ±2 пунктов метрики на каждой задаче (мягкий допуск до ±1.5–2 при подвыборке; при невыполнении — сначала калибровка гиперпараметров/реализации, абляции не запускаются).
- Проверка реализаций L2/L3: одинаковая процедура сборки memory units, отличается только правило выбора блоков.

5. ПЛАН АНАЛИЗА
- Первичная величина эффекта: дельта метрики условия против полного InfLLM (L1×R1) на задачу и на length bucket, с 95% bootstrap-CI по примерам (парный бутстрэп, 10k ресэмплов).
- Операционализация «критичности» (заранее): компонент критичен, если |Δ| ≥ min(2 пункта метрики, 10% от базового значения) И нижняя граница CI > 0; направление без значимой ширины CI не считается свидетельством. Отдельно отчёт по частотному критерию: доля задач, где CI исключает ноль.
- Тест взаимодействия LOOKUP × REPR: двухфакторный анализ по бутстрэп-контрастам (ANOVA по пер-сэмпловым дельтам, где метрики сопоставимы; иначе — контрасты (L1−L3) при разных repr с bootstrap-CI на разность дельт). Если взаимодействие значимо (критичность repr проявляется только при dynamic lookup) — репортим раздельные выводы по веткам.
- Per-length buckets: регрессия/контрасты |Δ| по длине — растёт ли критичность компонентов с длиной.
- Чувствительность k±1: отчёт о стабильности ранжирования условий и выводов.
- Все сравнения — парные, с поправкой на множественность (Holm) внутри семейства задач.

6. РЕСУРСЫ И ФИЗИБИЛИТИ
- Модель: 7–8B (LLaMA-2-7B / LLaMA-3-8B), bf16, ~16–20 ГБ на инференс; одна A100/H100 40–80 ГБ достаточна.
- Объём: базовая версия 6 условий + B0/B1/B2 + k±1 и B′ (≈10 конфигураций) × 9 задач LongBench × 100 примеров + streaming-PPL. Оценка: минуты на пример при 16–64k контекста с блочным вниманием → порядка 2–4 GPU-дней на полную версию, ~1 GPU-день на минимальную; полная матрица 12 условий — 4–6 GPU-дней.
- Инженерия: реализация хуков выбора блоков (dynamic/window/random) и замен repr в официальной реплике InfLLM; логирование выбранных блоков для диагностики (перекрытие выбора с окном, стабильность выбора по шагам) — качественная поддержка интерпретации.
- В данной среде (без GPU/сети) исполнение невозможно; дизайн предназначен для переноса во внешнее окружение с чекпоинтами.

7. ДОПУЩЕНИЯ (постулируются, не требования задачи)
- Размер базовой модели 7–8B; масштабные закономерности могут отличаться для 70B+.
- Гиперпараметры (block size, k) взяты из статьи/официального кода и одинаковы во всех условиях, кроме явных проверок чувствительности.
- Инференс-only достаточно (метод training-free); файнтюн под абляции не предполагается.
- Подвыборка 100 примеров/задачу даёт достаточную мощность для дельт ≥2 пунктов.

8. НЕОПРЕДЕЛЁННОСТИ
- Доступность чекпоинтов (лицензия LLaMA) и публичного кода; соответствие кода статье.
- Точные гиперпараметры block selection в реализации; возможное расхождение со статьёй — фиксируется до абляций.
- Версия InfLLM (v1 vs v2) — целевая v1; перенос выводов на v2 не предполагается.
- Реализуемость B2 (плотный attention на большом бюджете) ограничена памятью — выполняется только там, где физически возможно, и помечается как неполный контроль.
- Точный порог «критичности» (2 пункта / 10%) — конвенция, фиксируется заранее, дополняется CI-логикой, но абсолютные пороги в литературе не стандартизированы.

Оба целевых компонента (lookup и unit representations) напрямую соответствуют отдельным заменяемым элементам этого конвейера, что делает факторную матрицу реализуемой хуками в одной кодовой базе.
- Логика разделения «lookup vs объём»: L3 (random, тот же k) сохраняет объём памяти и уничтожает содержательность выбора; L2 (window) сохраняет объём и даёт локальность; L1−L3 изолирует вклад самого поиска, L1−L2 — вклад поиска сверх локальности. Это соответствует требованию контрола «отделить эффект lookup от меньшего объёма контекста».
- Включены все три уточнения исследователя как явные элементы: (1) чувствительность k±1 и альтернативный block size на полной конфигурации с правилом расширения сетки; (2) тест взаимодействия LOOKUP×REPR через двухфакторный анализ/бутстрэп-контрасты и операционализация критичности через |Δ| против полного InfLLM + ширина CI (порог ≥2 пункта или ≥10% и нижняя граница CI > 0), а не только направление; (3) предзарегистрированный критерий sanity-check: воспроизведение LongBench-чисел полного InfLLM в пределах ±2 пунктов до запуска абляций, при невыполнении — калибровка вместо абляций.
- Ресурсная оценка исходит из inference-only режима 7–8B модели в bf16 (единицы ГБ-десятки ГБ VRAM), типичных таймингов длинноконтекстного инференса и подвыборок 100 примеров/задачу; итог порядка 2–6 GPU-дней в зависимости от полноты матрицы. Датасеты и метрики соответствуют протоколу оригинальной работы InfLLM (LongBench + стриминговая перплексия), что позволяет sanity-check против опубликованных чисел.
assumptions: Базовая модель класса 7–8B (LLaMA-2-7B / LLaMA-3-8B), как в оригинальной работе; выводы могут не переноситься на 70B+

La pregunta de investigación es: ¿qué tan críticos son la memoria dinámica de contexto (lookup de bloques) y la elección de representaciones de unidades para el desempeño de InfLLM en tareas de contexto largo?

**PLAN (solo diseño, fase preliminar)**

**1. Inspección de entradas**
- `/workspace` contiene solo `task.json`; `track.md` (embebido) confirma que es tarea de solo diseño, sin repos ni cómputo requeridos.
- No hay implementación de InfLLM disponible; el diseño se apoya en la especificación pública del método: memoria de unidades (bloques no solapados del contexto), lookup dinámico por relevancia semántica (top-k bloques por token consulta) más atención local, sin reentrenamiento.

**2. Esbozo de enfoque experimental**

*Variables manipuladas (2 factores principales):*

- **Factor A — Mecanismo de lookup de memoria (4–5 niveles):**
  - A1 Intacto (InfLLM original, top-k semántico).
  - A2 Desactivado: sin memoria, solo ventana local (equivale al modelo base con ventana extendida local).
  - A3 Dañado-informativo: se recuperan top-k bloques **incorrectos** (p. ej., bloques aleatorios o con puntuación de retrieval invertida/barajada) — mismo presupuesto de atención, contenido irrelevante.
  - A4 Dañado-omisión: se elimina sistemáticamente el bloque que contiene la información relevante (corrupción dirigida).
  - A5 Sin selección: atención a *todos* los bloques con pesos uniformes (prueba si el valor está en la selección o solo en el acceso).

- **Factor B — Representación de unidades (3–4 niveles):**
  - B1 Original (representación por atención interna token-bloque).
  - B2 Mean-pooling de los estados ocultos del bloque.
  - B3 Embedding del último/primer token del bloque.
  - B4 Representación aleatoria pero fija por bloque (control de dañación: rompe el lookup sin cambiar el número de parámetros/cómputo).

*Tareas de contexto largo (métricas):*
- LongBench (subconjunto multi-categoría): NarrativeQA, QuALITY, Qasper (QA largo); GovReport/QMSum (resumen); PassageRetrieval-en y PassageCount (recuperación/agregación multi-hop).
- Needle-in-a-Haystack: precisión de recuperación como función de profundidad × longitud — diagnostica *dónde* falla cada condición.
- Reportar siempre score por tarea + media global + NIAH por profundidad.

*Diseño:* factorial A×B, con dosis-respuesta en k (nº de bloques recuperados) y en severidad de corrupción (A4 con 25/50/100% de omisión).

*Controles:*
- Modelo base, tamaño de bloque, ventana local, k, prompts y decodificación fijos entre condiciones.
- Sanidad: reproducir el rendimiento reportado de InfLLM intacto dentro de tolerancia antes de cualquier ablation.
- Baselines: modelo base con ventana local (A2) como piso; InfLLM intacto como techo.
- Placebo: corrupción aleatoria de la representación B4 en un contexto corto (donde la memoria no debería usarse) — no debe cambiar nada.
- Semillas múltiples para condiciones estocásticas (aleatorización de bloques); reportar media±IC.
- Registro de costo (latencia/memoria) para descartar que las diferencias sean artefactos de presupuesto de atención.

**3. Supuestos y su clasificación**

*Supuestos que NO cambiarían el diseño si varían:*
- Base model concreto (Llama-2/Mistral u otro): cambia números absolutos, no la estructura del factorial.
- Tamaño de bloque y k exactos: se fijan y se reportan; efectos esperados son robustos a valores razonables.
- Disponibilidad exacta de los datasets listados: cualquier batería multi-categoría de contexto largo sirve; solo ajustaría el subconjunto.

*Supuestos con consecuencias (cambiarían el diseño):*
- **Variante de InfLLM** (training-free puro vs. con preentrenamiento continuo): si es la variante entrenada, el factor B (representaciones) puede interactuar con el entrenamiento → añadiría evaluación de la variante training-free como contraste.
- **Presupuesto de cómputo disponible**: sin GPU, el diseño asume evaluación por inferencia; si solo hubiera cómputo mínimo, recortaría a A1/A2/A3 × B1/B2 en 2–3 tareas.
- **¿Es el lookup por-token o por-bloque-consulta?** La granularidad del retrieval afecta cómo implemento A3/A4; necesitaría confirmación del mecanismo exacto para fijar la operación de corrupción.
- **Acceso a la implementación**: el diseño asume que puedo intervenir el módulo de memoria (gancho/sustitución de representaciones). Si solo hubiera inferencia en caja negra vía API, los factores B serían inviables y el diseño se limitaría a corrupciones del *texto* de entrada.
- **Longitudes objetivo** (4k–32k vs. >100k): determina si NIAH por profundidad es factible y cuántas tareas caben en el presupuesto.

**Pregunta abierta al investigador** (opcional, dentro del presupuesto): ¿qué variante de InfLLM y qué rango de longitudes considera relevantes para el objetivo? Con eso fijaría la matriz final de condiciones.
