# Эксперимент: масштабирование суррогатных моделей аэродинамического сопротивления (Cd) по размеру обучающей выборки и различия между архитектурами
Данные: DrivAerNet++ — параметрические конфигурации DrivAer, 26 скалярных признаков (включая категорию задней части: fastback / notchback / estateback), целевая переменная Cd.

---

## 1. Rationale

Вопрос задачи двухчастный: (а) растёт ли точность суррогата с ростом n_train; (б) различается ли точность между архитектурами. Дизайн отвечает на оба одной процедурой: каждая модель обучается на одинаковых подвыборках растущего размера и оценивается на одном общем hold-out — это даёт сопоставимые кривые обучения и корректное попарное сравнение архитектур на каждом n.

26-мерный скалярный вход — это классическая область «малых данных»: GP исторически силён здесь, ансамбли деревьев и MLP — конкуренты, а линейная/полиномиальная регрессия дают нижний ориентир сложности и проверяют, есть ли вообще нелинейный сигнал. Выбор целевой величины — Cd (скаляр из аннотаций датасета), метрики — RMSE (основная, чувствительна к хвостовым ошибкам, важна для инженерного использования), MAE (робастность к выбросам), R² (доля объяснённой дисперсии, сопоставимо с литературой по DrivAer-суррогатам).

## 2. Данные и подготовка

2.1. Источник: официальный релиз DrivAerNet++ (метаданные конфигураций + Cd из CFD/wind-tunnel аннотаций). Из репозитория в этой среде данных НЕТ — подтверждено осмотром (в /workspace только task.json, documents.track.md: «Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required»).

2.2. Определение фактического N (шаг 0, до любой фиксации теста):
- Загрузить реальный релиз; взять таблицу конфигураций, у которых есть все 26 признаков И непустое Cd.
- N = размер этой таблицы после удаления дубликатов и строк с пропусками; зафиксировать N, версию релиза и хэш файла в протоколе.
- ~8000 конфигураций из публикации DrivAerNet++ — НЕПОДТВЕРЖДЁННОЕ число; всё ниже масштабируется от фактического N.

2.3. Проверка баланса категорий задней части (шаг 0b, до фиксации теста):
- Построить частотную таблицу fastback/notchback/estateback (и прочих категорий, если в релизе они есть) по Cd-срезу.
- Если минимальная категория в допустимом hold-out (шаг 3) содержит ≥ ~10% его объёма — обычная стратифицированная выборка; иначе — стратификация с минимальной квотой на редкую категорию, а в протоколе фиксируется, что редкая категория может ограничивать разрешающую способность теста.

2.4. Кодирование признаков: числовые — стандартизация (параметры fit только на train-подвыборке, никакой утечки из теста); категориальные — one-hot. Схема одинакова для всех моделей.

## 3. Разбиение и кривые обучения

3.1. Hold-out: один общий тест-набор ~10–15% от N (при N≈8000 → 1000–1200), стратифицированный по типу задней части, фиксируется seed'ом и используется для ВСЕХ моделей и ВСЕХ n. Остальное — пул для train-подвыборок.

3.2. Сетка n_train — АДАПТИВНАЯ:
- Нижняя граница: минимально осмысленный объём для 26 признаков — логарифмическая сетка начинается с ~2–4× числа признаков, т.е. n_min = max(64, 3×d_eff) ≈ 80 (d_eff — размерность после one-hot; если one-hot раздувает признаковое пространство, n_min пересчитывается от d_eff).
- Верхняя граница: n_max = весь пул train после вычета hold-out (≈ 0.85–0.9·N, фактическое значение после шага 2.2).
- Промежуточные точки: лог-сетка (множители ≈2) между n_min и n_max, например {80, 160, 320, 640, 1280, 2560, 5120, n_max} — обрезается сверху фактическим n_max.
- На каждую точку: 5 независимых случайных resample'ов train (фиксированные seed'ы, одни и те же подвыборки для всех моделей в данном повторе — это делает сравнение архитектур на каждом n ПАРНЫМ).

3.3. Насыщение кривой: критерий плато — относительное улучшение RMSE при удвоении n на последних двух точках < предзаданный порог (например <1%) при перекрытии 95% CI; фиксируется как наблюдение, а не как заранее заданный «успех».

## 4. Архитектуры-кандидаты

Единая схема подбора гиперпараметров для всех моделей (иначе сравнение архитектур смешается с разной настройкой): для каждой модели — небольшой заданный грид/сетка поиска, выбор по 5-fold CV внутри текущей train-подвыборки (критерий — RMSE), без обращения к тесту; сетка одинаковой «ширины бюджета» между моделями.

| Модель | Назначение | Ключевые гиперпараметры (CV) |
|---|---|---|
| Ridge-линейная | базлайн, нижний ориентир | α |
| Полиномиальная регрессия (deg 2, регуляризованная) | простая нелинейность | степень ∈ {1,2}, α |
| Gaussian Process (RBF+ARD, RBF+Matérn-3/2) | ядро сравнения, ядровый бейзлайн | kernel choice, noise; оптимизация log-marginal-likelihood |
| Random Forest | tree ensemble | n_estimators (фикс. большое), max_depth, min_samples_leaf |
| Gradient Boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) | tree ensemble | learning_rate, n_estimators (early stopping по внутренней CV), max_depth, subsample |
| MLP (2–3 скрытых слоя, ReLU, Adam, early stopping) | нейросетевой представитель | width, depth, lr, weight decay; ранний стоп по валидационному сплиту train |

Опционально (по желанию исследователя): kNN и предсказание средним — как sanity-бейзлайны, чтобы подтвердить наличие сигнала в 26 параметрах; в основной таблицу не входят.

5) GP fallback: если n_train превышает порог точного GP (ориентир ~4–8k при 26 признаках, уточняется по времени одного прогона на пилотной точке n=1600), включается sparse approximation (SVGP / inducing points, m≈512–1024) с тем же ядром. Порог и переключатель фиксируются ДО прогона полной сетки и применяются симметрично ко всем точкам n выше порога, чтобы верх сетки не обрезался несимметрично между моделями. Пилотная проверка: на n=1600 сравнить точный GP и sparse — если расхождение RMSE < шума повторов, переход считается прозрачным.

## 5. Controls

- C1. Общий hold-out + общие train-подвыборки на каждом n → парное сравнение архитектур без дисперсии от разной выборки.
- C2. Одинаковая схема CV/подбора гиперпараметров и сопоставимый вычислительный бюджет на модель (по одобренному уточнению 1).
- C3. Стандартизация/кодирование фитятся только на train каждого повтора.
- C4. Стратификация по типу задней части; предварительная проверка баланса (шаг 2.3) до фиксации теста.
- C5. Фиксация random seed'ов, версий библиотек, версии релиза данных.
- C6. Sanity-бейзлайны (среднее, kNN) — контроль того, что признаки несут сигнал.
- C7. Мониторинг выбросов/тяжёлых хвостов Cd; при обнаружении аномальных строк Cd — протоколируется, исключение только по явному и воспроизводимому правилу, зафиксированному до прогона.

## 6. Analysis plan (явные критерии ответа)

6.1. «Производительность растёт с n»:
- Для каждой модели — регрессия log(RMSE) (и R²) на log(n_train) по точкам верхнего диапазона (например последние 4 точки сетки).
- Критерий (а): наклон β < 0 (RMSE падает с n) с значимостью по 95% CI, построенным по 5 повторам (t-интервал / bootstrap по повторам). Дополнительно: непараметрический тест монотонного убывания (Page's trend / Jonckheere–Terpstra) по средним RMSE точек сетки.
- Отдельно фиксируется наличие плато (критерий 3.3) — «растёт, но выходит на насыщение» и «не растёт» — разные исходы, оба валидные.

6.2. «Различается ли между архитектурами»:
- На каждом n: попарные сравнения RMSE моделей по 5 повторам — Wilcoxon signed-rank (парность по общим подвыборкам), поправка Холма на множественность (k моделей → k(k−1)/2 пар).
- Отдельные выводы при малых n (первые 2–3 точки) и при n_max: если ранжирование моделей меняется между режимами — фиксируется crossover как валидный главный исход (например GP лучше при малых n, GBDT/MLP — при больших), а не как провал.
- Сводная таблица: RMSE/MAE/R² ± CI по каждой модели × каждой точке n; ранги моделей по n.
- Эффект размера выборки на «разрыв» между лучшей и худшей архитектурой: |ΔRMSE|(n) — сжимается или растёт с n.

6.3. Отчёт: (i) графики кривых обучения RMSE и R² vs n (log-x) с CI для всех моделей; (ii) таблица финальных метрик при n_max; (iii) сводка попарных тестов; (iv) явные вердикты по критериям 6.1–6.2.

## 7. Feasibility (честно, с оговорками)

- Данные: НЕ подтверждено в данной среде. /workspace пуст (только task.json), network=disabled, datasets=[]. Требуется доступ к официальному релизу DrivAerNet++ вне изоляции (HuggingFace/GitHub) — предположение A1, без которого эксперимент невозможен.
- Зависимости: НЕ подтверждено. numpy/scipy/sklearn/pandas/torch/xgboost не установлены (проверено импортами, Python 3.14.4); нужен pip-доступ вне изоляции. MLP и sparse GP — torch или эквивалент.
- Вычисления: CPU-only (gpu_enabled=false), 224 CPU (affinity среды; вне изоляции может отличаться). Оценка времени: доминируют (i) точный GP — O(n³), поэтому порог переключения на sparse GP фиксируется по пилоту; (ii) GBDT с CV — умеренно; (iii) MLP — минуты на точку сетки. Итого: |сетка| × 5 повторов × 6–8 моделей ≈ 200–280 обучений на полном прогоне; при CPU-параллелизации по повторам — порядка нескольких часов CPU-времени на модель, суммарно в пределах одних-двух суток машинного времени на 224 ядрах. Это оценка порядка величины, не подтверждённый бенчмарк.
- Риски и запасные варианты: (i) N меньше ожидаемого → сетка обрезается сверху по фактическому n_max, вывод по меньшему диапазону n, это фиксируется в протоколе; (ii) сильный дисбаланс категорий → квотированная стратификация + оговорка об ограниченной разрешающей способности теста; (iii) sparse GP расходится с точным на пилоте → уменьшить порог переключения, а не игнорировать расхождение.
- Design-only: данная среда не содержит данных/зависимостей, что согласуется с track.md; эксперимент выполняется вне её при подтверждении A1/A4, либо дизайн используется как готовая спецификация.

## 8. Допущения (assumptions — отдельно от фактов)

- A1. Релиз DrivAerNet++ с таблицей «26 параметров + Cd» доступен для загрузки вне данной изолированной среды.
- A2. Фактический N порядка тысяч (публикация: ~8000) — число неподтверждённое; все размеры сетки масштабируются от реального N (шаг 2.2).
- A3. 26 параметров — полный вектор признаков датасета, включая категориальные; точный перечень и кодирование проверяются по реальному файлу.
- A4. CPU-бюджет (224 ядра) доступен вне изоляции; GPU не нужен.
- A5. Подбор гиперпараметров 5-fold CV по RMSE — выбранная конвенция, не требование задачи.
- A6. Аннотации Cd достаточно однородны (единый CFD-сетап), чтобы сравнение архитектур не требовало поправок на источник данных.

## 9. Uncertainties (что остаётся неизвестным до шага 0)

- Точная структура релиза (CSV-схема, перечень 26 признаков, наличие прочих категорий задней части).
- Реальный баланс fastback/notchbook/estateback — проверяется шагом 2.3 до фиксации теста.
- Наличие сети/pip вне изоляции.
- Порог точного GP — определяется пилотом на n=1600, не фиксирован заранее.
- Временной бюджет — оценка, не измерение.

DISEÑO EXPERIMENTAL FINAL — Escalabilidad y arquitectura de sustitutos paramétricos para predicción de arrastre (DrivAerNet++, 26 parámetros)

═══════════════════════════════════════════
0. ALCANCE Y SUPUESTOS DECLARADOS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Pregunta de investigación: (a) ¿el rendimiento predictivo de modelos sustitutos basados en datos paramétricos mejora con mayor tamaño del conjunto de entrenamiento? (b) ¿difiere entre arquitecturas de modelos?

Supuestos (declarados como supuestos, NO como hechos verificados; las propiedades exactas de DrivAerNet++ no fueron verificables en el workspace, que contiene únicamente task.json):
- S1. Tamaño del dataset ≈ 8,000 configuraciones (orden de magnitud esperado de DrivAerNet++); si el conjunto real difiere, la malla de tamaños se reescala conservando la estructura logarítmica.
- S2. Existe un valor objetivo de Cd por configuración (proveniente de simulación CFD RANS del dataset).
- S3. Las tres configuraciones de trasera (fastback, notchback, estateback) están representadas en cantidad suficiente para estratificar.
- S4. La entrada es exclusivamente el vector de 26 parámetros de diseño (decisión fijada por el investigador); cualquier modelo que requiera geometría (malla, point cloud, campo de flujo) queda fuera de alcance.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. RATIONALE
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Los sustitutos aerodinámicos basados en parámetros tratan el diseño como un vector de baja dimensión (26 variables) y el Cd como respuesta escalar continua. Es esperable que (i) todos los modelos mejoren con más datos (leyes de escala de aprendizaje), pero (ii) la forma de la curva difiera por familia: ensambles de árboles suelen saturar temprano en tabulares de baja dimensión; las redes neuronales suelen necesitar más datos pero con mayor techo; los modelos lineales saturan pronto con techo bajo. El diseño empipa directamente sobre ambos factores para estimar efectos principales e interacción, con test fijo compartido para comparabilidad. La decisión de incluir familias contrastantes (lineal / árbol / boosting / red) garantiza que la pregunta (b) tenga rango de variabilidad real.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. FACTORES Y NIVELES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Factor A — Tamaño de entrenamiento n (dentro-sujeto): malla logarítmica de fracciones del conjunto de entrenamiento disponible: {5%, 10%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%}. Con S1 (≈8k, menos 20% de test ⇒ ≈6.4k de entrenamiento), esto da n ≈ {320, 640, 1280, 2560, 3840, 5120, 6400}. La malla se adapta proporcionalmente si el dataset real difiere (regla: mínimo 6 puntos, espaciado ~×2, máximo = 100% del train disponible).
Factor B — Arquitectura del sustituto (5 niveles):
  B1. Lineal regularizado (Ridge/Lasso con selección de α) — baseline paramétrico.
  B2. Random Forest (regresor).
  B3. Gradient boosting (XGBoost o LightGBM; elegir uno y documentar).
  B4. MLP pequeña (1–2 capas ocultas, p. ej. 128–64, ReLU, early stopping; adecuada a 26 entradas).
  B5. (Opcional, si el presupuesto de cómputo lo permite) Proceso gaussiano con kernel RBF+Matérn y ruido, o SVR-RBF — aporta comparación con modelo con incertidumbre calibrada.
Diseño: factorial completo A×B (7 tamaños × 5 arquitecturas = 35 celdas), réplicas por semilla (ver §4).

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. VARIABLES DE RESPUESTA Y MÉTRICAS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Variable de respuesta: Cd predicho vs. Cd CFD en el test set fijo.
Métrica primaria (decisión del investigador): MAE normalizado por la media de Cd del conjunto: nMAE = MAE(ΔCd)/mean(Cd_test). (Se evita MAPE como métrica única por sensibilidad a denominadores pequeños dado el rango estrecho de Cd.)
Métricas secundarias: nRMSE = RMSE/mean(Cd_test); R²; y opcionalmente el máximo error relativo (p95 de |ΔCd|/Cd) para diagnóstico de colas.
Todas las métricas se calculan sobre el mismo test set fijo para todas las celdas.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. CONTROLES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
C1. Test set fijo compartido: hold-out del 20% (o 15%), estratificado por tipo de trasera, generado una sola vez con semilla maestra; NUNCA re-muestreado entre celdas. Todos los modelos y tamaños se evalúan sobre el mismo test.
C2. Submuestreo del train: para cada tamaño n, submuestras estratificadas por tipo de trasera (para que las tres clases estén presentes en todos los tamaños) extraídas del mismo pool de entrenamiento; el resto del train no usado en esa celda se descarta (no se usa como " unlabeled" ni para preprocesamiento de test).
C3. Réplicas: ≥3 semillas independientes por celda (recomendado 5 si el cómputo lo permite) que controlan simultáneamente la submuestra de train y, para modelos estocásticos (RF, boosting, MLP, inicialización de red), la semilla del modelo. Se reportan curvas de aprendizaje con banda de incertidumbre (media ± IC95% por bootstrap o ±1.96·EE).
C4. Presupuesto de tuning equitativo (decisión del investigador): mismo número de configuraciones de hiperparámetros evaluadas por arquitectura vía CV interna (k=5 fold CV sobre el subconjunto de train de cada celda, p. ej. 20 combinaciones por arquitectura), independiente del tamaño de entrenamiento. El grid se define por arquitectura y se documenta en un apéndice; el tuning se hace solo en train (el test nunca participa).
C5. Preprocesamiento sin fuga: estandarización de los 26 parámetros ajustada solo con los datos de train de cada celda; codificación de variables categóricas de los parámetros (si las hay) definida a priori y documentada.
C6. Cegamiento del análisis: las curvas y tests se computan a partir de la tabla de resultados completa; no se ajustan arquitecturas post-hoc tras ver los resultados.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. PLAN DE ANÁLISIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
P1. Curvas de aprendizaje: para cada arquitectura, nMAE (y nRMSE) vs. n, con bandas IC95%. Visual principal del estudio.
P2. Efecto del tamaño (pregunta a): modelo lineal mixto sobre la tabla de resultados — nMAE ~ log(n) + arquitectura + log(n):arquitectura + (1|semilla) — o, alternativamente, ANOVA de dos vías con réplicas. Se reporta la pendiente media global d(nMAE)/d log(n) con IC, y el tamaño de saturación por arquitectura (primer n a partir del cual la mejora relativa entre puntos consecutivos < ε, p. ej. 2%).
P3. Efecto de arquitectura (pregunta b): en cada tamaño, comparación entre arquitecturas con test de Friedman sobre las réplicas (bloques = semillas) y post-hoc de Nemenyi (o Wilcoxon pareado con corrección Holm); en el tamaño máximo se reporta el ranking con diferencia mínima relevante predefinida (p. ej., una mejora de nMAE < 1% se declara práctica- mente irrelevante).
P4. Interacción tamaño×arquitectura (clave del diseño): término de interacción del modelo mixto; gráfico de interacción. Interpretación esperada documentada: si las curvas se cruzan (p. ej., MLP supera a boosting solo a partir de cierto n), la respuesta a (b) depende del presupuesto de datos — conclusión central del experimento.
P5. Criterios de escalabilidad por pendiente: por arquitectura, pendiente de la fase final de la curva (ajuste de ley de potencia nMAE ≈ a·n^−b; b≈0 indica saturación). Se declara "escalable" si b > umbral predefinido (p. ej. 0.05) en la región superior de la malla.
P6. Robustez: análisis por tipo de trasera (¿el ranking de arquitecturas cambia por subclase?) como análisis secundario, no primario.
P7. Entregables: tabla maestra de resultados (celda × semilla × métrica), figuras de curvas y de interacción, tabla de ranking Friedman/Nemenyi, y declaración explícita de supuestos S1–S4.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. FACTIBILIDAD SIN GPU
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- Datos tabulares de dimensión 26 y ≤6.4k filas por celda: Ridge/Lasso, RF, boosting y SVR/GP son triviales en CPU (segundos a minutos por ajuste).
- MLP pequeña (2 capas): entrenamiento en CPU del orden de segundos-minutos por ajuste; factible.
- Estimación de carga total: 35 celdas × 5 semillas × (1 ajuste final + tuning 20 configs × 5 folds internos ≈ 100 ajustes) ≈ 3,500–6,000 ajustes ligeros; con paralelización en los 224 núcleos declarados, horas como máximo. El único riesgo real es el GP en el tamaño máximo (O(n³) ≈ 6400³ — evitar GP a n máximo o usar aproximación sparse/inducing points; se documenta como restricción si B5 se incluye).
- No se requiere GPU en ningún punto del diseño.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
7. LIMITACIONES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- L1. Los resultados son válidos para el espacio paramétrico de DrivAerNet++ y la fidelidad CFD del dataset; no extrapolan a otros datasets ni a CFD de mayor fidelidad o experimentos de túnel.
- L2. Con entrada de solo 26 parámetros, existe un techo de predictibilidad irreducible (parámetros no capturan toda la variabilidad geométrica); las curvas pueden saturar por este techo y no por el algoritmo — interpretar la saturación con cautela.
- L3. El tuning equitativo por número de configuraciones no garantiza equidad en presupuesto de cómputo real; se documenta como decisión de equidad adoptada.
- L4. S1–S3 son supuestos no verificados localmente; si el dataset real difiere (tamaño, cobertura de traseras), el diseño se recalibra sin cambiar su estructura.
- L5. Las réplicas por semilla cuantifican variabilidad de submuestreo/entrenamiento, no variabilidad de la fidelidad CFD fuente.
- L6. Este documento es solo diseño; ningún experimento fue ejecutado y no se reclama ningún resultado numérico.

# 最终实验设计：参数化数据驱动的气动阻力（Cd）代理模型的规模可扩展性与架构差异

**任务性质声明**：本文件是纯设计型交付物（依 track.md："Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."）。本设计**未执行任何实验，不包含任何实测数据、运行日志或虚构结果**。文中所有数字要么是协议参数（我们自行设定），要么是明确标注为"估算"的计算量量级。

---

## 1. 目标与假设陈述

**研究问题**（源自 task.json）：(Q1) 基于参数化数据的代理模型预测性能是否随训练集规模增大而提升；(Q2) 性能是否因模型架构不同而有差异。

**可检验假设**：
- **H1（规模效应）**：随训练样本数 n 增加，测试集 Cd 预测误差（RMSE）单调下降，且边际收益递减（学习曲线趋于平缓）。
- **H2（架构主效应）**：在训练规模上平均后，四类架构的测试误差至少有一对存在显著差异。
- **H3（架构 × 规模交互，回答 Q2 的关键）**：架构间的相对排序随训练规模变化（预期方向：GPR 在小 n 占优，梯度提升树/MLP 在大 n 占优——此为方向性预期，非结论）。

**设计类型**：被试内（within-subject）析因设计，因子为"架构"（4 水平）×"训练规模"（8 水平），重复单位为随机种子（5 个）；所有格子共享同一固定测试集，这是配对/重复测量结构的基础。

---

## 2. 数据与划分方案

### 2.1 数据来源
DrivAerNet++ 数据集的参数化设计子集：每个样本为 26 维设计参数向量，目标量为该构型的 Cd 值；构型标签（fastback / notchback / estateback）用于分层。数据集细节（总量、参数定义、Cd 分布）**文档未给出**，全部落入假设登记表（A1、A2、A6）与不确定性清单。

### 2.2 固定测试/验证集（一次性构造，此后冻结）
1. 以固定种子 s₀=20260101，若构型标签可用（A6），按构型分层、无放回地抽出总样本的 **20%** 作为固定保留集；再将保留集对半分为 **验证集（10%，用于调参与早停）** 与 **测试集（10%，仅在每个格子最终评估时使用一次）**。
2. 该划分在全部架构、全部规模点、全部种子之间**完全共享且不再变动**——这是所有跨格子比较可比性的前提。
3. 若构型标签不可用（A6 失败的退化路径，依研究者修正要求写明）：退化为固定种子的纯随机划分；在设计中预先声明构型构成可能成为混杂因素，所有结论限定为"对实际抽到的构型构成成立"，不做构型间外推；若后续能恢复标签，补报按构型分组的误差分解作为事后诊断。

### 2.3 训练子集序列（嵌套 + 对数间隔）
1. 训练池 = 总样本 − 保留集（约 80%）。
2. 规模档序列采用**几何（对数间隔）序列**，8 档：n ∈ {50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200, 5120}（最大档假设训练池 ≥5120，见 A1；若 A1 不成立，按比例截断序列并在设计中记录实际档数，最小保持 5 档）。
3. **单调嵌套协议**（依研究者要求显式写入）：第 k 档训练集是第 k+1 档的真子集。实现：先以固定种子对训练池做一次全局随机排序，第 k 档 = 该排序的前 n_k 个样本。这一协议消除档间抽样噪声，使学习曲线反映纯规模效应而非抽样差异；统计后果（档间误差非独立）在 §5.4 中处理。
4. 每档内若标签可用，验证嵌套子集的构型比例与训练池整体比例的偏差（诊断性检查，非结果）。
5. **同一规模点上，四类架构使用完全相同的训练集**。

### 2.4 预处理协议
- 仅用 26 个参数作为输入特征；目标为 Cd（物理量纲）。
- 特征标准化（z-score）**仅在当前训练子集上拟合**，再变换验证/测试集（防止信息泄漏；嵌套子集意味着不同档的标准化参数不同，此为协议的一部分，统一记录）。
- 线性/多项式模型：二阶多项式扩展（26 维 → 351 个二阶交互 + 26 个平方项 + 线性项）作为可选变体，配合岭正则。
- 模型内部拟合可在标准化目标（z-scored Cd）上进行，但**所有评估报告均换算回 Cd 物理量纲**。

---

## 3. 架构谱系与调优协议

### 3.0 统一调优协议（对全部架构、全部规模点一致）
- **搜索方式**：固定种子的随机搜索，**每个格子固定 20 个配置**（搜索空间与轮数不随 n 改变）。
- **选择准则**：验证集 RMSE 最优的配置作为该格子的最终配置；**测试集只在最终配置确定后评估一次**。
- **公平性声明**：各架构搜索空间大小不同但轮数（20）相同；大 n 档单次拟合更贵，因此调优总预算按"轮数"而非"墙钟时间"定义，并在可行性论证（§6）中说明由此带来的成本不对称。
- 超参空间由我们自定（A3），各架构空间见下；均使用各库的默认非随机部分（随机性全部由受控种子提供）。

### 3.1 线性 / 岭回归（含可选二阶多项式变体）
- **选择理由**：最低容量基线。26 维输入下线性模型几乎无过拟合风险；若其在小 n 即接近复杂模型，可界定"参数化数据中线性成分的贡献"；二阶多项式（岭正则）捕捉常见的主效应交互。
- **超参空间**：正则强度 α ∈ logspace(−4, 3, 8) 档 × {线性, 二阶多项式} 两种特征化 = 16 组合（≤20 轮预算内）。
- **实现**：scikit-learn Ridge；闭式解，无需早停。

### 3.2 高斯过程回归（GPR）
- **选择理由**：小样本区间的经典强基线，核方法提供平滑性先验与不确定性估计；预期呈现"小 n 占优、大 n 受 O(n³) 成本限制"的典型行为，正是检验 H3 交互的理想成员。
- **超参空间**：核 ∈ {RBF, Matérn 5/2} × 核幅值尺度 ∈ {0.1, 1, 10} × 噪声水平初值 ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}，ARD 开启（≤20 组合）。
- **大样本可行性与降级预案（依研究者要求显式写入）**：
  - **主方案**：n ≤ 1600 时使用精确 GPR（Cholesky 分解，1600³/3 ≈ 1.4×10⁹ 浮点运算，秒级）。
  - **n > 1600 时**：切换到稀疏变分 GPR（ inducing 点固定 m=512，SVGP/SGPR 实现）。
  - **连续性校验**：在 n=1600 档同时运行精确与稀疏两种实现，若测试 RMSE 相对差 >2%，则在该档同时报告两者并以精确值为准、稀疏值仅作大 n 档参考（此为预登记的敏感性分析，非事后补救）。
  - **终极降级路径**：若稀疏实现不可用，则 GPR 在 n>1600 的格子记为缺失，采用混合模型对非平衡设计做估计（§5.4），并在报告中标注"GPR 大样本性能未测"。

### 3.3 梯度提升树（GBDT，LightGBM/XGBoost 类实现）
- **选择理由**：表格型参数数据上的强非线性基线，对特征交互与分段效应拟合能力强，中等样本以上通常占优；树模型对小 n 的过拟合倾向使其成为学习曲线"慢启动"端成员。
- **超参空间**：learning_rate ∈ {0.03, 0.1, 0.3} × num_leaves/depth ∈ {15, 31, 63} × min_child_samples ∈ {5, 20} × subsample ∈ {0.8, 1.0}，随机抽 20 组合；早停以验证集为准（patience=50 轮）。

### 3.4 小型多层感知机（MLP）
- **选择理由**：参数化深度代理模型的代表；归纳偏置最弱、样本效率预期最低，预期能体现"需要大样本才能追上树模型/GPR"的交互模式，是 H3 的关键检验成员。
- **超参空间**：隐层结构 ∈ {(64,), (128, 64), (256, 128, 64)} × 学习率 ∈ {1e-3, 3e-3} × weight_decay ∈ {1e-5, 1e-4} × dropout ∈ {0, 0.1}，随机抽 20 组合；早停（patience=20 epoch），批大小固定 64，Adam 优化器，CPU 训练（26 维输入下网络极小，无需 GPU）。

## 5. 统计分析计划

### 5.1 指标
- **共主指标**：测试集 **RMSE** 与 **MAE**（均为 Cd 物理量纲的绝对误差）；**辅助指标**：相对误差百分比（|Cd_pred − Cd| / Cd 的均值，即类 MAPE）。
- **为何同时报告绝对与相对指标（应对 Cd 分布未知，非假定结果）**：文档未给出 Cd 的量纲范围与分布形态。RMSE 对大误差敏感（平方惩罚），若 Cd 残差呈厚尾分布则 RMSE 由少数离群点主导；MAE 对离群稳健但不可微处信息较少；相对误差便于跨构型比较，但对 Cd 值接近零的样本不稳定（气动 Cd 实际范围通常远离零，但这属于外部常识而非文档信息，故只作辅助）。**决策逻辑（预登记）**：主结论同时以 RMSE 与 MAE 报告——若两者给出的显著性结论一致，则结论对指标选择稳健；若不一致，则报告残差分布诊断（偏度、重尾检查）并如实呈现两种口径的分歧，不择一隐瞒。

### 5.2 重复实验与汇总
- 每个格子（架构 × 规模档）独立重复 **5 个种子**（种子同时控制训练子集内的任何重抽样与模型初始化；训练子集本身由嵌套协议固定，故种子主要作用在初始化与袋内随机性上——对 ridge/GPR 无随机性时，5 次重复相同，如实记录为零方差）。
- 每格报告：均值 ± 标准差，以及基于 5 个种子的 t 分布 95% 置信区间。

### 5.3 主要检验
1. **H1（规模主效应）**：两因素重复测量方差分析（因子：架构 4 水平 × 规模 8 水平；重复单位：种子），规模主效应的 F 检验；辅以跨规模的单调趋势检验（Page's trend test）与相邻档的配对比较。
2. **H3（交互，回答 Q2 的关键统计量）**：同一模型中的**架构 × 规模交互项**，报告 F 值、偏 η²；违反球形性时用 Greenhouse–Geisser 校正（Mauchly 检验先行）。交互显著后做简单效应分析：在每个规模档内做架构间的成对比较（4 架构 → 6 对），用 **Holm–Bonferroni** 在每档内校正；并检验"排序是否翻转"（如小 n 档 GPR < GBDT 而大 n 档反向）。
3. **H2（架构主效应）**：同一 ANOVA 的架构主效应；事后成对比较用 Holm 校正。
- **效应量**：全部检验附偏 η² 与成对 Cohen's d（以种子内配对标准差为分母）。

### 5.4 方法论注意（预登记）
- 嵌套子集使不同规模档的误差高度相关，严格而言"规模"不是独立重复单位；重复测量 ANOVA 以种子为重复单位，将规模与架构作为被试内因子，已与该结构一致；若球形性严重违反，改用线性混合模型（随机截距=种子，固定效应=架构×规模、n 的连续项）作为稳健替代，两法结果并列报告。
- GPR 大样本缺失（若触发终极降级）按混合模型框架下的缺失处理，并明示"随机缺失"假设不可完全验证。

### 5.5 学习曲线幂律拟合（辅助证据）
- 对每个架构，在 8 个规模档的种子均值 RMSE 上拟合 **RMSE(n) = a·n^(−b) + c**（非线性最小二乘，固定种子初始化）。
- 报告 a、b、c 与拟合 R²；外推的渐近平台 c 仅作为"各架构在大样本下趋于何水平"的**辅助证据**，不作为主结论；显式声明：8 个点上的三参数拟合外推存在不确定性，且嵌套子集使各点非独立，拟合质量仅供参考。若幂律拟合劣（R² 低或 c 估计为负/发散），如实报告并放弃渐近外推的表述。

## 6. 可行性论证

**前提**：track.md 明确本任务不需要仓库与算力——本设计只需在纸面上自洽且在常规环境下可执行。以下为**估算（非实测）**的相对成本量级表，假定总样本约 8000（A1）、保留集 1600、训练池 6400：

| 架构 | 单次拟合相对成本（n=50 → n=5120） | 总调优+终拟合次数* | 粗略总 CPU 开销估算 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ridge / 多项式 Ridge | 毫秒级 → 亚秒级（闭式解） | 4×8×5×(≤20+1) 中其份额 ≈ 840 次 | < 0.5 CPU 时 |
| GPR（精确 ≤1600；稀疏 >1600） | 毫秒级 → 精确 n=1600 约 10⁹ 浮点运算（秒–十秒级）；稀疏 m=512 为分钟级 | ≈ 840 次 | 5–15 CPU 时 |
| GBDT | 秒级 → 分钟级（小网络表格数据） | ≈ 840 次 | 10–30 CPU 时 |
| 小型 MLP（CPU，早停） | 秒级 → 分钟级（≤3 层、≤64 批） | ≈ 840 次 | 20–50 CPU 时 |

\* 总计 = 4 架构 × 8 档 × 5 种子 × (20 调优配置 + 1 终拟合) ≈ 3360 次拟合。

**结论**：总开销约 40–100 CPU 时量级，输入维度仅 26、网络与树规模小，在常规多核 CPU 环境（如本环境所述 224 核量级的机器，或任何 16 核工作站分批跑数日）完全可执行，无需 GPU；GPR 大样本档是唯一成本敏感点，已由 §3.2 降级预案覆盖。因此"无仓库无算力"约束不影响设计本身的可行性——设计不需要在本任务环境中执行，但其执行路径不依赖特殊资源。

PROPOSED EXPERIMENT STRUCTURE (2)

Goal: test whether parametric-data surrogate performance for drag (Cd) improves with training-set size, and whether the improvement differs by architecture.

A. Candidate model architectures (span the inductive-bias spectrum, low-to-high complexity, all operating on the 26 design parameters):
1. Linear/ridge regression on the 26 parameters (plus a fixed low-order polynomial-feature variant) — baseline, parametric scalability curve.
2. Random forest / gradient-boosted trees (e.g., LightGBM/XGBoost) — strong classical tabular learner.
3. Gaussian process regression (e.g., with Matérn 5/2 kernel on standardized parameters) — classic small-data surrogate; expect favorable at small n, degrade relative to others at large n (O(n^3) scaling is itself an interesting finding/cost consideration).
4. Small MLP (2–4 hidden layers) trained deterministically (fixed seeds, early stopping on validation) — neural baseline; optionally a second neural variant (e.g., a wider/deeper MLP or a simple ResNet-style MLP) to test whether "architecture differences" hold within neural models too.

B. Training-set size variation:
- Nested subsampling ladder from the DrivAerNet++ parametric design matrix (n_train ∈ {~100, 200, 400, 800, ...} up to near-full training split; roughly log-spaced points, ≥6 levels).
- Fixed held-out test set (identical for all n and all models), drawn once from a stratified split that balances the three body types (fastback / notchback / estateback) so scaling curves are not confounded by class mix.
- Fixed validation set (~10–15%) used for hyperparameter selection / early stopping at every n, disjoint from test.
- K independent random subsamples per n (k ≥ 3, ideally 5) to report mean ± std per point; same seeds reused across architectures for paired comparison.

C. Metrics:
- Primary: RMSE and MAE of Cd on the fixed test set; also R².
- Secondary: scaling behavior — fit log(RMSE) vs log(n) power laws per architecture (slope = learning-rate exponent) and test slope differences; paired statistical comparison across seeds (e.g., per-n paired t-test or Wilcoxon between architectures).
- Cost side: training wall-clock time and (for GP) memory, since GP scalability limits are part of the answer.

D. Confound controls:
- Per-model hyperparameter tuning budget held constant across n (or tuned once at largest n, frozen for smaller n — I'd lean toward a light per-n sweep with capped budget, documented).
- Standardized inputs; identical splits and seeds across all architectures.
- Target normalization (standardize Cd) so RMSE is comparable across models.

CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS AND UNCERTAINTIES (3)

Assumptions (not fixed by the task):
1. DrivAerNet++ is publicly downloadable (~8k designs; drag labels for the full set, including the fastback/notchback/estateback variants). If access fails, the design falls back to a synthetic parametric drag function — a major deviation to be flagged.
2. The 26 parameters are a fixed numeric design vector; categorical attributes (e.g., body type) are one-hot or handled naturally by each model.
3. No GPU is required: on 224 CPU cores, MLPs on ≤8k×26 inputs are cheap; tree ensembles are cheap; GPs are the bottleneck (limit GP to n ≲ 2–4k or use sparse/inducing-point variants).
4. Preprocessing is straightforward: no heavy feature engineering, so architecture (not feature engineering) is the differentiator.

Uncertainties / open points:
1. Whether DrivAerNet++ drag labels cover all three body-type variants uniformly, or whether variant counts are imbalanced (affects stratified splits and whether per-variant analysis is feasible).
2. Exact train/test split convention used in the DrivAerNet++ paper vs. our own stratified split — I'd default to our own split for internal validity but note the deviation.
3. Hyperparameter treatment: per-n tuning vs. frozen-at-max-n tuning changes the shape of scaling curves; needs a decision (and possibly a small pilot to check sensitivity).
4. Seed count (3 vs 5) vs. total runtime budget; a pilot run at the two extreme n values would calibrate wall-clock per model and confirm whether 5 seeds × ~6 sizes × ~6 models is feasible in-session.
5. Noise floor: CFD drag labels have finite-mesh noise; small-n curves may plateau at a level set by label noise rather than model capacity — worth noting as an interpretation caveat, not something we can measure without mesh-level metadata.
6. Whether the intended deliverable expects code skeletons or purely a written design (track.md suggests design-only; no compute needed).

No experiment has been executed; this is inspection plus a proposal only. I will develop the full design (with concrete splits, tuning protocol, statistical tests, and feasibility checks) upon your approval.

FINAL DELIVERABLE — EXPERIMENT DESIGN (written design only; NO experiment was run, no pilot executed, no results claimed)

Title: Training-set-size scaling of parametric surrogate models for aerodynamic drag (Cd) on DrivAerNet++ 26-parameter designs

1. RESEARCH QUESTION AND RATIONALE
Q1: Does surrogate predictive performance for drag (Cd) improve as training-set size n grows?
Q2: Does the improvement (scaling behavior) differ across model architectures?
Rationale: Parametric surrogates (inputs = 26 design parameters, output = Cd) are the cheap alternative to CFD, but their data-efficiency is architecture-dependent: classical low-bias models (trees, boosting) saturate early; high-capacity models (MLPs) need more data; GPs excel at small n but scale poorly computationally. A controlled learning-curve comparison isolates these effects.

2. DATA
- Source: DrivAerNet++ parametric design matrix (~8,000 car designs; fastback/notchback/estateback variants) with CFD drag coefficients Cd; feature vector = the 26 specified design parameters, one-hot encoded if any are categorical.
- ASSUMPTION (not verifiable here — network disabled, no local data): the dataset is publicly downloadable and Cd labels cover all three variants.
- Imbalance adaptation: if variant counts are imbalanced, (a) all splits are stratified proportional to the population (preserves real-world error estimates); (b) an OPTIONAL equal-variant balanced test subset is retained for subgroup comparison; (c) OPTIONAL per-variant subgroup analysis: learning curves per body type, run only if n_variant at the smallest ladder rung ≥ 128 (e.g., a variant with <~10% of designs supports only the larger rungs); otherwise report a per-variant error decomposition on the fixed test set only.

3. SPLIT PROTOCOL (internal validity over external comparability)
- One global split: 70% train pool (~5,600) / 15% validation (~1,200) / 15% test (~1,200), stratified by body type, drawn once with a fixed seed and reused for every model, every n, every seed. The test set is never touched by tuning or training.
- Training subsets at size n are drawn from the 70% train pool by k independent random subsamples (seeds s1..s5, reused identically across all architectures → paired comparisons).
- LIMITATION (explicit): this is OUR stratified split, not the official DrivAerNet++ train/test split; results are internally valid (same test set everywhere) but not directly comparable to published leaderboard numbers. Stated as a deviation.

4. TRAINING-SIZE LADDER
n_train ∈ {128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 5600} (≈ log-spaced, 7 points, ending at the full train-pool size).
Validation set fixed at full ~1,200 for all n. Test set fixed at ~1,200 for all n and all models.

5. MODEL ARCHITECTURE SET (all on the same 26 inputs, standardized using training-subset statistics only)
M1 Ridge regression (linear baseline).
M2 Ridge on fixed degree-2 polynomial features (modest parametric expansion; no data-driven feature selection so architecture, not feature engineering, is the differentiator).
M3 Random forest.
M4 Gradient-boosted trees (LightGBM/XGBoost).
M5 Exact Gaussian process, Matérn-5/2 + constant-mean, ARD lengthscales, standardized inputs. GP scalability treatment is EXPLICIT: exact GP only for n ≤ 2048; for n = 4096 and 5600 use a sparse/inducing-point variational GP (m = 512 inducing points, inducing set subsampled once per seed from the training subset). The n-cap and switch point are fixed a priori and reported alongside results (mixing exact and approximate GP is itself flagged as a caveat on the GP curve).
M6 MLP: 3 hidden layers × 128 units, ReLU, Adam, early stopping on validation RMSE, fixed epoch cap, deterministic seeds (CPU-only environment; this capacity is appropriate for 26-d inputs and avoids conflating scaling with GPU-scale model size).
M7 (sensitivity anchor) A second neural variant — wider MLP (4×256) — so that "architecture differences" can also be assessed within the neural family, not just between families.
Total: 7 architectures.

6. HYPERPARAMETER POLICY (per researcher decision: fixed, capped, per-size)
- For every (architecture, n, seed): random search with a FIXED BUDGET of 8 configurations drawn from a per-architecture search space that is IDENTICAL at every n (e.g., RF: max_depth ∈ {4,8,16,32,None}, min_samples_leaf ∈ {1,2,5,10}, n_estimators ∈ {100,300}; GBM: learning_rate ∈ {0.01,0.03,0.1}, num_leaves/depth, n_estimators ∈ {100,300,600}; MLP: lr ∈ {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}, weight_decay, dropout; GP: lengthscale/nuiseance priors). Selection criterion: validation RMSE. Fixed budget + identical space at every n is the fairness device: small n cannot "win" by exhausting a bigger budget, and large n cannot be handicapped by a tiny one.
- Justification over frozen-at-max-n: hyperparameters optimal at n=5600 are typically too flexible or mis-regularized for n=128, so a frozen policy would depress small-n performance and exaggerate the apparent benefit of more data (steeper artificial slope). Conversely, unlimited per-size tuning could overfit the small validation sets at small n, making small-n look artificially good and flattening the curve (bias toward "no benefit"). The capped, size-invariant budget sits between these biases and keeps search effort constant, which is the quantity we hold fixed.
- MITIGATION / sensitivity check: for at least one architecture (M4, gradient boosting) report BOTH the tuned curve (capped per-size budget) and a frozen curve (best configuration selected once at n=5600, reused at all n). If the two slopes differ materially, that is reported as an explicit tuning-sensitivity result. Additionally report the validation-vs-test gap at each n per model as an overfitting-to-validation diagnostic.

7. METRICS
- Primary: RMSE of Cd on the fixed test set (per (model, n, seed)).
- Secondary: MAE, R², and normalized RMSE (RMSE / std of test Cd).
- Scaling metrics: per architecture, fit log(test RMSE) = a − b·log(n); b is the learning-rate exponent; compare b across architectures with bootstrap CIs.
- Cost metrics: wall-clock fit time and peak memory per fit (relevant especially to GP).

8. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS PLAN
- Learning curves: mean ± std over the 5 seeds per (model, n), same-subsample pairing across models.
- Main test: linear mixed model / two-way design on log(RMSE) with factors architecture and log(n) plus interaction; the interaction term directly answers Q2 (do scaling slopes differ?). Follow-up pairwise per-n comparisons between architectures using paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank across the 5 seed pairs, with Holm correction for the 21 pairwise architecture comparisons.
- Slope comparison: per-architecture b with bootstrap (resample seeds) 95% CIs; overlap/non-overlap of CIs reported alongside the mixed-model interaction.
- Effect framing: report RMSE ratios (e.g., RMSE at n=128 vs n=5600 per model) in addition to p-values.

9. CONTROLS
- Identical splits, subsample seeds, and standardization (fit on training subset only) across all models.
- Fixed early-stopping rule and epoch cap for MLPs; identical tree counts budget for RF/GBM search space; inducing-point count fixed for sparse GP.
- Environment pinning (library versions recorded); single-thread settings documented per library for reproducibility, with seeds parallelized across the 224 CPU cores.
- No test-set access during any tuning or model selection.

10. FEASIBILITY / RESOURCE ESTIMATE (estimate only — nothing was run)
Rough per-fit wall-clock on the CPU-only environment (single fit, one core-class job; 224 cores available to parallelize seeds/configs):
| Model | n=128 | n=1024 | n=4096–5600 |
| Ridge / poly-ridge | <0.1 s | <0.1 s | <0.5 s |
| RF (300 trees) | ~1–5 s | ~10–30 s | ~1–3 min |
| GBM | ~1–5 s | ~10–30 s | ~1–3 min |
| Exact GP | seconds | ~1–5 min | n/a (capped at 2048) |
| Sparse GP (m=512) | ~seconds | ~1–5 min | ~10–40 min |
| MLP (CPU) | ~1–2 min | ~5–10 min | ~15–30 min |
Total fits: 7 models × 7 sizes × 5 seeds = 245 final fits, plus tuning ≈ 245 × 8 = 1,960 candidate fits (many trivial). Optimistic aggregate ≈ 20–60 CPU-hours; pessimistic (sparse-GP and MLP tuning dominating) ≈ 150–300 CPU-hours. With ~200 usable cores this is on the order of 1–2 wall-clock days in the pessimistic case — feasible but not trivial, hence the fallback below.
- Seed policy: DEFAULT 5 seeds per (model, n). Documented fallback: if the pessimistic estimate is confirmed (e.g., sparse-GP tuning exceeding ~1 h per config), reduce to 3 seeds AND/OR reduce the tuning budget to 4 configurations for the two neural and GP models only; the reduction is applied uniformly across architectures and reported. Any fallback decision is recorded before unblinded results are examined.

11. INTERPRETATION CAVEATS
- CFD label-noise plateau: Cd labels carry finite-mesh/numerical noise; learning curves may plateau at a noise floor set by label quality rather than model capacity. We cannot estimate this floor without mesh-level metadata; small-n-vs-large-n gaps may therefore understate true model differences. Stated as an interpretation caveat, not measured.
- GP curve mixes exact (n≤2048) and sparse (n>2048) formulations; slope discontinuities near the switch point are attributed with that caveat.
- Tuning-policy sensitivity (Section 6) bounds but does not eliminate hyperparameter-driven slope bias.
- Scaling claims are bounded by the available data range (n ≤ ~5,600); extrapolation to much larger n is out of scope.
- Deviation from the official DrivAerNet++ split (Section 3).
- CPU-only training limits neural-model scale; conclusions about "neural architectures" apply to MLPs of this class on 26-d inputs, not to large deep models.

12. PSEUDOCODE OUTLINE
```
load parametric matrix X (N≈8000 × 26) and Cd y
stratified_split(X, y, by=variant) -> train_pool, val, test      # fixed seed, once
for n in [128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 5600]:
    for s in seeds[1..5]:                                        # default 5, fallback 3
        subset = subsample(train_pool, n, seed=s)                # same subsets reused by all models
        for model in [ridge, poly_ridge, rf, gbm, gp, mlp, wide_mlp]:
            candidates = random_search(model.space, budget=8)    # identical space at every n
            best = argmin_val_rmse(fit(candidates, subset, val)) # standardize on subset only
            test_rmse[model, n, s] = evaluate(best, test)
            log fit_time, peak_memory
# frozen sensitivity curve (M4 only):
best_5600 = argmin over tuning at n=5600; evaluate best_5600 (retrained on each subset) at all n
analyze: learning curves, log-log slopes + bootstrap CIs,
         mixed model log(RMSE) ~ architecture * log(n),
         paired per-n tests (Holm-corrected), val-vs-test gaps
```

13. STATEMENT
This is a design only. No code was written against data, no dataset was downloaded, no pilot or full run was executed, and no numerical results are claimed. All figures in Section 10 are feasibility estimates, not measurements.

Assumptions (distinct from fixed task requirements): DrivAerNet++ availability with Cd labels for all variants; 26 parameters form a fixed numeric vector (categoricals one-hot); CPU-only compute is sufficient per Section 10; preprocessing limited to standardization/one-hot so architecture is the differentiator. Fixed by the task: 26-parameter DrivAerNet++ inputs, Cd target, design-only scope, the researcher decisions in items (1)–(6) of your instruction.

Exact filenames/entry points to be confirmed from your setup topics.
- **Evaluation/logging:** JaxMARL baselines typically log episode returns, win rate (for SMAC-family tasks where win/loss is defined by the environment), and steps/sec; evaluation is usually a fixed number of evaluation episodes run periodically during training. Exact metric names and cadence to be confirmed.
- **Time reporting:** JaxMARL emphasizes wall-clock speed via `jax.vmap`/`pmap` batched stepping, so "training time" is usually reported as wall-clock seconds (or steps/sec) to reach a win-rate threshold, alongside total environment steps.

## (3) High-level approach sketch (design-only)

**Question decomposition:** (a) training-time comparison — wall-clock and/or environment steps for PPO vs Q-Learning to reach a performance threshold; (b) normalized-score comparison — final/peak normalized performance.

**Proposed design skeleton:**
1. **Task set:** 3–4 SMAX maps spanning difficulty and agent count (e.g., easy `8m`-style, hard asymmetric `5m_vs_6m`-style, super-hard `mmm2`-style; final map list subject to your confirmation).

4. **Metrics:**

   - *Normalized score:* per-map normalized performance = (score − random-policy baseline) / (best-known/upper reference − random baseline); for SMAX, win rate itself is often a natural 0–1 normalized metric — I propose win rate as primary normalized score, with the normalized-return definition as sensitivity analysis.
5. **Analysis:** per-map paired comparison across seeds (mean ± std, bootstrap CI or Mann–Whitney), plus aggregate normalized score across maps.

# Final Experiment Design: JaxMARL PPO vs Q-Learning in SMAX — Training Time and Normalized Score

**Status: design only.** No experiment has been run and none may be claimed as run. This repository contains no JaxMARL code (only `task.json`, whose `track.md` states "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"); therefore every JaxMARL/SMAX-specific claim below that cannot be confirmed from the supplied context is marked **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION]** and must be revisited against the actual JaxMARL release before any execution.

---

## 1. Research question and hypotheses

**Question:** How does JaxMARL's PPO compare to Q-Learning in SMAX environments in terms of (a) training time and (b) normalized score?

**Operationalization:**
- (a) *Training time*: reported two ways — (i) fixed-budget learning curves with time-to-threshold read off at multiple win-rate thresholds, and (ii) environment steps-to-threshold as a sample-efficiency measure.
- (b) *Normalized score*: primary metric is **SMAX win rate** (native 0–1 metric, well-defined per map per the SMAC-style task definition) **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION: that SMAX exposes a binary win/loss outcome identical in semantics to SMAC; to be confirmed from the environment code]**.

**Working hypotheses (to be tested, not asserted):**
- H1: On wall-clock time to threshold, PPO may be faster because JaxMARL's vectorized (`vmap`/`pmap`) stepping favors large-batch on-policy rollouts — but this is hardware-conditional (Section 5).
- H2: On environment steps-to-threshold (sample efficiency), the value-based Q-Learning variant may be competitive or better on easier maps, with the gap widening or reversing on harder/asymmetric maps.
- H3: On final normalized score (win rate), relative ranking is map-dependent; hard asymmetric and super-hard maps are where prior SMAC literature reports the largest algorithm separations.

---

## 2. Factors, levels, and runs

| Factor | Levels | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Algorithm | PPO (JaxMARL as-shipped), Q-Learning variant (JaxMARL as-shipped, QMIX-style value-based **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION on exact variant name]**) | Both from the same JaxMARL release; identical env and eval harness |
| Map | 3–4 SMAX maps spanning difficulty tiers: easy, hard asymmetric, super-hard | See Section 3; list is an assumption |
| Seed | ≥3 identical seeds per (map × algorithm) cell, extended to 5 if budget allows | Same seed produces the same env instance/reset stream in both algorithms |
| Tuning | As-shipped defaults (primary); small budget-capped sensitivity check (secondary) | Section 6 |

**Total runs (illustrative budget):** 2 algorithms × 4 maps × 3 seeds = **24 training runs** for the primary comparison, plus a sensitivity check of ~8–12 short additional runs (Section 6). Each run is independent; no cross-arm coupling beyond shared seeds and configs.

---

## 3. Map selection **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION — revisit against actual JaxMARL release]**

Candidate maps spanning the standard SMAC difficulty categories, chosen to vary agent count and asymmetry:
1. **Easy / symmetric, moderate agent count** (e.g., an `8m`-class or `2s3z`-class map) — expected: both algorithms plateau near high win rate; comparison focuses on time-to-threshold.
2. **Hard asymmetric** (e.g., a `5m_vs_6m`-class map) — expected: larger separation; sensitive to exploration and credit assignment.
3. **Super-hard** (e.g., an `mmm2`-class or `6h_vs_8z`-class map) — expected: low absolute win rates; tests whether either algorithm reaches thresholds at all (censoring will matter).
4. (Optional 4th) **Small-n micro map** (e.g., a `2s_vs_1sc`-class map) to probe scalability from the other direction.

Selection criteria (fixed a priori): (i) spans ≥3 difficulty tiers, (ii) agent count varies by ≥2× across the set, (iii) all maps are present in the same JaxMARL release so identical harness code applies, (iv) at least one map where published/known performance for both algorithm families is non-saturated, so thresholds are reachable by at least one arm. Exact map availability in SMAX is not confirmable here and is explicitly flagged.

---

## 4. Training protocol (fixed for all runs)

All settings below are **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION]** where they depend on JaxMARL defaults; they are stated as fixed design constants so the design is falsifiable.

- **Training step budget:** a fixed cap of **T = 10M environment steps per run** (illustrative; see Section 8 feasibility note). No early stopping based on performance — the budget cap is the only stopping rule for the primary curves, so learning curves remain comparable.
- **Wall-clock cap:** additionally, a **wall-clock cap of 24 hours per run** on the designated hardware; runs hitting the wall-clock cap are censored identically to runs hitting the step cap (Section 5).
- **Episode/rollout configuration:** episode horizon and rollout/batch parameters taken from JaxMARL's as-shipped defaults per algorithm; they are recorded verbatim in the design's config manifest and are *not* equalized across algorithms (PPO's rollout length vs Q-Learning's replay/target cadence are intrinsic to each method — see Section 6 fairness statement).
- **Evaluation protocol (identical for both algorithms):**
  - Evaluation episodes: a fixed number (e.g., **32 eval episodes**) run at fixed intervals in environment steps (e.g., every 100k steps) using **greedy/deterministic action selection** with exploration off.
  - Evaluation uses fresh environment instances (held-out from training dynamics but not a separate map — SMAX provides no official eval split **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION]**).
  - Win rate at an eval point = fraction of eval episodes ending in a win. Primary normalized score = win rate at the final eval point; secondary = mean of the last K eval points (e.g., K = 5) to reduce endpoint noise; peak win rate reported for context only (peak is optimistic-biased).
  - All logging (metric names, eval cadence) recorded from the actual harness at execution time; any deviation from assumed conventions is documented as a deviation note.

---

## 5. Training-time and normalized-score metrics (per researcher-fixed requirements)

**Normalized score (primary):** per-map win rate ∈ [0, 1], as defined in Section 4. Aggregate across maps: mean of per-map win rates (macro-average), so easy maps do not dominate.

**Sensitivity analysis (clearly labeled, not primary):** return-based normalized score = (score − baseline_random) / (reference_best − baseline_random). This is computed **only if** reference baselines (random-policy score and a best-known/oracle-style reference) are available for every chosen map from published or reproducible sources. **If references are unavailable for any map, that map is excluded from the sensitivity analysis only — no reference points are fabricated**, and the primary win-rate analysis stands alone.

**Training-time reporting (both modes, per fixed requirements):**
1. **Fixed-budget learning curves:** normalized score (win rate) vs environment steps, plotted per run with cross-seed mean ± standard deviation per (map × algorithm).
2. **Time-to-threshold at multiple thresholds:** thresholds at **50% and 80% win rate** (and additionally 90% where at least one arm saturates). Read off as the first eval point at which the run's win rate meets/exceeds the threshold; interpolation between eval points is not used (threshold arrival is defined at eval-point resolution, and eval-point spacing is small relative to the budget).
3. **Steps-to-threshold:** same threshold-arrival events counted in environment steps — the sample-efficiency measure.
4. **Censoring:** a run that never reaches a threshold within the step cap or wall-clock cap is recorded as **censored** at the cap, not as "infinite" and not as a metric failure. Analysis uses survival-style treatment: report the censoring fraction per (map × algorithm × threshold), compute median time-to-threshold with a Kaplan–Meier-style estimator or inverted-censoring bootstrap, and use a censored-data comparison (e.g., log-rank test on threshold-arrival "survival" curves) as the inferential tool where censoring is present. If both arms saturate a threshold on a map with no censoring, a plain per-seed paired comparison is used instead.
5. **Wall-clock conditionality:** all wall-clock conclusions are stated as **conditional on a single fixed, identical hardware configuration** (same accelerator type, count, and JAX backend for every run). The design notes explicitly that JaxMARL's vectorized batched stepping can shift wall-clock results relative to sample efficiency: PPO-style large-batch rollouts may exploit `vmap`/`pmap` parallelism better and appear faster in wall-clock even if steps-to-threshold is worse. Wall-clock and steps-to-threshold are therefore reported as **separate, non-interchangeable** results.

---

## 6. Hyperparameter fairness policy (per fixed requirements)

- **Primary comparison: as-released.** Each algorithm uses JaxMARL's own default configuration, unmodified except for seeds and logging. This answers "how do the released implementations compare out of the box," which is the question as posed.
- **Sensitivity check (secondary, budget-capped, documented, not an exhaustive search):** for each algorithm and one representative hard map, vary a small number of the most impactful hyperparameters (for PPO: learning rate and rollout length; for the Q-Learning variant: learning rate and target-update/epsilon cadence) over ~3 values each in a one-factor-at-a-time sweep, capped at **~4 extra runs per algorithm**. The sensitivity check exists solely to qualify conclusions: if the ranking flips under modest retuning of either arm, the as-released result is labeled fragile.
- **Explicit fairness statement in the deliverable:** PPO and Q-Learning have intrinsically different compute/step profiles (on-policy rollout batches vs replay-based updates); equalizing steps does not equalize gradient updates or wall-clock, and vice versa. The design therefore never claims a single "fair" budget and instead reports both step-normalized and wall-clock-normalized views with the hardware conditionality of Section 5.

---

## 7. Analysis plan

- **Per-map paired comparisons across seeds:** for each map, paired by seed (same seed runs both algorithms on the same map instance). Report mean ± std and per-seed differences for (i) final win rate, (ii) time-to-threshold at each threshold. Inference: with 3–5 seeds, nonparametric paired tests (sign test / exact Wilcoxon where n ≥ 5) plus bootstrap CIs over seeds; no parametric normality assumptions.
- **Censored thresholds:** log-rank test on threshold-arrival curves (Section 5.4) when censoring is present; censoring fractions reported alongside every time-to-threshold number.
- **Aggregate normalized score:** macro-averaged final win rate across maps per algorithm, with per-map values always shown (aggregation alone can mask sign reversals). A rank-based aggregate (mean per-map rank) is reported as a robustness check.
- **Multiplicity:** per-map tests are descriptive; the confirmatory claim is restricted to (a) the aggregate normalized score comparison and (b) time-to-threshold on the designated representative hard map. This limits false-positive risk from testing many map × threshold cells.
- **Pre-registration-style spec:** thresholds, eval cadence, budget caps, and seeds are fixed before any run and recorded in a config manifest; any deviation is logged.

---

## 8. Feasibility assessment and illustrative budget (marked assumption)

**Illustrative budget (assumption, not a measured quantity):** 24 primary runs × up to 10M env steps each, with a 24h wall-clock cap per run; ~8–12 additional sensitivity runs. On GPU-accelerated JaxMARL (its intended setting), published step-throughput figures for SMAX-class envs are orders of magnitude above CPU throughput **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION]**, making the full grid plausible within days of single-accelerator time; on CPU-only hardware the step cap would likely dominate.

**Scaling if budget shrinks:**
- Halve seeds (3 → 2): keep per-map curves; downgrade inference to descriptive only (no tests); state loss of power explicitly.
- Halve step budget (10M → 5M): threshold analysis shifts to lower thresholds (50% primary, 80% secondary); super-hard map may become fully censored — report it as such rather than dropping it silently.
- Reduce maps 4 → 3: drop the optional micro map; aggregate normalized score remains defined over the remaining set, and this change is noted in the aggregate.
- Wall-clock cap binding before step cap: report both cap-hit fractions; wall-clock and step-based results then diverge and are presented separately per Section 5.4–5.5.

---

## 9. Assumptions and limitations (explicit)

**Fixed task requirements (from researcher):** win rate as primary normalized score; return-based normalization only as labeled sensitivity analysis with no fabricated references; both fixed-budget curves with multi-threshold time-to-threshold AND steps-to-threshold, with censoring; wall-clock results conditional on fixed identical hardware; as-shipped defaults primary + capped sensitivity check; map list flagged as assumption; illustrative budget marked as assumption.

**Assumptions (stated, not verified):**
1. **[UNVERIFIED]** SMAX exposes binary win/loss per episode and a per-episode return, and its semantics match the SMAC family.
2. **[UNVERIFIED]** JaxMARL contains the assumed algorithm variants (a PPO-family method and a QMIX/DQN-family Q-Learning method) with as-shipped default configs in a single release.
3. **[UNVERIFIED]** The candidate map list (Section 3) exists in SMAX with those difficulty characteristics.
4. **[UNVERIFIED]** Evaluation harness supports greedy evaluation over a fixed number of episodes at fixed step intervals.
5. **Assumed:** hardware identical across all runs; JAX backend/version pinned; environment version pinned (SMAX difficulty can shift with unit-balance patches).
6. **Assumed:** 3–5 seeds suffice for directional conclusions; the design does not claim high statistical power for per-map null results.
7. **Assumed:** random-policy and reference baselines exist for the sensitivity analysis only where sourced; none are invented.

**Limitations:**
- Results are specific to the as-released JaxMARL implementations and defaults; they do not generalize to tuned or reimplemented baselines.
- Wall-clock findings are hardware-conditional by construction (Section 5.5) and may reverse on different accelerators.
- Threshold-arrival resolution is limited by eval cadence.
- Super-hard maps may yield heavy censoring, in which case the design reports censoring honestly rather than forcing a ranking.
- This is a design-only deliverable: no runs, no data, and no results are claimed anywhere in this document.

---

## 10. Controls summary (fixed)

| Control | Fix |
|---|---|
| Seeds | Same seed set (≥3) shared across algorithms per map |
| Maps | 3–4 maps per Section 3, identical across algorithms |
| Agent counts/units | Determined by map; identical across algorithms |
| Evaluation protocol | 32 eval episodes, greedy actions, fixed step interval, both algorithms identical |
| Budgets | 10M env steps cap + 24h wall-clock cap per run (illustrative) |
| Hardware/software | Single pinned accelerator config, pinned JAX/env versions |
| Hyperparameters | As-shipped defaults (primary); capped 1-factor sensitivity check (secondary) |
| Logging | Config manifest + deviation log; all metric names captured from the actual harness at execution time |

No experiment is claimed as executed. All map, algorithm, and harness specifics marked **[UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION]** must be confirmed against the actual JaxMARL/SMAX code before this design could be executed.

INITIAL INSPECTION REPORT + PROPOSED EXPERIMENT APPROACH (design-only; nothing was run or installed)

=====================================================================
1) WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE IN /workspace
=====================================================================
• /workspace contains exactly one file: task.json (410 bytes). It holds the question ("How does JaxMARL's PPO compare to Q-Learning in SMAX environments in terms of training time and normalized score?"), a one-line context ("Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required."), and no other documents.
• There is NO cloned JaxMARL repository, no config files, no baseline entry points, no docs anywhere on the box: a filesystem search for "*jaxmarl*" / "*smax*" returned nothing; /home/actor is empty; /usr/local/games is empty.
• Python check: `import jax` and `import jaxmarl` both raise ModuleNotFoundError; pip lists no JAX/RL packages. Network is disabled (pip download fails immediately), so the repo cannot be fetched in this sandbox.
• Hardware snapshot (exploration sandbox): CPU-only (no GPU), 224 CPU cores visible, CUDA toolkit stubs present but no JAX stack installed.

Consequence: I cannot report observed configs/entry points from source in this workspace. Everything below about JaxMARL's structure comes from documented knowledge of the public FLAIR-Oxford/JaxMARL repository, and I flag it as UNVERIFIED-in-workspace. From that knowledge, the relevant artifacts are:
  – SMAX maps under jaxmarl/environments/smax/: 5m_vs_6m, 8m, 10m_vs_11m, 2s3z, 2s5z, 3s5z, 3s5z_vs_3s6z, 6h_vs_8z, 2c64_40z, 27m_vs_30m, 25m2z_vs_25m2z, MMM2, etc.
  – PPO baseline: baselines/IPPO/main.py with per-map Hydra configs (e.g., baselines/IPPO/config/smax/ippo_smax_<map>.yaml).
  – Q-learning baseline: baselines/QMIX/ (QMIX and VDN variants) with analogous per-map Hydra configs. JaxMARL does not ship a plain (non-decomposed) multi-agent Q-Learning baseline; "Q-Learning" in the question most plausibly maps to QMIX/VDN — this is a clarification point (see §3).
  – JaxMARL paper (Fu et al., 2024, arXiv:2312.12586) documents SMAC-style normalized metrics and GPU speedups.

=====================================================================
2) PROPOSED HIGH-LEVEL EXPERIMENT APPROACH
=====================================================================
Design: fixed-computation-budget comparison of JaxMARL's IPPO ("PPO") vs QMIX ("Q-Learning") on SMAX, measuring (a) wall-clock training time and (b) normalized score.

Environments (SMAX maps, spanning scale/complexity, ~6 maps):
  – Small: 5m_vs_6m, 2s3z
  – Medium: 3s5z, 6h_vs_8z (hard asymmetric case)
  – Large: 10m_vs_11m, 2c64_40z (or 27m_vs_30m)
Rationale: JAX speedups are claimed to grow with map size, so the training-time comparison must span map scale; including one hard asymmetric map tests robustness rather than just speed. Optional sensitivity: swap in 3s5z_vs_3s6z.

Seeds: 5 seeds minimum per (algorithm × map) cell (60 runs for 2×6; 10 seeds preferred if budget allows). Report mean ± 95% bootstrap CI and IQM aggregate across maps (rliable-style).

"Training time" definition (choose one primary, one secondary):
  – Primary: wall-clock seconds to reach a FIXED environment-timestep budget (e.g., 1M steps on small maps, 5M on large), identical for both algorithms, measured on the same single GPU after a warm-up run that absorbs JIT compilation (JAX compile time is excluded but reported separately).
  – Secondary: time-normalized score = area under the normalized-score-vs-wall-clock-hours curve (sampled at fixed eval checkpoints), which captures both speed and learning speed, since a faster JAX implementation may also simply reach good scores sooner.

Normalized score definition: SMAX exposes a win-rate/return-based evaluation. Proposed anchor-based normalization per map:
  normalized score = (score − random_policy_score) / (heuristic_baseline_score − random_policy_score), clipped to [0,1],
 where score = win rate (or mean episode return mapped via the same anchor formula), the random-policy score comes from an untrained policy evaluated in the same harness, and the "expert" anchor is SMAX's built-in heuristic agent (e.g., "independent" attack-closest heuristic) win rate. If a heuristic anchor is unavailable for a map, fall back to min–max normalization over the observed range across both algorithms, and say so explicitly in results.

Fairness controls:
  – Use each algorithm's per-map default hyperparameters from JaxMARL's shipped configs (both are already tuned for SMAX in the repo) rather than retuning, to avoid a tuning-budget confound; document the exact commit/hash.
  – Identical evaluation protocol (eval frequency, number of eval episodes, deterministic vs stochastic env steps), same environment versions, same hardware, runs run sequentially on one device (concurrent runs would distort wall-clock).

Deliverable: a design document (this turn = plan only; full design after approval), with a run matrix (algo × map × seed), budget table, and pre-registered analysis plan.

=====================================================================
3) CONSEQUENTIAL ASSUMPTIONS AND UNCERTAINTIES TO FLAG
=====================================================================
Assumptions (my proposed defaults, not task-fixed):
  A1. "Q-Learning" = QMIX (JaxMARL's value-decomposition Q-learning baseline; VDN available as an ablation). If the question intends IQL or another variant, the design changes materially.
  A2. Fixed-timestep budget, not fixed wall-clock, is the fairest primary time metric (fixed wall-clock would confound sample-efficiency differences).
  A3. Heuristic baseline is a valid normalization anchor for all maps.
  A4. Defaults from JaxMARL configs are acceptable hyperparameters (no retuning).
  A5. 5 seeds/cell is enough for CI width that supports a qualitative conclusion; more if budget allows.

Uncertainties / open items (stating the fixed constraints where known):
  U1. Compute/runtime budget is UNSTATED. The cell count implies roughly 60 runs; on small maps this is likely tractable (<1 day GPU), on 2c64_40z each run can be hours. Need: how many GPU-hours are available, and whether large maps can be dropped if over budget.
  U2. Hardware constraints are UNSTATED for the execution phase. This exploration sandbox has no GPU and no network, so if execution is expected elsewhere I need to know: GPU model/count, whether runs may share a GPU (distorts wall-clock), and whether JAX must target CPU (which would invert JaxMARL's headline speedup claims and make wall-clock comparisons uninformative).
  U3. Which JaxMARL version/commit to pin, and which SMAX config flags to use (e.g., the paper's reported settings like add_move_state/add_local_obs defaults) — I could not verify any of this from source in the workspace.
  U4. Whether "training time" should include or exclude JIT compile time, and whether time-normalized AUC is wanted as a co-primary or secondary metric.
  U5. Exact definition of the score to normalize (win rate vs. episode return) and the evaluation cadence/episode count are not specified by the task.
  U6. Seed count / statistical rigor bar (5 vs 10 seeds) depends on budget; the rliable aggregate also needs enough maps to be meaningful.
  U7. Whether hyperparameter retuning per algorithm is permitted or defaults-only is required (defaults-only favors neither algorithm but may understate one).

Recommended clarifications from you (within your remaining topic budget): (a) confirm Q-Learning = QMIX, (b) GPU-hours budget and hardware, (c) fixed-timestep budget per map, (d) score metric for normalization (win rate vs return). I have not run anything and will not produce the full design document until you approve this approach.
